skills.name: performance-code-review
skills.description: Reviews a pull request or diff before merge specifically for performance and scalability risks — algorithmic complexity, N+1 and unindexed queries, unbounded loops/payloads, missing pagination, chatty network calls, blocking I/O, memory growth, caching mistakes and frontend bundle/render cost — and states which concerns need a benchmark before merge. Use when asked for a "performance review", "will this scale", "check this for N+1", "is this query OK", "review for latency", or a PR touches hot paths, queries or large data sets.
skills.body:
# Performance-Focused Code Review

Reviews a change *before* it ships for code patterns that become slow, expensive or unstable at production scale. It reasons from expected data sizes and traffic, not micro-optimisations, and separates findings that are clear from reading the code (an N+1 loop) from those that need measurement (whether a cache helps). For a regression that already happened in production, use `performance-regression-investigation` instead.

## When to use / when not to use

Use when:
- A PR touches request hot paths, database queries/ORM code, batch jobs, data pipelines, caching, or rendering of large lists.
- A feature will meet much larger data than test fixtures (big tenants, long histories).
- Reviewers ask "will this scale?"

Do not use when:
- Something is already slow in production → `performance-regression-investigation`.
- Estimating capacity for a new system → `capacity-scaling-estimate`.
- General review → `pull-request-review` (it may escalate here).

## What to ask for first

1. **Diff** and the code path's role (API endpoint, background job, UI screen).
2. **Scale**: typical and worst-case data sizes (rows per tenant, items per list, payload sizes), request rate, latency budget/SLO.
3. **Data layer**: database and ORM, existing indexes/schema, cache layer, query plans if available.
4. **Measurement options**: can I run benchmarks, `EXPLAIN`/`EXPLAIN ANALYZE` on a non-production copy, a profiler, or bundle analyzer?

If scale is unknown, assume 100× the test fixture size and say so.

## Steps

1. **Identify hot paths** in the diff and their frequency (per request, per item, per page load, nightly).
2. **Complexity.** Nested loops over growing collections, repeated linear searches (use maps/sets), sorting inside loops, quadratic string building, regexes with catastrophic backtracking on user input.
3. **Database.** N+1 queries from lazy loading or per-item queries; `SELECT *` on wide tables; filters/sorts without supporting indexes; missing pagination or `LIMIT`; `OFFSET` pagination on large tables; long transactions and lock scope; counting large tables on every request; migrations that rewrite big tables (link `safe-database-migration-plan`).
4. **Network & I/O.** Sequential calls that could be batched or parallel; calls inside loops; missing timeouts; synchronous/blocking I/O on event loops or request threads; large payloads without compression or streaming.
5. **Memory.** Loading full result sets or files into memory; unbounded caches/maps; listeners or subscriptions not cleaned up; large objects captured in closures.
6. **Caching.** Correct keys (including tenant/user/locale), invalidation on writes, TTLs, stampede protection, caching of errors, cache that hides personal data across users.
7. **Concurrency.** Thread-pool or connection-pool exhaustion, unbounded fan-out, missing backpressure on queues, retries without jitter.
8. **Frontend (if relevant).** Bundle size from new imports, re-renders from unstable props/inline objects, long lists without virtualisation, layout thrashing, unoptimised images.
9. **Estimate impact** with simple arithmetic (e.g. "200 items × 1 query × 5 ms ≈ 1 s per request") and label it an estimate.
10. **Decide what needs measurement** and propose the specific benchmark, query plan, or load test.

**Severity**: **[blocker]** will clearly breach SLO or exhaust resources at known scale · **[major]** likely problem at expected growth · **[minor]** inefficiency with small impact · **[measure]** cannot judge without data.

## Output format

```
## Scope & assumptions
Path: <endpoint/job>  Scale assumed: <rows, rps, payload>  Budget: <p95 target>

## Findings
**[blocker]** `orders/service.py:88` — N+1: one query per order line inside loop.
Estimate: 500 lines × ~3 ms ≈ 1.5 s added (estimate). Fix: prefetch/join or batch `IN` query.

## Needs measurement
| Concern | How to measure | Pass criterion |

## Measurements run (if any)
<command / EXPLAIN output summary, exit code>

## Verdict: OK | fix blockers | benchmark before merge
```

## Quality checks

- [ ] Findings tied to concrete code locations and realistic data sizes, not generic advice.
- [ ] Estimates shown with arithmetic and labelled as estimates; measured numbers quoted from actual output.
- [ ] Database findings consider indexes and query plans, not only query count.
- [ ] No premature micro-optimisation flagged as blocking.
- [ ] Caching suggestions include invalidation and key-scoping (no cross-user data leaks).
- [ ] Each [measure] item has a specific method and pass criterion.

## Limits

- Never present an estimate as a measurement or claim a benchmark result without running it; report commands and exit codes for anything executed.
- Run `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` or load tests only against non-production environments the user approves.
- Performance depends on data distribution and infrastructure; conclusions from reading code are hypotheses until measured.

skills.body:
# 성능 중심 코드 리뷰

변경이 배포되기 *전에* 운영 규모에서 느려지거나 비싸지거나 불안정해질 코드 패턴을 찾습니다. 마이크로 최적화가 아니라 예상 데이터 크기와 트래픽에서 출발하며, 코드만 읽어도 명확한 문제(N+1 루프)와 측정이 필요한 문제(캐시가 도움이 되는지)를 구분합니다. 이미 운영에서 발생한 성능 저하는 `performance-regression-investigation-ko`를 사용합니다.

## 사용 시점 / 사용하지 않는 경우

사용하는 경우:
- PR이 요청 핫 패스, DB 쿼리/ORM 코드, 배치, 데이터 파이프라인, 캐시, 대량 목록 렌더링을 건드릴 때
- 기능이 테스트 fixture보다 훨씬 큰 데이터(대형 고객사, 긴 이력)를 만나게 될 때
- 리뷰어가 "이거 스케일 돼?"라고 물을 때

사용하지 않는 경우:
- 이미 운영에서 느려짐 → `performance-regression-investigation-ko`
- 신규 시스템 용량 추정 → `capacity-scaling-estimate-ko`
- 일반 리뷰 → `pull-request-review-ko`(필요 시 이 스킬로 넘어옵니다)

## 먼저 확인할 사항

1. **diff**와 해당 코드 경로의 역할(API 엔드포인트, 백그라운드 잡, UI 화면)
2. **규모**: 일반·최악의 데이터 크기(테넌트당 행 수, 목록당 항목 수, 페이로드 크기), 요청률, 지연 예산/SLO
3. **데이터 계층**: DB와 ORM, 기존 인덱스·스키마, 캐시 계층, 가능하면 실행 계획
4. **측정 수단**: 벤치마크, 비운영 복제본에서의 `EXPLAIN`/`EXPLAIN ANALYZE`, 프로파일러, 번들 분석기 실행 가능 여부

규모를 모르면 "테스트 fixture의 100배"로 가정하고 명시합니다.

## 리뷰 절차

1. **핫 패스를 식별합니다.** diff 안의 핫 패스와 실행 빈도(요청당, 항목당, 페이지 로드당, 야간)
2. **복잡도.** 커지는 컬렉션에 대한 중첩 루프, 반복 선형 탐색(맵/셋 사용), 루프 내 정렬, 이차 문자열 결합, 사용자 입력에 대한 catastrophic backtracking 정규식
3. **데이터베이스.** lazy loading이나 항목별 쿼리로 인한 N+1, 넓은 테이블의 `SELECT *`, 인덱스 없는 필터·정렬, 페이지네이션/`LIMIT` 누락, 대형 테이블의 `OFFSET` 페이지네이션, 긴 트랜잭션과 잠금 범위, 매 요청 대형 테이블 count, 큰 테이블을 재작성하는 마이그레이션(`safe-database-migration-plan-ko` 연계)
4. **네트워크·I/O.** 배치나 병렬화할 수 있는 순차 호출, 루프 안 호출, 타임아웃 누락, 이벤트 루프·요청 스레드의 블로킹 I/O, 압축·스트리밍 없는 대형 페이로드
5. **메모리.** 전체 결과 집합·파일을 메모리에 적재, 무제한 캐시·맵, 정리되지 않는 리스너·구독, 클로저에 잡힌 큰 객체
6. **캐시.** 올바른 키(테넌트/사용자/로케일 포함), 쓰기 시 무효화, TTL, 스탬피드 방지, 오류 캐싱, 사용자 간 개인정보가 섞이는 캐시
7. **동시성.** 스레드 풀·커넥션 풀 고갈, 무제한 fan-out, 큐 backpressure 누락, jitter 없는 재시도
8. **프론트엔드(해당 시).** 새 import로 인한 번들 크기, 불안정한 props·인라인 객체로 인한 재렌더, 가상화 없는 긴 목록, 레이아웃 스래싱, 최적화되지 않은 이미지
9. **영향을 추정합니다.** 간단한 계산으로 보여주고 추정임을 표시합니다(예: "200개 × 쿼리 1회 × 5ms ≈ 요청당 1초").
10. **측정이 필요한 항목**을 정하고 구체적 벤치마크·실행 계획·부하 테스트를 제안합니다.

**심각도**: **[필수]** 알려진 규모에서 SLO 위반·자원 고갈이 명확 · **[중요]** 예상 성장 시 문제 가능성 높음 · **[권장]** 영향이 작은 비효율 · **[측정 필요]** 데이터 없이는 판단 불가

## 결과물 형식

```
## 범위와 가정
경로: <엔드포인트/잡>  가정 규모: <행 수, rps, 페이로드>  예산: <p95 목표>

## 발견 사항
**[필수]** `orders/service.py:88` — N+1: 루프 안에서 주문 라인마다 쿼리 1회
추정: 500라인 × 약 3ms ≈ 1.5초 증가(추정). 수정안: prefetch/join 또는 `IN` 배치 쿼리

## 측정 필요
| 우려 사항 | 측정 방법 | 통과 기준 |

## 실행한 측정 (있다면)
<명령 / EXPLAIN 결과 요약, exit code>

## 판정: 문제 없음 | 필수 항목 수정 | 머지 전 벤치마크
```

## 자체 점검

- [ ] 발견 사항이 일반론이 아니라 구체적 코드 위치와 현실적 데이터 크기에 연결되는가
- [ ] 추정치는 계산과 함께 "추정"으로 표시하고, 측정값은 실제 출력에서 인용했는가
- [ ] DB 발견 사항이 쿼리 수뿐 아니라 인덱스와 실행 계획을 고려하는가
- [ ] 섣부른 마이크로 최적화를 [필수]로 올리지 않았는가
- [ ] 캐시 제안에 무효화와 키 범위(사용자 간 데이터 누출 방지)가 포함되는가
- [ ] [측정 필요] 항목마다 구체적 방법과 통과 기준이 있는가

## 한계

- 추정치를 측정값처럼 제시하거나 실행하지 않은 벤치마크 결과를 주장하지 않습니다. 실행한 것은 명령과 exit code로 보고합니다.
- `EXPLAIN ANALYZE`나 부하 테스트는 사용자가 승인한 비운영 환경에서만 실행합니다.
- 성능은 데이터 분포와 인프라에 좌우되므로 코드 리딩에서 나온 결론은 측정 전까지 가설입니다.

skills.body:
# Performance-Focused Code Review

Change के ship होने से *पहले* उन code patterns को review करता है जो production scale पर धीमे, महँगे या अस्थिर हो जाते हैं। यह micro-optimisations से नहीं, अपेक्षित data sizes और traffic से सोचता है, और उन findings को जो code पढ़कर ही साफ़ हैं (N+1 loop) उनसे अलग रखता है जिन्हें measurement चाहिए (cache से फ़ायदा होगा या नहीं)। Production में पहले से हुई regression के लिए `performance-regression-investigation-hi` इस्तेमाल करें।

## कब उपयोग करें / कब नहीं

उपयोग करें जब:
- PR request hot paths, database queries/ORM code, batch jobs, data pipelines, caching, या बड़ी lists की rendering छूता हो।
- Feature को test fixtures से बहुत बड़ा data मिलेगा (बड़े tenants, लंबी history, sale-day traffic)।
- Reviewers पूछें "क्या ये scale करेगा?"

उपयोग न करें जब:
- Production में पहले से धीमा है → `performance-regression-investigation-hi`
- नए system की capacity estimate → `capacity-scaling-estimate-hi`
- General review → `pull-request-review-hi` (ज़रूरत पर यहाँ escalate करेगा)

## पहले क्या पूछें

1. **Diff** और code path का role (API endpoint, background job, UI screen)।
2. **Scale**: सामान्य और worst-case data sizes (per tenant rows, per list items, payload sizes), request rate, latency budget/SLO।
3. **Data layer**: database और ORM, मौजूदा indexes/schema, cache layer, उपलब्ध हों तो query plans।
4. **Measurement options**: क्या benchmarks, non-production copy पर `EXPLAIN`/`EXPLAIN ANALYZE`, profiler या bundle analyzer चला सकते हैं?

Scale पता न हो तो test fixture size का 100× मानें और यह लिखें।

## चरण

1. **Hot paths पहचानें** — diff में कौन-से हैं और कितनी बार चलते हैं (per request, per item, per page load, nightly)।
2. **Complexity।** बढ़ती collections पर nested loops, बार-बार linear search (maps/sets इस्तेमाल करें), loops के अंदर sorting, quadratic string building, user input पर catastrophic backtracking वाले regex।
3. **Database।** Lazy loading या per-item queries से N+1; चौड़ी tables पर `SELECT *`; बिना supporting index के filters/sorts; pagination या `LIMIT` गायब; बड़ी tables पर `OFFSET` pagination; लंबे transactions और lock scope; हर request पर बड़ी table का count; बड़ी tables rewrite करने वाले migrations (`safe-database-migration-plan-hi` से link करें)।
4. **Network & I/O।** Sequential calls जो batch या parallel हो सकते हैं; loops के अंदर calls; missing timeouts; event loop या request threads पर synchronous/blocking I/O; बिना compression या streaming के बड़े payloads।
5. **Memory।** पूरे result sets या files memory में load करना; unbounded caches/maps; साफ़ न होने वाले listeners/subscriptions; closures में पकड़े गए बड़े objects।
6. **Caching।** सही keys (tenant/user/locale सहित), writes पर invalidation, TTLs, stampede protection, errors की caching, ऐसा cache जो users के बीच personal data मिला दे।
7. **Concurrency।** Thread-pool या connection-pool exhaustion, unbounded fan-out, queues पर backpressure न होना, बिना jitter के retries।
8. **Frontend (अगर लागू)।** नए imports से bundle size, unstable props/inline objects से re-renders, बिना virtualisation की लंबी lists, layout thrashing, unoptimised images — कम-end Android devices और धीमे networks को ध्यान में रखें।
9. **Impact estimate करें** सरल गणित से (जैसे "200 items × 1 query × 5 ms ≈ हर request पर 1 s") और इसे estimate लिखें।
10. **Measurement वाली चीज़ें तय करें** और specific benchmark, query plan या load test प्रस्तावित करें।

**Severity**: **[blocker]** known scale पर SLO साफ़ तौर पर टूटेगा या resources ख़त्म होंगे · **[major]** अपेक्षित growth पर समस्या की संभावना · **[minor]** कम impact वाली inefficiency · **[measure]** data के बिना फ़ैसला संभव नहीं।

## Output format

```
## Scope और assumptions
Path: <endpoint/job>  Assumed scale: <rows, rps, payload>  Budget: <p95 target>

## Findings
**[blocker]** `orders/service.py:88` — N+1: loop के अंदर हर order line पर एक query।
Estimate: 500 lines × ~3 ms ≈ 1.5 s अतिरिक्त (estimate)। Fix: prefetch/join या batch `IN` query।

## Measurement चाहिए
| Concern | कैसे measure करें | Pass criterion |

## चलाए गए measurements (यदि कोई)
<command / EXPLAIN output summary, exit code>

## Verdict: OK | blockers fix करें | merge से पहले benchmark
```

## Quality checks

- [ ] Findings ठोस code locations और realistic data sizes से जुड़े हैं, generic सलाह नहीं।
- [ ] Estimates गणित के साथ और "estimate" label के साथ; measured numbers असली output से।
- [ ] Database findings में सिर्फ़ query count नहीं, indexes और query plans भी देखे गए।
- [ ] Premature micro-optimisation को blocking नहीं बनाया।
- [ ] Caching suggestions में invalidation और key-scoping (cross-user data leak नहीं) शामिल।
- [ ] हर [measure] item का specific तरीका और pass criterion है।

## सीमाएँ

- Estimate को कभी measurement की तरह न दिखाएँ, और बिना चलाए benchmark result का दावा न करें; जो चलाया उसका command और exit code बताएँ।
- `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` या load tests सिर्फ़ user द्वारा approved non-production environments पर।
- Performance data distribution और infrastructure पर निर्भर है; code पढ़कर निकले निष्कर्ष measurement तक hypotheses हैं।

skills.name: pull-request-description-writer
skills.description: Writes a clear pull request title and description from a diff, commits and ticket — what changed and why, how it was tested (with real evidence), risk and rollout/rollback notes, and where reviewers should focus — following the repo's PR template if one exists. Use when an engineer says "write the PR description", "draft a PR summary", "fill in the PR template", "describe these changes for reviewers", or "make this PR easy to review".
skills.body:
# Pull Request Description Writer

Produces a PR title and body that let a reviewer understand the change in under two minutes and review it in the right order. It explains intent before mechanics, states honestly how the change was verified, highlights risk and the parts that deserve the closest attention, and links the ticket. It never claims testing that did not happen.

## When to use / when not to use

Use when:
- A branch is ready and needs a PR title/body, or an existing description is thin.
- The repo has a PR template that needs filling in from the actual changes.
- A large PR needs a reviewer guide (suggested reading order).

Do not use when:
- You need someone to review the code → `pull-request-review`.
- Writing user-facing release notes for a whole version → use the release process (`release-readiness-smoke-test` covers release notes as an item).
- Writing a design document → `technical-design-doc-rfc`.

## What to ask for first

1. **The change**: diff or branch vs base, commit messages.
2. **Why**: ticket/issue link, problem statement, or one sentence from the author.
3. **Template & conventions**: `.github/pull_request_template.md` or team format; title convention (e.g. Conventional Commits `feat(scope): …`, ticket prefix).
4. **Verification done**: tests run and results, manual testing steps, screenshots/recordings for UI.
5. **Rollout**: feature flag, migration, config changes, deploy order, rollback.
6. **Audience**: reviewers' familiarity with the area.

## Steps

1. **Read the diff** and group changes by purpose (feature logic, refactor, tests, config, migration, docs). Separate behavior changes from pure refactors — reviewers read them differently.
2. **Write the title**: imperative, specific, ≤72 characters, following the repo convention. Example: `feat(billing): prorate refunds for mid-cycle cancellations`.
3. **Summary**: 2–4 sentences — the problem, the approach, the user-visible effect.
4. **Changes**: bullet list grouped by area; name important files or modules; mention anything deleted or renamed.
5. **Why this approach**: alternatives considered in one or two lines if the choice is non-obvious.
6. **Testing**: list what was actually done — automated tests added, commands run with results, manual steps. Anything not verified is listed as such.
7. **Risk & rollout**: risk level, migrations (backward compatible?), flags and default state, config/secrets needed, rollback steps, monitoring to watch.
8. **Reviewer guide**: suggested reading order for big PRs, the 1–3 places that most need scrutiny, explicit out-of-scope items.
9. **Screenshots** for UI changes (before/after placeholders if the author must add them).
10. **Links**: ticket, design doc, related PRs, follow-up tickets.
11. **Fit the template**: if a template exists, use its headings in order and remove irrelevant sections rather than leaving them empty.

## Output format

```
Title: <type(scope): imperative summary>

## Summary
## Changes
- ...
## Why this approach (optional)
## Testing
- [x] Unit tests added: `path/...`  — `<command>` → exit 0 (<N> passed)
- [ ] Manual check on staging — NOT DONE
## Risk & rollout
Risk: low/medium/high — <why>   Flag: <name, default off>   Migration: <yes/no, backward compatible?>
Rollback: <steps>
## Reviewer guide
Start with `...`, then `...`. Please look closely at <...>. Out of scope: <...>
## Screenshots (UI only)
## Links
Closes <ISSUE-123>
```

## Quality checks

- [ ] A reviewer can explain what and why after reading the summary alone.
- [ ] Testing section reflects only what was actually run, with commands/results; gaps are explicit.
- [ ] Risk, migration, flag and rollback information present whenever relevant.
- [ ] Behavior changes are distinguished from refactors.
- [ ] Follows repo template and title convention; no empty boilerplate sections.
- [ ] No secrets, internal hostnames or customer data in the description; screenshots use example data.

## Limits

- Never write "all tests pass" or tick a testing checkbox unless the author supplied the result or you ran it and saw exit code 0.
- Do not invent ticket numbers, metrics or reviewer names; use placeholders like `[ISSUE-?]`.
- Describe the diff that exists; if the diff and the stated intent disagree, point it out rather than papering over it.

- [ ] Testing section reflects only what was actually run, with commands/results; gaps are explicit.
- [ ] Risk, migration, flag and rollback information present whenever relevant.
- [ ] Behavior changes are distinguished from refactors.
- [ ] Follows repo template and title convention; no empty boilerplate sections.
- [ ] No secrets, internal hostnames or customer data in the description; screenshots use example data.

## Limits

- Never write "all tests pass" or tick a testing checkbox unless the author supplied the result or you ran it and saw exit code 0.
- Do not invent ticket numbers, metrics or reviewer names; use placeholders like `[ISSUE-?]`.
- Describe the diff that exists; if the diff and the stated intent disagree, point it out rather than papering over it.

skills.body:
# PR 설명 작성

리뷰어가 2분 안에 변경을 이해하고 올바른 순서로 리뷰할 수 있도록 PR 제목과 본문을 작성합니다. 구현 방식보다 의도를 먼저 설명하고, 어떻게 검증했는지 정직하게 밝히며, 위험과 가장 꼼꼼히 봐야 할 부분을 강조하고 티켓을 연결합니다. 하지 않은 테스트를 했다고 쓰지 않습니다.

## 사용 시점 / 사용하지 않는 경우

사용하는 경우:
- 브랜치가 준비되어 PR 제목·본문이 필요하거나 기존 설명이 부실할 때
- 저장소 PR 템플릿을 실제 변경 내용으로 채워야 할 때
- 큰 PR에 리뷰 가이드(추천 읽기 순서)가 필요할 때

사용하지 않는 경우:
- 코드 리뷰 자체 → `pull-request-review-ko`
- 버전 전체의 사용자용 릴리스 노트 → 릴리스 절차(`release-readiness-smoke-test-ko`에서 항목으로 다룸)
- 설계 문서 → `technical-design-doc-rfc-ko`

## 먼저 확인할 사항

1. **변경 내용**: base 대비 diff 또는 브랜치, 커밋 메시지
2. **목적**: 티켓/이슈 링크, 문제 정의, 또는 작성자의 한 문장
3. **템플릿과 컨벤션**: `.github/pull_request_template.md` 또는 팀 형식, 제목 규칙(Conventional Commits `feat(scope): …`, 티켓 접두어 등), 제목·본문 언어(한국어/영어)
4. **수행한 검증**: 실행한 테스트와 결과, 수동 테스트 절차, UI 스크린샷·녹화
5. **배포**: 피처 플래그, 마이그레이션, 설정 변경, 배포 순서, 롤백
6. **독자**: 리뷰어의 해당 영역 숙련도

## 작성 절차

1. **diff를 읽고** 목적별로 묶습니다(기능 로직, 리팩터링, 테스트, 설정, 마이그레이션, 문서). 동작 변경과 순수 리팩터링을 분리합니다 — 리뷰어가 읽는 방식이 다릅니다.
2. **제목**: 구체적이고 72자 이내, 저장소 규칙을 따릅니다. 예: `feat(billing): 월 중도 해지 시 환불 일할 계산`
3. **요약**: 2~4문장 — 문제, 접근 방식, 사용자에게 보이는 효과
4. **변경 사항**: 영역별 bullet, 중요한 파일·모듈 명시, 삭제·이름 변경도 언급
5. **이 방식을 택한 이유**: 선택이 자명하지 않으면 검토한 대안을 1~2줄로
6. **테스트**: 실제로 한 것만 — 추가한 자동화 테스트, 실행한 명령과 결과, 수동 절차. 검증하지 않은 것은 그렇다고 적습니다.
7. **위험과 배포**: 위험도, 마이그레이션(하위 호환 여부), 플래그와 기본값, 필요한 설정·시크릿, 롤백 절차, 지켜볼 모니터링
8. **리뷰 가이드**: 큰 PR의 추천 읽기 순서, 가장 꼼꼼히 봐야 할 1~3곳, 명시적 범위 외 항목
9. **스크린샷**: UI 변경 시(작성자가 넣어야 하면 전/후 자리표시자)
10. **링크**: 티켓, 설계 문서, 관련 PR, 후속 티켓
11. **템플릿 맞추기**: 템플릿이 있으면 제목 순서대로 쓰고, 해당 없는 섹션은 빈칸으로 두지 말고 제거하거나 "해당 없음"으로 표시합니다.

## 결과물 형식

```
제목: <type(scope): 요약>

## 요약
## 변경 사항
- ...
## 이 방식을 택한 이유 (선택)
## 테스트
- [x] 단위 테스트 추가: `path/...` — `<명령>` → exit 0 (<N> passed)
- [ ] 스테이징 수동 확인 — 미수행
## 위험과 배포
위험도: 낮음/보통/높음 — <이유>   플래그: <이름, 기본 off>   마이그레이션: <유/무, 하위 호환?>
롤백: <절차>
## 리뷰 가이드
`...`부터 보시고 `...` 순서를 권합니다. <...> 부분을 특히 봐 주세요. 범위 외: <...>
## 스크린샷 (UI만)
## 링크
Closes <ISSUE-123>
```

## 자체 점검

- [ ] 요약만 읽어도 리뷰어가 무엇을 왜 바꿨는지 설명할 수 있는가
- [ ] 테스트 섹션이 실제 실행한 것만 명령·결과와 함께 담고, 공백을 명시했는가
- [ ] 해당되는 경우 위험, 마이그레이션, 플래그, 롤백 정보가 있는가
- [ ] 동작 변경과 리팩터링을 구분했는가
- [ ] 저장소 템플릿과 제목 규칙을 따르고 빈 보일러플레이트 섹션이 없는가
- [ ] 시크릿, 내부 호스트명, 고객 데이터가 없고 스크린샷은 예시 데이터를 쓰는가

## 한계

- 작성자가 결과를 제공했거나 직접 실행해 exit code 0을 확인한 경우가 아니면 "모든 테스트 통과"를 쓰거나 테스트 체크박스를 체크하지 않습니다.
- 티켓 번호, 지표, 리뷰어 이름을 지어내지 않고 `[ISSUE-?]` 같은 자리표시자를 씁니다.
- 실제 diff를 설명합니다. diff와 명시된 의도가 다르면 덮지 말고 지적합니다.

skills.description: Diff, commits और ticket से साफ़ pull request title और description लिखता है — क्या बदला और क्यों, कैसे test हुआ (असली evidence के साथ), risk और rollout/rollback notes, और reviewers को कहाँ ध्यान देना है — repo में PR template हो तो उसे follow करता है। जब engineer कहे "PR description लिखो", "PR summary draft करो", "PR template भरो", "reviewers के लिए changes describe करो", या "इस PR को review करना आसान बनाओ", तब उपयोग करें।
skills.body:
# Pull Request Description Writer

ऐसा PR title और body तैयार करता है जिससे reviewer दो मिनट में change समझ ले और सही क्रम में review करे। यह mechanics से पहले intent समझाता है, ईमानदारी से बताता है कि change कैसे verify हुआ, risk और सबसे ज़्यादा ध्यान माँगने वाले हिस्सों को उजागर करता है, और ticket link करता है। जो testing हुई ही नहीं, उसका दावा कभी नहीं करता।

## कब उपयोग करें / कब नहीं

उपयोग करें जब:
- Branch तैयार है और PR title/body चाहिए, या मौजूदा description कमज़ोर है।
- Repo के PR template को असली changes से भरना है।
- बड़े PR के लिए reviewer guide (suggested reading order) चाहिए।

उपयोग न करें जब:
- Code review करवाना हो → `pull-request-review-hi`
- पूरे version के user-facing release notes → release process (`release-readiness-smoke-test-hi` में item के रूप में)
- Design document लिखना → `technical-design-doc-rfc-hi`

## पहले क्या पूछें

1. **Change**: base के मुकाबले diff या branch, commit messages।
2. **क्यों**: ticket/issue link, problem statement, या author का एक वाक्य।
3. **Template और conventions**: `.github/pull_request_template.md` या team format; title convention (Conventional Commits `feat(scope): …`, ticket prefix)। PR text किस भाषा में चाहिए (अक्सर English)?
4. **हुआ verification**: चलाए गए tests और results, manual testing steps, UI के screenshots/recordings।
5. **Rollout**: feature flag, migration, config changes, deploy order, rollback।
6. **Audience**: reviewers इस area से कितने परिचित हैं।

## चरण

1. **Diff पढ़ें** और changes को purpose से group करें (feature logic, refactor, tests, config, migration, docs)। Behavior changes को pure refactors से अलग रखें — reviewers इन्हें अलग तरह से पढ़ते हैं।
2. **Title लिखें**: imperative, specific, ≤72 characters, repo convention के अनुसार। उदाहरण: `feat(billing): prorate refunds for mid-cycle cancellations`।

skills.body:
# Pull Request Review

Performs the general-purpose review a strong senior engineer would give: first understand what the change is meant to do, then check whether it does that correctly and safely, whether it is tested, and whether it will be easy to live with. Every comment is labeled by severity, points to a specific location, explains *why*, and suggests a concrete fix. The review ends with an explicit verdict so the author knows exactly what blocks merge.

## When to use / when not to use

Use when:
- A PR, patch or local diff needs a review before merge.
- An author wants a self-review pass before requesting reviewers.

Do not use when — or use alongside:
- A focused security pass is needed (auth, input handling, secrets, personal data) → `secure-code-review`.
- The PR is a dependency or framework upgrade → `dependency-upgrade-review`.
- The main concern is latency, memory or query cost → `performance-code-review`.
- The author needs a PR description written → `pull-request-description-writer`.

## What to ask for first

1. **The diff**: PR link, patch, or branch compared to base; plus the PR description/ticket.
2. **Intent and scope**: what problem it solves; anything intentionally out of scope.
3. **Context**: language/framework, team conventions (style guide, lint rules, ADRs), and critical areas touched.
4. **Review depth**: quick pass vs. full review; any part the author specifically wants eyes on.
5. **Can I run things?** Tests, linters, type checks locally. If not, state that the review is static only.

## Steps

1. **Understand intent.** Read the description and ticket; write a one-paragraph summary of what the PR does. If you cannot, that is the first comment (unclear purpose or PR too large — suggest splitting above ~400 changed lines of logic).
2. **Map the change.** List files by role (logic, API, schema, config, tests, generated). Skip generated/vendored files but note if they look unexpectedly changed.
3. **Correctness.** Trace main paths and edge cases: null/empty, boundaries, error handling, concurrency/races, transactions and partial failure, time zones, retries/idempotency, resource cleanup, backward compatibility of APIs, events and schemas.
4. **Design.** Fit with existing architecture and patterns, right layer for the logic, duplication, naming, hidden coupling, public API surface, feature-flag hygiene.
5. **Tests.** Are new behaviors and the bug (if a fix) covered? Do assertions check behavior? Missing failure-path tests? Run them if possible and record the exit code.
6. **Operability.** Logging (no secrets/personal data in logs), metrics, error messages, config defaults, migrations and rollback, docs/changelog.
7. **Quick security and performance scan.** Obvious injection, authz gaps, secrets, N+1 queries, unbounded loops or payloads. Escalate to the dedicated skill if anything substantial appears.
8. **Write comments** with a severity label, location, issue, reason and suggestion. Batch repeated issues into one comment ("same in 4 places: …"). Ask questions when intent is unclear instead of asserting a bug.
9. **Verdict.** Approve only if there are no blocking comments; otherwise request changes and list blockers.

**Severity labels**
- **[blocker]** — bug, data loss, security hole, broken contract, failing/missing tests for core behavior. Must fix before merge.
- **[major]** — significant design, reliability or maintainability problem; fix now or agree on a ticketed follow-up.
- **[minor]** — improves clarity or robustness; author's call.
- **[nit]** — style or taste; never blocks.
- **[question]** — need information to judge.
- **[praise]** — call out something done well (be specific).

## Output format

```
## Summary
<what the PR does, in 2–4 sentences> | Risk: low/medium/high
Verified: <tests/lint/typecheck run with command + exit code | static review only>

## Verdict: APPROVE | APPROVE WITH NITS | REQUEST CHANGES
Blockers: <list or "none">

## Comments
**[blocker]** `path/file.ts:L42-48` — <issue>. Why: <impact>. Suggestion: <fix or code snippet>
**[minor]** `...`
...

## Tests to add
## Follow-ups (non-blocking, suggest tickets)
```

## Quality checks

- [ ] Every comment has severity, file:line, reason and a concrete suggestion or question.
- [ ] Blockers are real defects or risks, not preferences; nits are labeled nits.
- [ ] Verdict matches the comments (no approve with open blockers).
- [ ] Repeated issues grouped; review is proportionate to PR size.
- [ ] Tone is about the code, not the author; at least one specific positive note when deserved.
- [ ] Claims about runtime behavior are either verified by running or phrased as "likely"/questions.

## Limits

- Never state that tests, lint or builds pass unless they were run; judge by exit code and report the command. CI status shown in the PR counts only if you actually saw it.
- Do not invent APIs, library behaviors, CVEs or version facts; flag uncertainty.
- A review reduces risk; it does not guarantee correctness. The merge decision stays with the human reviewer and code owners.

# 풀 리퀘스트 리뷰

뛰어난 시니어 엔지니어가 하는 범용 코드 리뷰를 수행합니다. 먼저 변경의 의도를 이해하고, 그 의도를 정확하고 안전하게 구현했는지, 테스트되었는지, 앞으로 유지보수하기 쉬운지를 확인합니다. 모든 코멘트에는 심각도 라벨, 구체적 위치, 이유, 구체적 제안이 붙습니다. 마지막에 명확한 판정을 내려 작성자가 무엇이 머지를 막는지 정확히 알 수 있게 합니다.

## 사용 시점 / 사용하지 않는 경우

사용하는 경우:
- 머지 전에 PR, 패치, 로컬 diff 리뷰가 필요할 때
- 작성자가 리뷰어 지정 전에 셀프 리뷰를 원할 때

다음은 별도 스킬을 쓰거나 병행합니다.
- 인증, 입력 처리, 시크릿, 개인정보 등 보안 집중 점검 → `secure-code-review-ko`
- 의존성·프레임워크 업그레이드 PR → `dependency-upgrade-review-ko`
- 지연·메모리·쿼리 비용이 주 관심사 → `performance-code-review-ko`
- PR 설명 작성 → `pull-request-description-writer-ko`

## 먼저 확인할 사항

1. **diff**: PR 링크, 패치, 또는 base 대비 브랜치 + PR 설명/티켓
2. **의도와 범위**: 해결하려는 문제, 의도적으로 제외한 것

4. **리뷰 깊이**: 빠른 확인 vs 전체 리뷰, 작성자가 특히 봐 달라는 부분
5. **실행 가능 여부**: 로컬에서 테스트·린트·타입 체크를 돌릴 수 있는지. 불가하면 정적 리뷰임을 밝힙니다.

## 리뷰 절차

1. **의도를 파악합니다.** 설명과 티켓을 읽고 PR이 하는 일을 한 문단으로 요약합니다. 요약이 안 되면 그것이 첫 코멘트입니다(목적 불명확, 또는 PR이 너무 큼 — 로직 변경이 약 400줄을 넘으면 분할 제안).
2. **변경을 분류합니다.** 파일을 역할별로(로직, API, 스키마, 설정, 테스트, 생성 코드) 나눕니다. 생성·vendored 파일은 건너뛰되 예상 밖 변경은 지적합니다.
3. **정확성.** 주요 경로와 엣지 케이스를 추적합니다: null/빈 값, 경계, 오류 처리, 동시성·경쟁 조건, 트랜잭션과 부분 실패, 타임존, 재시도·멱등성, 리소스 정리, API·이벤트·스키마의 하위 호환
4. **설계.** 기존 아키텍처·패턴과의 일관성, 로직의 계층 위치, 중복, 네이밍, 숨은 결합, 공개 API 범위, 피처 플래그 정리
5. **테스트.** 새 동작과 (버그 수정이라면) 해당 버그가 커버되는지, assertion이 동작을 검증하는지, 실패 경로 테스트 누락은 없는지. 가능하면 실행하고 exit code를 기록합니다.
6. **운영성.** 로그(시크릿·개인정보 미포함), 메트릭, 오류 메시지, 설정 기본값, 마이그레이션과 롤백, 문서/변경 내역
7. **보안·성능 빠른 확인.** 명백한 인젝션, 권한 누락, 시크릿, N+1 쿼리, 무제한 루프·페이로드. 중대한 것이 보이면 전용 스킬로 넘깁니다.
8. **코멘트를 작성합니다.** 심각도 라벨, 위치, 문제, 이유, 제안. 반복되는 문제는 하나로 묶습니다("같은 패턴 4곳: …"). 의도가 불분명하면 버그라고 단정하지 말고 질문합니다. 톤은 사람이 아니라 코드를 향하게 하고, "~하는 게 어떨까요?", "~로 보이는데 의도하신 건지 궁금합니다"처럼 제안형으로 씁니다. 필수 수정은 돌려 말하지 말고 분명히 표시합니다.
9. **판정합니다.** 차단 코멘트가 없을 때만 승인하고, 있으면 변경 요청과 함께 차단 사유를 나열합니다.

- **[필수]** — 버그, 데이터 손실, 보안 구멍, 계약 파손, 핵심 동작의 테스트 실패·누락. 머지 전 반드시 수정

- **[사소]** (nit) — 스타일·취향. 절대 차단하지 않음
- **[질문]** — 판단에 정보가 필요함
- **[칭찬]** — 잘한 점을 구체적으로 언급

```
## 요약
<PR이 하는 일 2~4문장> | 위험도: 낮음/보통/높음

## 후속 작업 (비차단, 티켓 제안)
```

## 자체 점검

- [ ] 모든 코멘트에 심각도, 파일:라인, 이유, 구체적 제안 또는 질문이 있는가
- [ ] [필수]는 취향이 아니라 실제 결함·위험이며, 사소한 의견은 [사소]로 표시했는가

skills.body:
# Pull Request Review

वह general-purpose review करता है जो एक मज़बूत senior engineer देगा: पहले समझें कि change क्या करना चाहता है, फिर देखें कि वह यह सही और सुरक्षित तरीके से करता है या नहीं, tested है या नहीं, और आगे maintain करना आसान होगा या नहीं। हर comment पर severity label, specific location, *क्यों* की व्याख्या और ठोस suggestion होता है। Review एक explicit verdict के साथ ख़त्म होता है ताकि author को ठीक-ठीक पता हो कि merge किस चीज़ से रुका है।

## कब उपयोग करें / कब नहीं

उपयोग करें जब:
- Merge से पहले PR, patch या local diff का review चाहिए।
- Author reviewers माँगने से पहले self-review pass चाहता है।

इनके लिए अलग skill इस्तेमाल करें या साथ में चलाएँ:
- Focused security pass (auth, input handling, secrets, personal data) → `secure-code-review-hi`
- Dependency या framework upgrade PR → `dependency-upgrade-review-hi`
- मुख्य चिंता latency, memory या query cost → `performance-code-review-hi`
- PR description लिखना → `pull-request-description-writer-hi`

## पहले क्या पूछें

1. **Diff**: PR link, patch, या base से compared branch; साथ में PR description/ticket।
2. **Intent और scope**: कौन-सी समस्या हल होती है; क्या जानबूझकर scope से बाहर है।
3. **Context**: language/framework, team conventions (style guide, lint rules, ADRs), critical areas।
4. **Review depth**: quick pass या full review; author किस हिस्से पर ख़ास नज़र चाहता है।

skills.body:
# Secure Code Review

A defensive review of code the user owns, aimed at finding exploitable weaknesses before they ship. It follows the OWASP Top 10 categories and ASVS-style controls, but always reasons from the actual data flow: where untrusted input enters, what it can reach, and who is allowed to do what. Each finding includes a realistic attack scenario, severity, and a concrete fix — no generic checklists pasted as findings.

## When to use / when not to use

Use when:
- A PR touches authentication, sessions, authorization, payments, file handling, external URLs, templates, queries, crypto, or personal data.
- A new public endpoint, webhook, or admin feature is added.
- A periodic security pass on a module is requested.

Do not use when:
- General code quality review → `pull-request-review` (it will escalate here).
- Reviewing third-party package upgrades for known vulnerabilities → `dependency-upgrade-review`.
- Testing systems the user does not own or is not authorised to assess — decline.

## What to ask for first

1. **Code and scope**: diff or paths; entry points (routes, handlers, jobs, CLI).
2. **Architecture**: framework, auth mechanism (session, JWT, OAuth/OIDC), tenancy model, where it is deployed, what sits in front (WAF, gateway).
3. **Data sensitivity**: does it handle personal data, credentials, payment data, health data? Which jurisdictions' privacy laws apply (e.g. GDPR, India DPDP Act, Korea PIPA)?
4. **Threat model**: who are the users and attackers (anonymous internet, authenticated user, other tenant, insider)?
5. **Tools**: may I run SAST/secret scanners/dependency audit locally (e.g. Semgrep, gitleaks, `npm audit`, `pip-audit`)?

## Steps

1. **Map trust boundaries.** List entry points and the untrusted inputs each accepts (body, query, headers, cookies, files, webhooks, queue messages). Trace each to sinks: DB, shell, filesystem, HTML, redirects, outbound HTTP, deserializers, logs.
2. **Access control (A01).** Every endpoint enforces authN and object-level authZ server-side (IDOR: can user A fetch user B's resource by ID?); tenant isolation in queries; admin-only actions gated; deny by default.
3. **Injection (A03).** Parameterised queries/ORM without raw string concatenation; no shell with user input; template auto-escaping not disabled; NoSQL operator injection; LDAP/XPath; header and log injection.
4. **Input & output handling.** Allow-list validation, size limits, file upload type/size/storage location, path traversal, XSS (output encoding, `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`/`v-html`), open redirects, CSRF protection on cookie-authenticated state changes, CORS configuration.
5. **AuthN & sessions (A07).** Password hashing with a slow algorithm (bcrypt/scrypt/Argon2), MFA flows, token expiry and rotation, JWT algorithm pinning and signature verification, session fixation, brute-force/rate limiting, secure cookie flags.
6. **Crypto & secrets (A02).** No hard-coded keys/tokens; secrets from a manager or env; TLS verification not disabled; modern algorithms; random from a CSPRNG.
7. **SSRF & deserialization (A10, A08).** Outbound requests to user-supplied URLs restricted (block internal ranges/metadata endpoints); no unsafe deserialization of untrusted data; webhook signature verification.
8. **Misconfiguration (A05).** Debug modes, verbose errors with stack traces, default credentials, permissive security headers.
9. **Logging & privacy (A09).** Security events logged (login failures, permission denials) without logging passwords, tokens or unnecessary personal data; retention aligned with policy; data minimisation and deletion paths exist where personal data is stored.
10. **Dependencies (A06).** New packages and versions; run the ecosystem's audit tool if allowed and report real output.
11. **Rate findings** with severity based on exploitability × impact, write the fix, and suggest a test that proves the fix (e.g. "user B gets 403 on user A's invoice").

**Severity**: **Critical** (remote, unauthenticated, data exposure/RCE) · **High** (authenticated privilege escalation, IDOR on sensitive data) · **Medium** (requires unusual conditions, limited impact) · **Low** (defense-in-depth, hardening) · **Info**.

## Output format

```
## Scope & threat model
Entry points reviewed: ...  Out of scope: ...  Tools run: <name, command, exit code | none>

## Findings
### [High] IDOR on GET /invoices/:id  — OWASP A01
Location: `api/invoices.ts:31`
Scenario: an authenticated user changes the id and reads another tenant's invoice.
Evidence: query filters by id only, no tenant/owner check.
Fix: <code-level fix>
Test: <test that proves it>

## Privacy / compliance notes (personal data, logging, retention)
## Hardening suggestions (Low/Info)
## Verdict: no blocking issues | fix Critical/High before merge
```

## Quality checks

- [ ] Every finding has a concrete location, plausible attack scenario, severity rationale and fix.
- [ ] Object-level authorization checked for every new endpoint, not only authentication.
- [ ] No generic "consider validating input" without pointing at a specific sink.
- [ ] False-positive risk stated where data flow could not be fully traced.
- [ ] Personal data handling and logging reviewed against the stated privacy regime.
- [ ] Scanner results quoted from actual runs, with command and exit code.

## Limits

- Defensive review of the user's own code only; do not produce weaponised exploits beyond what is needed to explain and test the fix.
- Never invent CVE IDs, advisory numbers, or affected version ranges; cite them only from a tool's output or an advisory the user provided, otherwise say "check advisories".
- Never claim code is "secure" — state what was reviewed and what was not. Static review misses runtime and configuration issues; recommend penetration testing for high-risk releases.
- Privacy-law points are engineering checks, not legal advice; confirm obligations with the privacy/legal team.

- Defensive review of the user's own code only; do not produce weaponised exploits beyond what is needed to explain and test the fix.
- Never invent CVE IDs, advisory numbers, or affected version ranges; cite them only from a tool's output or an advisory the user provided, otherwise say "check advisories".
- Never claim code is "secure" — state what was reviewed and what was not. Static review misses runtime and configuration issues; recommend penetration testing for high-risk releases.

skills.body:
# 보안 코드 리뷰 (시큐어 코딩)

사용자가 소유한 코드를 배포 전에 방어적 관점에서 검토해 악용 가능한 약점을 찾습니다. OWASP Top 10 분류와 ASVS 수준의 통제를 기본 틀로 쓰되, 항상 실제 데이터 흐름(신뢰할 수 없는 입력이 어디로 들어와 어디까지 닿는지, 누가 무엇을 할 수 있는지)에서 출발합니다. 국내 서비스라면 개인정보 보호법과 ISMS-P 인증기준의 개발보안·접근통제·암호화 요구도 함께 확인합니다. 모든 발견 사항에는 현실적인 공격 시나리오, 심각도, 구체적 수정안이 붙으며, 일반 체크리스트를 발견 사항처럼 붙여넣지 않습니다.

## 사용 시점 / 사용하지 않는 경우

사용하는 경우:
- PR이 인증, 세션, 인가, 결제, 파일 처리, 외부 URL, 템플릿, 쿼리, 암호화, 개인정보를 다룰 때
- 새 공개 엔드포인트, 웹훅, 관리자 기능이 추가될 때
- 모듈 단위 정기 보안 점검, ISMS-P 심사 대비 개발보안 점검 요청

사용하지 않는 경우:
- 일반 코드 품질 리뷰 → `pull-request-review-ko`(필요 시 이 스킬로 넘어옵니다)
- 외부 패키지 업그레이드의 알려진 취약점 검토 → `dependency-upgrade-review-ko`
- 사용자가 소유하지 않았거나 점검 권한이 없는 시스템 — 거절합니다.

## 먼저 확인할 사항

1. **코드와 범위**: diff 또는 경로, 진입점(라우트, 핸들러, 배치, CLI)
2. **아키텍처**: 프레임워크, 인증 방식(세션, JWT, OAuth/OIDC), 멀티테넌시 구조, 배포 위치, 앞단 구성(WAF, 게이트웨이)
3. **데이터 민감도**: 개인정보, 고유식별정보(주민등록번호 등), 민감정보, 비밀번호, 결제·신용정보 처리 여부와 대략적 정보주체 규모
4. **적용 기준**: 개인정보 보호법, ISMS-P 인증 대상 여부, 전자금융 관련 규정 적용 여부, 사내 시큐어코딩 가이드(KISA 가이드 등)
5. **위협 모델**: 사용자와 공격자(비인증 외부, 인증 사용자, 타 테넌트, 내부자)
6. **도구**: 로컬에서 SAST·시크릿 스캐너·의존성 감사(Semgrep, gitleaks, `npm audit`, `pip-audit` 등) 실행 가능 여부

## 리뷰 절차

1. **신뢰 경계를 그립니다.** 진입점과 각 진입점이 받는 비신뢰 입력(body, query, header, cookie, 파일, 웹훅, 큐 메시지)을 나열하고 sink(DB, shell, 파일시스템, HTML, 리다이렉트, 외부 HTTP, 역직렬화, 로그)까지 추적합니다.
2. **접근 통제(A01).** 모든 엔드포인트가 서버 측에서 인증과 객체 단위 인가를 수행하는지(IDOR: 사용자 A가 ID만 바꿔 B의 자원을 조회할 수 있는가), 쿼리의 테넌트 격리, 관리자 기능 통제, 기본 거부
3. **인젝션(A03).** 문자열 결합 없는 파라미터 바인딩/ORM, 사용자 입력이 들어가는 shell 실행 금지, 템플릿 자동 이스케이프 유지, NoSQL 연산자 인젝션, 헤더·로그 인젝션
4. **입출력 처리.** 허용 목록 검증, 크기 제한, 파일 업로드(확장자·MIME·크기·저장 위치·실행 권한), 경로 조작, XSS(출력 인코딩, `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`/`v-html`), 오픈 리다이렉트, 쿠키 인증 상태 변경의 CSRF 방어, CORS 설정
5. **인증·세션(A07).** 비밀번호는 안전한 일방향 해시(bcrypt/scrypt/Argon2), MFA 흐름, 토큰 만료·갱신, JWT 알고리즘 고정과 서명 검증, 세션 고정, 무차별 대입 방지(로그인 실패 횟수 제한), 쿠키 보안 속성
6. **암호화·시크릿(A02).** 하드코딩된 키·토큰 금지, 시크릿 매니저/환경 변수 사용, TLS 검증 비활성화 금지, 최신 알고리즘, CSPRNG 사용. 고유식별정보·비밀번호 등 법령상 암호화 대상이 저장·전송 시 암호화되는지
7. **SSRF·역직렬화(A10, A08).** 사용자 제공 URL로의 외부 요청 제한(내부 대역·클라우드 메타데이터 차단), 비신뢰 데이터의 안전하지 않은 역직렬화 금지, 웹훅 서명 검증
8. **설정 오류(A05).** 디버그 모드, 스택 트레이스 노출, 기본 계정, 보안 헤더 누락
9. **로깅·개인정보(A09) — 국내 기준 점검.**
   - 로그인 실패, 권한 거부 등 보안 이벤트를 남기되 비밀번호, 토큰, 불필요한 개인정보는 로그에 남기지 않음(마스킹)
   - 개인정보처리시스템 접속기록(누가, 언제, 어디서, 어떤 정보주체의 정보를, 무엇을 했는지)이 남고 위·변조 방지 대책이 있는지, 보관 기간이 안전성 확보조치 기준에 맞는지(일반적으로 1년 이상, 대규모·고유식별정보·민감정보 처리 시 2년 이상 — 현행 고시 확인 필요)
   - 개인정보 다운로드·대량 조회 기능에 사유 확인·모니터링이 있는지
   - 수집 최소화, 보유기간 경과 시 파기 경로, 주민등록번호 처리 제한 위반 여부
   - 유출 탐지 시 통지·신고(현행법상 72시간 이내 기준 — 확인 필요)를 지원할 수 있는 로깅·알림이 있는지
   - ISMS-P 대상이면 인증 및 권한관리, 접근통제, 암호화 적용, 정보시스템 도입 및 개발 보안 관련 인증기준과의 대응(항목 번호는 현행 인증기준으로 확인)
10. **의존성(A06).** 신규 패키지와 버전. 허용되면 감사 도구를 실행하고 실제 출력만 보고합니다.
11. **평가와 수정안.** 악용 가능성 × 영향으로 심각도를 정하고 수정안과 수정을 증명할 테스트(예: "사용자 B가 A의 청구서에 접근하면 403")를 제안합니다.

**심각도**: **치명**(원격·비인증, 데이터 노출/RCE) · **높음**(인증 사용자의 권한 상승, 민감 데이터 IDOR) · **보통**(특수 조건 필요, 제한적 영향) · **낮음**(심층 방어, 하드닝) · **참고**

## 결과물 형식

```
## 범위와 위협 모델
검토 진입점: ...  범위 외: ...  실행 도구: <이름, 명령, exit code | 없음>

## 발견 사항
### [높음] GET /invoices/:id IDOR — OWASP A01
위치: `api/invoices.ts:31`
시나리오: 인증된 사용자가 id를 바꿔 다른 테넌트의 청구서를 조회
근거: id로만 조회하고 테넌트/소유자 확인 없음
수정안: <코드 수준 수정>
검증 테스트: <수정을 증명할 테스트>

## 개인정보 보호법 / ISMS-P 관점 확인 사항
## 하드닝 제안 (낮음/참고)
## 판정: 차단 사유 없음 | 치명·높음 수정 후 머지
```

## 자체 점검

- [ ] 발견 사항마다 구체적 위치, 현실적 공격 시나리오, 심각도 근거, 수정안이 있는가
- [ ] 모든 신규 엔드포인트에 대해 인증뿐 아니라 객체 단위 인가를 확인했는가
- [ ] 구체적 sink 없이 "입력 검증을 고려하세요" 같은 일반론을 쓰지 않았는가
- [ ] 데이터 흐름을 끝까지 추적하지 못한 곳은 오탐 가능성을 밝혔는가
- [ ] 개인정보 로깅·접속기록·암호화·파기를 국내 기준으로 점검했는가
- [ ] 스캐너 결과를 실제 실행 출력에서 명령·exit code와 함께 인용했는가

## 한계

- 사용자 소유 코드에 대한 방어적 리뷰만 수행합니다. 수정 설명과 검증에 필요한 수준을 넘는 공격 코드는 작성하지 않습니다.
- CVE ID, 권고 번호, 영향 버전 범위를 지어내지 않습니다. 도구 출력이나 사용자가 제공한 권고문에 있을 때만 인용하고, 아니면 "권고문 확인 필요"로 둡니다.
- 코드가 "안전하다"고 단정하지 않고 검토한 범위와 검토하지 않은 범위를 밝힙니다. 정적 리뷰는 런타임·설정 문제를 놓칠 수 있으므로 고위험 배포에는 모의해킹을 권합니다.
- 개인정보 보호법·ISMS-P 관련 내용은 엔지니어링 점검이며 법률 자문이 아닙니다. 고시·인증기준은 개정될 수 있으므로 개인정보 보호책임자·법무팀과 현행 기준을 확인합니다.

## 리뷰 절차

1. **신뢰 경계를 그립니다.** 진입점과 각 진입점이 받는 비신뢰 입력(body, query, header, cookie, 파일, 웹훅, 큐 메시지)을 나열하고 sink(DB, shell, 파일시스템, HTML, 리다이렉트, 외부 HTTP, 역직렬화, 로그)까지 추적합니다.
2. **접근 통제(A01).** 모든 엔드포인트가 서버 측에서 인증과 객체 단위 인가를 수행하는지(IDOR: 사용자 A가 ID만 바꿔 B의 자원을 조회할 수 있는가), 쿼리의 테넌트 격리, 관리자 기능 통제, 기본 거부
3. **인젝션(A03).** 문자열 결합 없는 파라미터 바인딩/ORM, 사용자 입력이 들어가는 shell 실행 금지, 템플릿 자동 이스케이프 유지, NoSQL 연산자 인젝션, 헤더·로그 인젝션
4. **입출력 처리.** 허용 목록 검증, 크기 제한, 파일 업로드(확장자·MIME·크기·저장 위치·실행 권한), 경로 조작, XSS(출력 인코딩, `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`/`v-html`), 오픈 리다이렉트, 쿠키 인증 상태 변경의 CSRF 방어, CORS 설정
5. **인증·세션(A07).** 비밀번호는 안전한 일방향 해시(bcrypt/scrypt/Argon2), MFA 흐름, 토큰 만료·갱신, JWT 알고리즘 고정과 서명 검증, 세션 고정, 무차별 대입 방지(로그인 실패 횟수 제한), 쿠키 보안 속성
6. **암호화·시크릿(A02).** 하드코딩된 키·토큰 금지, 시크릿 매니저/환경 변수 사용, TLS 검증 비활성화 금지, 최신 알고리즘, CSPRNG 사용. 고유식별정보·비밀번호 등 법령상 암호화 대상이 저장·전송 시 암호화되는지
7. **SSRF·역직렬화(A10, A08).** 사용자 제공 URL로의 외부 요청 제한(내부 대역·클라우드 메타데이터 차단), 비신뢰 데이터의 안전하지 않은 역직렬화 금지, 웹훅 서명 검증
8. **설정 오류(A05).** 디버그 모드, 스택 트레이스 노출, 기본 계정, 보안 헤더 누락
9. **로깅·개인정보(A09) — 국내 기준 점검.**
   - 로그인 실패, 권한 거부 등 보안 이벤트를 남기되 비밀번호, 토큰, 불필요한 개인정보는 로그에 남기지 않음(마스킹)
   - 개인정보처리시스템 접속기록(누가, 언제, 어디서, 어떤 정보주체의 정보를, 무엇을 했는지)이 남고 위·변조 방지 대책이 있는지, 보관 기간이 안전성 확보조치 기준에 맞는지(일반적으로 1년 이상, 대규모·고유식별정보·민감정보 처리 시 2년 이상 — 현행 고시 확인 필요)
   - 개인정보 다운로드·대량 조회 기능에 사유 확인·모니터링이 있는지
   - 수집 최소화, 보유기간 경과 시 파기 경로, 주민등록번호 처리 제한 위반 여부
   - 유출 탐지 시 통지·신고(현행법상 72시간 이내 기준 — 확인 필요)를 지원할 수 있는 로깅·알림이 있는지
   - ISMS-P 대상이면 인증 및 권한관리, 접근통제, 암호화 적용, 정보시스템 도입 및 개발 보안 관련 인증기준과의 대응(항목 번호는 현행 인증기준으로 확인)
10. **의존성(A06).** 신규 패키지와 버전. 허용되면 감사 도구를 실행하고 실제 출력만 보고합니다.
11. **평가와 수정안.** 악용 가능성 × 영향으로 심각도를 정하고 수정안과 수정을 증명할 테스트(예: "사용자 B가 A의 청구서에 접근하면 403")를 제안합니다.

**심각도**: **치명**(원격·비인증, 데이터 노출/RCE) · **높음**(인증 사용자의 권한 상승, 민감 데이터 IDOR) · **보통**(특수 조건 필요, 제한적 영향) · **낮음**(심층 방어, 하드닝) · **참고**

## 결과물 형식

```
## 범위와 위협 모델
검토 진입점: ...  범위 외: ...  실행 도구: <이름, 명령, exit code | 없음>

## 발견 사항
### [높음] GET /invoices/:id IDOR — OWASP A01
위치: `api/invoices.ts:31`
시나리오: 인증된 사용자가 id를 바꿔 다른 테넌트의 청구서를 조회
근거: id로만 조회하고 테넌트/소유자 확인 없음
수정안: <코드 수준 수정>
검증 테스트: <수정을 증명할 테스트>

## 개인정보 보호법 / ISMS-P 관점 확인 사항
## 하드닝 제안 (낮음/참고)
## 판정: 차단 사유 없음 | 치명·높음 수정 후 머지
```

## 자체 점검

- [ ] 발견 사항마다 구체적 위치, 현실적 공격 시나리오, 심각도 근거, 수정안이 있는가
- [ ] 모든 신규 엔드포인트에 대해 인증뿐 아니라 객체 단위 인가를 확인했는가
- [ ] 구체적 sink 없이 "입력 검증을 고려하세요" 같은 일반론을 쓰지 않았는가
- [ ] 데이터 흐름을 끝까지 추적하지 못한 곳은 오탐 가능성을 밝혔는가
- [ ] 개인정보 로깅·접속기록·암호화·파기를 국내 기준으로 점검했는가
- [ ] 스캐너 결과를 실제 실행 출력에서 명령·exit code와 함께 인용했는가

## 한계

- 사용자 소유 코드에 대한 방어적 리뷰만 수행합니다. 수정 설명과 검증에 필요한 수준을 넘는 공격 코드는 작성하지 않습니다.
- CVE ID, 권고 번호, 영향 버전 범위를 지어내지 않습니다. 도구 출력이나 사용자가 제공한 권고문에 있을 때만 인용하고, 아니면 "권고문 확인 필요"로 둡니다.
- 코드가 "안전하다"고 단정하지 않고 검토한 범위와 검토하지 않은 범위를 밝힙니다. 정적 리뷰는 런타임·설정 문제를 놓칠 수 있으므로 고위험 배포에는 모의해킹을 권합니다.
- 개인정보 보호법·ISMS-P 관련 내용은 엔지니어링 점검이며 법률 자문이 아닙니다. 고시·인증기준은 개정될 수 있으므로 개인정보 보호책임자·법무팀과 현행 기준을 확인합니다.

skills.body:
# Secure Code Review

User के अपने code का defensive review, ताकि exploitable कमज़ोरियाँ ship होने से पहले मिलें। यह OWASP Top 10 categories और ASVS-style controls को ढाँचे के रूप में इस्तेमाल करता है, पर हमेशा असली data flow से सोचता है: untrusted input कहाँ से आता है, कहाँ तक पहुँच सकता है, और कौन क्या कर सकता है। भारत में चलने वाली services के लिए DPDP Act 2023 के security safeguards व breach readiness और CERT-In के logging requirements को engineering checks के रूप में देखता है। हर finding में realistic attack scenario, severity और ठोस fix होता है — generic checklist को finding बनाकर paste नहीं किया जाता।

## कब उपयोग करें / कब नहीं

उपयोग करें जब:
- PR authentication, sessions, authorization, payments/UPI, file handling, external URLs, templates, queries, crypto या personal data छूता हो।
- नया public endpoint, webhook या admin feature जुड़ रहा हो।
- किसी module का periodic security pass या audit की तैयारी माँगी गई हो।

उपयोग न करें जब:
- General code quality review → `pull-request-review-hi` (ज़रूरत पर यहाँ escalate करेगा)
- Third-party package upgrades की known vulnerabilities → `dependency-upgrade-review-hi`
- ऐसे systems जिनका user owner नहीं या जिनकी जाँच की अनुमति नहीं — मना करें।

## पहले क्या पूछें

1. **Code और scope**: diff या paths; entry points (routes, handlers, jobs, CLI)।
2. **Architecture**: framework, auth mechanism (session, JWT, OAuth/OIDC), tenancy model, deployment, आगे क्या है (WAF, API gateway)।
3. **Data sensitivity**: personal data, Aadhaar/PAN जैसे identifiers, credentials, payment data, health data, बच्चों का data?
4. **लागू नियम**: DPDP Act 2023 (Data Fiduciary/Processor की भूमिका), CERT-In Directions, sector regulator (जैसे RBI payment data localisation, अगर लागू), GDPR अगर EU users हैं।
5. **Threat model**: users और attackers कौन हैं (anonymous internet, authenticated user, दूसरा tenant, insider)।
6. **Tools**: क्या locally SAST/secret scanners/dependency audit (Semgrep, gitleaks, `npm audit`, `pip-audit`) चला सकते हैं?

## चरण

1. **Trust boundaries map करें।** Entry points और हर एक के untrusted inputs (body, query, headers, cookies, files, webhooks, queue messages) list करें; हर एक को sinks तक trace करें: DB, shell, filesystem, HTML, redirects, outbound HTTP, deserializers, logs।
2. **Access control (A01)।** हर endpoint server-side पर authN और object-level authZ करता है (IDOR: क्या user A, ID बदलकर user B का resource ले सकता है?); queries में tenant isolation; admin actions gated; default deny।
3. **Injection (A03)।** Raw string concatenation के बिना parameterised queries/ORM; user input के साथ shell नहीं; template auto-escaping बंद नहीं; NoSQL operator injection; header और log injection।
4. **Input & output handling।** Allow-list validation, size limits, file upload (type/size/storage location/execute permission), path traversal, XSS (output encoding, `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`/`v-html`), open redirects, cookie-authenticated state changes पर CSRF protection, CORS configuration।
5. **AuthN & sessions (A07)।** Slow algorithm से password hashing (bcrypt/scrypt/Argon2), OTP/MFA flows (OTP expiry, attempt limits, OTP brute force), token expiry और rotation, JWT algorithm pinning और signature verification, session fixation, rate limiting, secure cookie flags।
6. **Crypto & secrets (A02)।** Hard-coded keys/tokens नहीं; secrets manager या env से; TLS verification disabled नहीं; modern algorithms; CSPRNG से randomness; sensitive identifiers का storage और transit में encryption/masking।
7. **SSRF & deserialization (A10, A08)।** User-supplied URLs पर outbound requests सीमित (internal ranges/cloud metadata endpoints block); untrusted data का unsafe deserialization नहीं; payment gateway/webhook signature verification।
8. **Misconfiguration (A05)।** Debug modes, stack traces वाली verbose errors, default credentials, कमज़ोर security headers।
9. **Logging & privacy (A09) — भारतीय संदर्भ के checks:**
   - Security events (login failures, permission denials) log हों, पर passwords, OTPs, tokens, पूरे Aadhaar/card numbers या अनावश्यक personal data log न हों (masking)।
   - DPDP Act 2023: purpose limitation और data minimisation (जितना ज़रूरी उतना ही collect), consent withdrawal और erasure के code paths, बच्चों के data के लिए verifiable parental consent का flow, retention ख़त्म होने पर deletion।
   - DPDP Rules 2025 (13 Nov 2025 को notified, obligations चरणबद्ध रूप से लागू — commencement dates verify करें): reasonable security safeguards (encryption/masking, access control, access logs की monitoring और retention), और personal data breach की सूचना Data Protection Board व प्रभावित Data Principals को — विस्तृत report 72 घंटे के भीतर। क्या code breach detect करने और प्रभावित users पहचानने लायक audit data रखता है?
   - CERT-In Directions (28 अप्रैल 2022): निर्दिष्ट cyber incidents की report 6 घंटे के भीतर, ICT system logs 180 दिन तक भारत के भीतर सुरक्षित रखना, और system clocks का NTP sync (NIC/NPL servers या उनसे traceable)। Changed services के logs इन requirements के अनुरूप retention/location पर जाते हैं या नहीं — verify करें।
10. **Dependencies (A06)।** नए packages और versions; अनुमति हो तो ecosystem audit tool चलाएँ और असली output report करें।
11. **Findings rate करें** — exploitability × impact से severity, fix लिखें, और fix साबित करने वाला test सुझाएँ (जैसे "user B को user A के invoice पर 403 मिले")।

**Severity**: **Critical** (remote, unauthenticated, data exposure/RCE) · **High** (authenticated privilege escalation, sensitive data पर IDOR) · **Medium** (असामान्य conditions चाहिए, सीमित impact) · **Low** (defense-in-depth, hardening) · **Info**।

## Output format

```
## Scope और threat model
Reviewed entry points: ...  Out of scope: ...  Tools run: <name, command, exit code | none>

## Findings
### [High] GET /invoices/:id पर IDOR — OWASP A01
Location: `api/invoices.ts:31`
Scenario: authenticated user id बदलकर दूसरे tenant का invoice पढ़ लेता है।
Evidence: query सिर्फ़ id से filter करती है, tenant/owner check नहीं।
Fix: <code-level fix>
Test: <fix साबित करने वाला test>

## DPDP / CERT-In notes (personal data, logging, retention, breach readiness)
## Hardening suggestions (Low/Info)
## Verdict: कोई blocking issue नहीं | merge से पहले Critical/High fix करें
```

## Quality checks

- [ ] हर finding में ठोस location, plausible attack scenario, severity का कारण और fix है।
- [ ] हर नए endpoint के लिए सिर्फ़ authentication नहीं, object-level authorization भी check हुआ।
- [ ] किसी specific sink की ओर इशारा किए बिना "input validate करने पर विचार करें" जैसी generic बातें नहीं।
- [ ] जहाँ data flow पूरी तरह trace नहीं हो सका, false-positive की संभावना बताई।
- [ ] Personal data handling, logging, retention और breach readiness भारतीय संदर्भ में देखी गई।
- [ ] Scanner results असली runs से, command और exit code के साथ।

## सीमाएँ

- सिर्फ़ user के अपने code का defensive review; fix समझाने और test करने से ज़्यादा weaponised exploits नहीं।
- CVE IDs, advisory numbers या affected version ranges कभी न गढ़ें; सिर्फ़ tool output या user द्वारा दी गई advisory से quote करें, वरना "advisories check करें" लिखें।
- Code को कभी "secure" घोषित न करें — बताएँ क्या review हुआ और क्या नहीं। Static review runtime और configuration issues miss कर सकता है; high-risk releases के लिए penetration testing (जैसे CERT-In empanelled auditor से) सुझाएँ।
- DPDP Act/Rules और CERT-In से जुड़े points engineering checks हैं, legal advice नहीं; समय-सीमाएँ, commencement dates और दायित्व legal/privacy team और आधिकारिक notifications से verify करें।

- PR authentication, sessions, authorization, payments/UPI, file handling, external URLs, templates, queries, crypto या personal data छूता हो।
- नया public endpoint, webhook या admin feature जुड़ रहा हो।
- किसी module का periodic security pass या audit की तैयारी माँगी गई हो।

उपयोग न करें जब:
- General code quality review → `pull-request-review-hi` (ज़रूरत पर यहाँ escalate करेगा)
- Third-party package upgrades की known vulnerabilities → `dependency-upgrade-review-hi`
- ऐसे systems जिनका user owner नहीं या जिनकी जाँच की अनुमति नहीं — मना करें।

## पहले क्या पूछें

1. **Code और scope**: diff या paths; entry points (routes, handlers, jobs, CLI)।
2. **Architecture**: framework, auth mechanism (session, JWT, OAuth/OIDC), tenancy model, deployment, आगे क्या है (WAF, API gateway)।
3. **Data sensitivity**: personal data, Aadhaar/PAN जैसे identifiers, credentials, payment data, health data, बच्चों का data?
4. **लागू नियम**: DPDP Act 2023 (Data Fiduciary/Processor की भूमिका), CERT-In Directions, sector regulator (जैसे RBI payment data localisation, अगर लागू), GDPR अगर EU users हैं।
5. **Threat model**: users और attackers कौन हैं (anonymous internet, authenticated user, दूसरा tenant, insider)।
6. **Tools**: क्या locally SAST/secret scanners/dependency audit (Semgrep, gitleaks, `npm audit`, `pip-audit`) चला सकते हैं?

## चरण

1. **Trust boundaries map करें।** Entry points और हर एक के untrusted inputs (body, query, headers, cookies, files, webhooks, queue messages) list करें; हर एक को sinks तक trace करें: DB, shell, filesystem, HTML, redirects, outbound HTTP, deserializers, logs।
2. **Access control (A01)।** हर endpoint server-side पर authN और object-level authZ करता है (IDOR: क्या user A, ID बदलकर user B का resource ले सकता है?); queries में tenant isolation; admin actions gated; default deny।
3. **Injection (A03)।** Raw string concatenation के बिना parameterised queries/ORM; user input के साथ shell नहीं; template auto-escaping बंद नहीं; NoSQL operator injection; header और log injection।
4. **Input & output handling।** Allow-list validation, size limits, file upload (type/size/storage location/execute permission), path traversal, XSS (output encoding, `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`/`v-html`), open redirects, cookie-authenticated state changes पर CSRF protection, CORS configuration।
5. **AuthN & sessions (A07)।** Slow algorithm से password hashing (bcrypt/scrypt/Argon2), OTP/MFA flows (OTP expiry, attempt limits, OTP brute force), token expiry और rotation, JWT algorithm pinning और signature verification, session fixation, rate limiting, secure cookie flags।
6. **Crypto & secrets (A02)।** Hard-coded keys/tokens नहीं; secrets manager या env से; TLS verification disabled नहीं; modern algorithms; CSPRNG से randomness; sensitive identifiers का storage और transit में encryption/masking।
7. **SSRF & deserialization (A10, A08)।** User-supplied URLs पर outbound requests सीमित (internal ranges/cloud metadata endpoints block); untrusted data का unsafe deserialization नहीं; payment gateway/webhook signature verification।
8. **Misconfiguration (A05)।** Debug modes, stack traces वाली verbose errors, default credentials, कमज़ोर security headers।
9. **Logging & privacy (A09) — भारतीय संदर्भ के checks:**
   - Security events (login failures, permission denials) log हों, पर passwords, OTPs, tokens, पूरे Aadhaar/card numbers या अनावश्यक personal data log न हों (masking)।
   - DPDP Act 2023: purpose limitation और data minimisation (जितना ज़रूरी उतना ही collect), consent withdrawal और erasure के code paths, बच्चों के data के लिए verifiable parental consent का flow, retention ख़त्म होने पर deletion।
   - DPDP Rules 2025 (13 Nov 2025 को notified, obligations चरणबद्ध रूप से लागू — commencement dates verify करें): reasonable security safeguards (encryption/masking, access control, access logs की monitoring और retention), और personal data breach की सूचना Data Protection Board व प्रभावित Data Principals को — विस्तृत report 72 घंटे के भीतर। क्या code breach detect करने और प्रभावित users पहचानने लायक audit data रखता है?
   - CERT-In Directions (28 अप्रैल 2022): निर्दिष्ट cyber incidents की report 6 घंटे के भीतर, ICT system logs 180 दिन तक भारत के भीतर सुरक्षित रखना, और system clocks का NTP sync (NIC/NPL servers या उनसे traceable)। Changed services के logs इन requirements के अनुरूप retention/location पर जाते हैं या नहीं — verify करें।
10. **Dependencies (A06)।** नए packages और versions; अनुमति हो तो ecosystem audit tool चलाएँ और असली output report करें।
11. **Findings rate करें** — exploitability × impact से severity, fix लिखें, और fix साबित करने वाला test सुझाएँ (जैसे "user B को user A के invoice पर 403 मिले")।

**Severity**: **Critical** (remote, unauthenticated, data exposure/RCE) · **High** (authenticated privilege escalation, sensitive data पर IDOR) · **Medium** (असामान्य conditions चाहिए, सीमित impact) · **Low** (defense-in-depth, hardening) · **Info**।

## Output format

```
## Scope और threat model
Reviewed entry points: ...  Out of scope: ...  Tools run: <name, command, exit code | none>

## Findings
### [High] GET /invoices/:id पर IDOR — OWASP A01
Location: `api/invoices.ts:31`
Scenario: authenticated user id बदलकर दूसरे tenant का invoice पढ़ लेता है।
Evidence: query सिर्फ़ id से filter करती है, tenant/owner check नहीं।
Fix: <code-level fix>
Test: <fix साबित करने वाला test>

## DPDP / CERT-In notes (personal data, logging, retention, breach readiness)
## Hardening suggestions (Low/Info)
## Verdict: कोई blocking issue नहीं | merge से पहले Critical/High fix करें
```

## Quality checks

- [ ] हर finding में ठोस location, plausible attack scenario, severity का कारण और fix है।
- [ ] हर नए endpoint के लिए सिर्फ़ authentication नहीं, object-level authorization भी check हुआ।
- [ ] किसी specific sink की ओर इशारा किए बिना "input validate करने पर विचार करें" जैसी generic बातें नहीं।
- [ ] जहाँ data flow पूरी तरह trace नहीं हो सका, false-positive की संभावना बताई।
- [ ] Personal data handling, logging, retention और breach readiness भारतीय संदर्भ में देखी गई।
- [ ] Scanner results असली runs से, command और exit code के साथ।

## सीमाएँ

- सिर्फ़ user के अपने code का defensive review; fix समझाने और test करने से ज़्यादा weaponised exploits नहीं।
- CVE IDs, advisory numbers या affected version ranges कभी न गढ़ें; सिर्फ़ tool output या user द्वारा दी गई advisory से quote करें, वरना "advisories check करें" लिखें।
- Code को कभी "secure" घोषित न करें — बताएँ क्या review हुआ और क्या नहीं। Static review runtime और configuration issues miss कर सकता है; high-risk releases के लिए penetration testing (जैसे CERT-In empanelled auditor से) सुझाएँ।
- DPDP Act/Rules और CERT-In से जुड़े points engineering checks हैं, legal advice नहीं; समय-सीमाएँ, commencement dates और दायित्व legal/privacy team और आधिकारिक notifications से verify करें।

skills.body:
# Data Room & Diligence Checklist

Creates a clean, stage-appropriate data room plan so diligence doesn't stall a round. The output is a folder index, a document-by-document status checklist, the gaps and clean-up items (often corporate housekeeping that takes weeks), and a sharing plan that separates what goes out before a term sheet from what is shared only after.

## When to use / when not to use

Use when:
- Preparing for a raise and wanting diligence-ready documents before the first lead meeting.
- An investor sent a diligence request list and you need to map it to what exists.
- Auditing corporate housekeeping (cap table, IP assignments, 83(b)s) ahead of a priced round.

Do not use when:
- Understanding the term sheet itself → `founder-term-sheet-explainer`.
- Answering partner-meeting questions → `founder-investor-qa-prep`.
- Building the financial model that goes in the room → `founder-operating-model`.
- Legal diligence opinions — counsel reviews substance; this skill tracks completeness.

## What to ask for first

1. Stage and instrument (SAFE round needs far less than a priced Series A).
2. Entity: Delaware C-corp? Date of incorporation; foreign subsidiaries; prior entity conversions.
3. Existing documents and where they live (drive, cap table tool, counsel's records).
4. Known issues: missing IP assignments, unsigned board consents, founders without 83(b) elections, contractors in other countries, open disputes.
5. Data room tool and who will administer access.
6. Any investor request list received (paste it).

## Steps

1. **Size the room to the stage.** Pre-seed/SAFE: deck, cap table, incorporation docs, key metrics, founder background. Priced seed/Series A: full index below.
2. **Build the index** using the standard folders:
   1. Corporate: certificate of incorporation (and amendments), bylaws, board and stockholder consents/minutes, good standing, foreign qualifications.
   2. Capitalization: fully diluted cap table, stock purchase agreements, 83(b) election copies with proof of timely filing, option plan and grants, board approvals, 409A reports, SAFEs/notes, side letters.
   3. Financial: historical P&L/balance sheet/cash flow (monthly), bank statements on request, operating model, budget vs. actual, AR/AP aging, debt and grants.
   4. Commercial: customer list with contract value and terms (anonymized pre-term-sheet), top customer contracts, pipeline, churn/retention data, pricing.
   5. Product & technology: architecture overview, roadmap, security practices and any SOC 2/ISO reports, open-source usage, uptime/incident history.
   6. IP: invention assignment / PIIA agreements for every founder, employee and contractor; patents and applications; trademarks; domain ownership.
   7. People: org chart, offer letters, contractor agreements, employee handbook, benefit plans, worker classification notes.
   8. Legal & compliance: material contracts, privacy policy and terms, data processing agreements, litigation/claims, licenses, export control or regulated-industry items.
   9. Tax: federal/state filings, sales-tax nexus analysis if applicable, R&D credit claims.
   10. Insurance: D&O, general liability, cyber (if any).
3. **Mark status per document:** Ready / Draft / Missing / Not applicable / Needs counsel. Assign an owner and due date.
4. **Flag red flags and fixes.** Common: founder IP not assigned to the company; missing or late 83(b)s; options granted without board approval or without a current 409A; cap table not matching signed documents; unsigned customer contracts; contractors abroad without IP assignment. Each gets a fix path and "counsel needed: yes/no".
5. **Set the sharing plan.** Tier 1 (pre-term-sheet): deck, metrics summary, high-level model. Tier 2 (post-term-sheet, under NDA if requested): contracts, cap table detail, employee data. Never share personal data (salaries tied to names, SSNs) beyond what is necessary; redact where possible.
6. **Map investor requests.** If a request list exists, map each item to a folder/document or a gap.
7. **Write an index README** that explains structure, naming convention (`02.3_Option-Plan_2024-03-01.pdf`), and a contact for questions.

## Output format

1. **Readiness summary**: % ready by folder, top 5 blockers with owners.
2. **Index & checklist table**

| # | Folder | Document | Status | Owner | Due | Share tier | Notes / red flag |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

3. **Red flags & fix plan** (issue → risk → fix → counsel needed → time estimate from founder/counsel).
4. **Investor request mapping** (if provided).
5. **Data room README** text.

## Quality checks

- [ ] Room scope fits the stage; no Series A burden for a pre-seed SAFE.
- [ ] Cap table, signed equity documents and board approvals are cross-checked for consistency.
- [ ] Every person who created IP has a signed assignment listed (or a gap flagged).
- [ ] Personal data minimized and sharing tiers defined.
- [ ] Every status is factual from the founder's inventory; nothing marked "Ready" by assumption.
- [ ] Naming convention and version dates consistent.

## Limits

- Not legal or tax advice. Fixes for equity, 83(b), 409A, IP and tax items must be handled by counsel/tax advisers; some (e.g., late 83(b)) may not be curable.
- This checklist tracks completeness; it does not judge legal sufficiency of any document.
- Don't fabricate documents, dates or filings; mark unknowns `[VERIFY]`.

skills.name: founder-data-room-checklist-ko
skills.description: 한국 스타트업의 투자 실사(DD)에 대비해 단계에 맞는 데이터룸 폴더 구조와 서류 체크리스트를 만들고, 서류별 준비 상태·담당자·보완 사항·공개 범위를 정리합니다. "데이터룸 만들어줘", "실사 자료 목록", "투자사가 요청한 DD 자료 정리", "투자 실사 준비" 등의 요청에 사용합니다.
skills.body:
# 데이터룸 및 실사 체크리스트 (한국)

실사 때문에 라운드가 지연되지 않도록 단계에 맞는 데이터룸 계획을 세웁니다. 결과물은 폴더 목록, 서류별 준비 상태표, 보완이 필요한 항목(주주명부·등기·지식재산 귀속처럼 몇 주가 걸리는 정리 작업 포함), 텀시트 전후 공개 범위 계획입니다.

## 사용 시점 / 사용하지 않는 경우

사용하는 경우:
- 리드 투자자 미팅 전에 실사 서류를 미리 갖추려 할 때
- 투자사(VC·액셀러레이터)가 실사 자료 요청 목록을 보냈을 때
- 우선주 라운드 전 주주명부·등기·정관·주식매수선택권 정리 상태를 점검할 때

사용하지 않는 경우:
- 텀시트 해설 → `founder-term-sheet-explainer-ko`
- 심사역 질문 대비 → `founder-investor-qa-prep-ko`
- 재무 모델 작성 → `founder-operating-model-ko`
- 법률 실사 의견 — 내용 판단은 변호사·회계사가, 이 스킬은 완비 여부를 관리합니다.

## 먼저 확인할 사항

1. 단계와 투자 방식(엔젤·조건부지분인수계약은 우선주 시리즈A보다 범위가 훨씬 작습니다)
2. 법인 정보: 설립일, 본점 소재지, 자회사·해외법인, 벤처기업 확인·기업부설연구소·이노비즈 등 인증 여부
3. 보유 서류와 위치(구글 드라이브, 세무대리인 보관, 법무사 보관)
4. 알려진 이슈: 창업자 개인 명의 특허·상표, 미작성 주주총회·이사회 의사록, 주식매수선택권 부여 절차 누락, 명의신탁 주식, 4대보험 미가입 인력, 진행 중인 분쟁
5. 정부지원금 수령 내역(협약 조건상 지분 변동·사업 전환 제한이 있는지)
6. 투자사가 보낸 요청 목록(붙여 넣기)

## 작성 절차

1. **단계별 범위 설정**: 엔젤·시드 초기에는 IR 자료, 주주명부, 법인 등기사항전부증명서, 정관, 핵심 지표, 재무제표 정도로 충분합니다. 우선주 라운드는 아래 전체 목록을 사용합니다.
2. **폴더 구성**
   1. 법인: 법인 등기사항전부증명서(최근 발급), 정관(변경 이력 포함), 주주총회·이사회 의사록, 사업자등록증, 법인 인감증명서는 필요 시에만
   2. 지분: 주주명부, 주식 변동 내역(주식등변동상황명세서), 기존 투자계약서·주주간계약서, 조건부지분인수계약·전환사채 계약, 주식매수선택권 부여 계약과 주총 결의, 창업자 간 주주 계약
   3. 재무·세무: 최근 3개년(또는 설립 이후) 재무제표와 세무조정계산서, 월별 손익, 부가가치세 신고서, 원천세 신고, 4대보험 완납증명, 국세·지방세 완납증명서, 차입금·보증 내역, 재무 모델, 예산 대비 실적
   4. 사업·영업: 고객 리스트(텀시트 전에는 익명화), 주요 계약서·발주서·견적서, 매출 집중도, 파이프라인, PoC 결과
   5. 기술·제품: 아키텍처 개요, 로드맵, 보안 체계(ISMS 등 인증 여부), 오픈소스 라이선스 사용 내역
   6. 지식재산: 특허·상표 출원·등록 현황과 권리자 명의, 직무발명 규정과 승계 기록, 외주 개발 계약의 산출물 귀속 조항
   7. 인사·노무: 조직도, 근로계약서, 취업규칙(상시 10명 이상이면 신고 의무 — 확인 필요), 4대보험 가입 현황, 퇴직급여 적립 방식, 프리랜서 계약

   9. 정부지원: 정부지원사업·R&D 협약서, 사업비 정산 상태, 지분 변동·폐업 시 제한 조건, 기술료 의무
   10. 보험: 임원배상책임, 영업배상, 사이버 보험(있는 경우)
3. **서류별 상태 표시**: 준비 완료 / 초안 / 미보유 / 해당 없음 / 전문가 검토 필요. 담당자와 기한을 지정합니다.
4. **문제 항목과 보완 방안**: 자주 나오는 이슈 — 창업자 개인 명의 특허·상표(법인 이전 필요), 직무발명 승계 미비, 주주명부와 등기·계약 불일치, 주식매수선택권 부여 시 정관 근거·주총 특별결의 누락, 명의신탁 주식, 체납, 정부과제 협약상 사전 승인 필요 사항. 각 항목에 보완 방법과 전문가(변호사·세무사·법무사·변리사) 필요 여부를 적습니다.

1. **준비도 요약**: 폴더별 준비율, 상위 5개 장애 요인과 담당자

|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

4. **투자사 요청 매핑** (해당 시)
5. **데이터룸 안내문**

# 데이터룸 및 실사 체크리스트 (한국)

실사 때문에 라운드가 지연되지 않도록 단계에 맞는 데이터룸 계획을 세웁니다. 결과물은 폴더 목록, 서류별 준비 상태표, 보완이 필요한 항목(주주명부·등기·지식재산 귀속처럼 몇 주가 걸리는 정리 작업 포함), 텀시트 전후 공개 범위 계획입니다.

## 사용 시점 / 사용하지 않는 경우

- 리드 투자자 미팅 전에 실사 서류를 미리 갖추려 할 때
- 투자사(VC·액셀러레이터)가 실사 자료 요청 목록을 보냈을 때

사용하지 않는 경우:
- 텀시트 해설 → `founder-term-sheet-explainer-ko`
- 심사역 질문 대비 → `founder-investor-qa-prep-ko`

# डेटा रूम और डिलिजेंस चेकलिस्ट (भारत)

यह स्किल स्टेज के अनुरूप साफ़-सुथरा डेटा रूम प्लान बनाती है ताकि डिलिजेंस से राउंड न रुके। आउटपुट: फ़ोल्डर इंडेक्स, दस्तावेज़-वार स्थिति, कमियाँ और सुधार (ROC फ़ाइलिंग, शेयर आवंटन रिकॉर्ड, IP असाइनमेंट जैसे काम जिनमें हफ़्ते लगते हैं), और टर्म शीट से पहले/बाद में क्या साझा करें इसकी योजना।

## कब उपयोग करें / कब नहीं

उपयोग करें:
- लीड निवेशक मीटिंग से पहले डिलिजेंस-तैयार दस्तावेज़ चाहिए।
- निवेशक ने डिलिजेंस अनुरोध सूची भेजी है और उसे मौजूदा दस्तावेज़ों से मिलाना है।
- प्राइस्ड CCPS राउंड से पहले कॉर्पोरेट हाउसकीपिंग (ROC, कैप टेबल, ESOP) की जाँच।

उपयोग न करें:
- टर्म शीट समझना → `founder-term-sheet-explainer-hi`
- पार्टनर मीटिंग प्रश्न → `founder-investor-qa-prep-hi`
- फ़ाइनेंशियल मॉडल → `founder-operating-model-hi`
- कानूनी राय — वकील/CA सामग्री की समीक्षा करते हैं; यह स्किल पूर्णता ट्रैक करती है।

## पहले क्या पूछें

1. स्टेज और इंस्ट्रूमेंट (एंजेल/iSAFE राउंड में प्राइस्ड सीरीज़ A से बहुत कम चाहिए)।
2. इकाई: प्राइवेट लिमिटेड? निगमन तिथि, CIN, विदेशी होल्डिंग/सब्सिडियरी (फ़्लिप संरचना), DPIIT मान्यता संख्या।
3. मौजूदा दस्तावेज़ कहाँ हैं (ड्राइव, CA/CS के पास, MCA पोर्टल)।
4. ज्ञात समस्याएँ: ROC फ़ाइलिंग में देरी, संस्थापक के नाम पर ट्रेडमार्क/डोमेन, बिना बोर्ड अनुमोदन के ESOP, विदेशी निवेश के बाद FC-GPR देर से, GST/TDS नोटिस, लंबित विवाद।
5. सरकारी अनुदान/इनक्यूबेटर सीड फंड (शर्तें जो शेयरहोल्डिंग बदलाव सीमित करें)।
6. निवेशक की अनुरोध सूची (पेस्ट करें)।

## चरण

1. **स्टेज के अनुसार दायरा।** एंजेल/प्री-सीड: डेक, कैप टेबल, MoA/AoA, निगमन प्रमाणपत्र, मुख्य मेट्रिक्स। प्राइस्ड राउंड: नीचे पूरी सूची।
2. **फ़ोल्डर इंडेक्स बनाएँ।**
   1. कॉर्पोरेट: निगमन प्रमाणपत्र, MoA, AoA (संशोधन सहित), बोर्ड/शेयरधारक प्रस्ताव और मिनट्स, वैधानिक रजिस्टर (सदस्य रजिस्टर आदि), ROC वार्षिक फ़ाइलिंग (AOC-4, MGT-7/7A), DPIIT मान्यता प्रमाणपत्र।
   2. कैपिटलाइज़ेशन: फ़ुली-डाइल्यूटेड कैप टेबल, शेयर आवंटन रिकॉर्ड (PAS-3), प्राइवेट प्लेसमेंट दस्तावेज़ (PAS-4/PAS-5 — [जाँचें]), मौजूदा SHA/SSA, iSAFE/CCD/नोट, ESOP योजना, शेयरधारक अनुमोदन और ग्रांट लेटर, डीमैट स्थिति (ISIN) — [जाँचें: निजी कंपनियों के लिए डीमैट आवश्यकता]।
   3. FEMA (विदेशी निवेश हो तो): FC-GPR/FC-TRS फ़ाइलिंग, FIRC/KYC, वैल्यूएशन रिपोर्ट, वार्षिक FLA रिटर्न।
   4. वित्त और कर: ऑडिटेड वित्तीय विवरण, मासिक MIS, बैंक स्टेटमेंट (अनुरोध पर), GST पंजीकरण और रिटर्न (GSTR-1/3B), TDS रिटर्न, आयकर रिटर्न, ऑपरेटिंग मॉडल, बजट बनाम वास्तविक।
   5. वाणिज्यिक: ग्राहक सूची (टर्म शीट से पहले गुमनाम), मुख्य अनुबंध/PO, पाइपलाइन, चर्न/रिटेंशन, प्राइसिंग।
   6. प्रोडक्ट और टेक: आर्किटेक्चर, रोडमैप, सुरक्षा प्रथाएँ, ओपन-सोर्स उपयोग।
   7. IP: संस्थापकों, कर्मचारियों और फ़्रीलांसरों से IP असाइनमेंट, ट्रेडमार्क/पेटेंट आवेदन और स्वामी का नाम, डोमेन स्वामित्व।
   8. लोग: संगठन चार्ट, नियुक्ति पत्र, कंसल्टेंट अनुबंध, PF/ESIC पंजीकरण और भुगतान, लागू श्रम/शॉप्स एंड एस्टैब्लिशमेंट पंजीकरण।
   9. कानूनी और अनुपालन: प्राइवेसी पॉलिसी, नियम व शर्तें, डिजिटल व्यक्तिगत डेटा संरक्षण (DPDP) अधिनियम तैयारी — [जाँचें: नियमों की प्रभावी तिथियाँ], लाइसेंस, मुक़दमे/नोटिस।
   10. अनुदान और बीमा: सरकारी/इनक्यूबेटर अनुदान अनुबंध और शर्तें, D&O/साइबर बीमा।
3. **हर दस्तावेज़ की स्थिति।** तैयार / ड्राफ़्ट / अनुपलब्ध / लागू नहीं / विशेषज्ञ आवश्यक। ज़िम्मेदार और तिथि।
4. **रेड फ़्लैग और सुधार।** आम: ट्रेडमार्क या डोमेन संस्थापक के व्यक्तिगत नाम पर; फ़्रीलांसर से IP असाइनमेंट नहीं; कैप टेबल और PAS-3/सदस्य रजिस्टर में अंतर; ESOP बिना शेयरधारक अनुमोदन; FC-GPR देर से (कंपाउंडिंग/लेट फ़ीस — [जाँचें]); ROC फ़ाइलिंग बकाया; GST/TDS डिफ़ॉल्ट। हर एक पर सुधार मार्ग और "CA/CS/वकील आवश्यक: हाँ/नहीं"।
5. **साझा करने के स्तर।** स्तर 1 (टर्म शीट से पहले): डेक, मेट्रिक सारांश, उच्च-स्तरीय मॉडल। स्तर 2 (टर्म शीट के बाद, NDA सहित): अनुबंध, विस्तृत कैप टेबल, कर्मचारी डेटा। PAN, आधार, नाम-वार वेतन जैसे व्यक्तिगत डेटा को न्यूनतम और मास्क करें।
6. **निवेशक अनुरोध मैपिंग।** हर आइटम को फ़ोल्डर/दस्तावेज़ या कमी से जोड़ें।
7. **README लिखें।** संरचना, नामकरण नियम (`02.3_ESOP-Plan_2024-03-01.pdf`), संपर्क व्यक्ति।

## आउटपुट फ़ॉर्मैट

1. **तैयारी सारांश:** फ़ोल्डर-वार % तैयार, शीर्ष 5 बाधाएँ और ज़िम्मेदार।
2. **इंडेक्स और चेकलिस्ट तालिका**

| # | फ़ोल्डर | दस्तावेज़ | स्थिति | ज़िम्मेदार | तिथि | साझा स्तर | टिप्पणी / रेड फ़्लैग |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

3. **रेड फ़्लैग सुधार योजना** (समस्या → जोखिम → सुधार → विशेषज्ञ आवश्यक → समय [विशेषज्ञ से पुष्टि])
4. **निवेशक अनुरोध मैपिंग** (यदि हो)
5. **डेटा रूम README**

## गुणवत्ता जाँच

- [ ] दायरा स्टेज के अनुरूप है।
- [ ] कैप टेबल, PAS-3, सदस्य रजिस्टर और SHA आपस में मेल खाते हैं।
- [ ] हर IP निर्माता का असाइनमेंट सूचीबद्ध है या कमी चिह्नित।
- [ ] विदेशी निवेश हो तो FEMA फ़ाइलिंग अलग से जाँची गई।
- [ ] व्यक्तिगत डेटा न्यूनतम; साझा स्तर तय।
- [ ] कोई दस्तावेज़ अनुमान से "तैयार" नहीं दिखाया गया।

## सीमाएँ

- यह कानूनी या कर सलाह नहीं है। कंपनी अधिनियम, FEMA, GST और श्रम अनुपालन के सुधार CA/CS/वकील करें; फ़ॉर्म नंबर और समय-सीमाएँ बदलती हैं — MCA/RBI पोर्टल से पुष्टि करें।
- यह सूची पूर्णता ट्रैक करती है, किसी दस्तावेज़ की कानूनी पर्याप्तता नहीं।
- दस्तावेज़, तिथियाँ या फ़ाइलिंग न गढ़ें; अज्ञात पर `[जाँचें]`।

   4. वित्त और कर: ऑडिटेड वित्तीय विवरण, मासिक MIS, बैंक स्टेटमेंट (अनुरोध पर), GST पंजीकरण और रिटर्न (GSTR-1/3B), TDS रिटर्न, आयकर रिटर्न, ऑपरेटिंग मॉडल, बजट बनाम वास्तविक।
   5. वाणिज्यिक: ग्राहक सूची (टर्म शीट से पहले गुमनाम), मुख्य अनुबंध/PO, पाइपलाइन, चर्न/रिटेंशन, प्राइसिंग।
   6. प्रोडक्ट और टेक: आर्किटेक्चर, रोडमैप, सुरक्षा प्रथाएँ, ओपन-सोर्स उपयोग।
   7. IP: संस्थापकों, कर्मचारियों और फ़्रीलांसरों से IP असाइनमेंट, ट्रेडमार्क/पेटेंट आवेदन और स्वामी का नाम, डोमेन स्वामित्व।
   8. लोग: संगठन चार्ट, नियुक्ति पत्र, कंसल्टेंट अनुबंध, PF/ESIC पंजीकरण और भुगतान, लागू श्रम/शॉप्स एंड एस्टैब्लिशमेंट पंजीकरण।
   9. कानूनी और अनुपालन: प्राइवेसी पॉलिसी, नियम व शर्तें, डिजिटल व्यक्तिगत डेटा संरक्षण (DPDP) अधिनियम तैयारी — [जाँचें: नियमों की प्रभावी तिथियाँ], लाइसेंस, मुक़दमे/नोटिस।
   10. अनुदान और बीमा: सरकारी/इनक्यूबेटर अनुदान अनुबंध और शर्तें, D&O/साइबर बीमा।
3. **हर दस्तावेज़ की स्थिति।** तैयार / ड्राफ़्ट / अनुपलब्ध / लागू नहीं / विशेषज्ञ आवश्यक। ज़िम्मेदार और तिथि।
4. **रेड फ़्लैग और सुधार।** आम: ट्रेडमार्क या डोमेन संस्थापक के व्यक्तिगत नाम पर; फ़्रीलांसर से IP असाइनमेंट नहीं; कैप टेबल और PAS-3/सदस्य रजिस्टर में अंतर; ESOP बिना शेयरधारक अनुमोदन; FC-GPR देर से (कंपाउंडिंग/लेट फ़ीस — [जाँचें]); ROC फ़ाइलिंग बकाया; GST/TDS डिफ़ॉल्ट। हर एक पर सुधार मार्ग और "CA/CS/वकील आवश्यक: हाँ/नहीं"।
5. **साझा करने के स्तर।** स्तर 1 (टर्म शीट से पहले): डेक, मेट्रिक सारांश, उच्च-स्तरीय मॉडल। स्तर 2 (टर्म शीट के बाद, NDA सहित): अनुबंध, विस्तृत कैप टेबल, कर्मचारी डेटा। PAN, आधार, नाम-वार वेतन जैसे व्यक्तिगत डेटा को न्यूनतम और मास्क करें।
6. **निवेशक अनुरोध मैपिंग।** हर आइटम को फ़ोल्डर/दस्तावेज़ या कमी से जोड़ें।
7. **README लिखें।** संरचना, नामकरण नियम (`02.3_ESOP-Plan_2024-03-01.pdf`), संपर्क व्यक्ति।

## आउटपुट फ़ॉर्मैट

1. **तैयारी सारांश:** फ़ोल्डर-वार % तैयार, शीर्ष 5 बाधाएँ और ज़िम्मेदार।
2. **इंडेक्स और चेकलिस्ट तालिका**

| # | फ़ोल्डर | दस्तावेज़ | स्थिति | ज़िम्मेदार | तिथि | साझा स्तर | टिप्पणी / रेड फ़्लैग |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

3. **रेड फ़्लैग सुधार योजना** (समस्या → जोखिम → सुधार → विशेषज्ञ आवश्यक → समय [विशेषज्ञ से पुष्टि])
4. **निवेशक अनुरोध मैपिंग** (यदि हो)
5. **डेटा रूम README**

## गुणवत्ता जाँच

- [ ] दायरा स्टेज के अनुरूप है।
- [ ] कैप टेबल, PAS-3, सदस्य रजिस्टर और SHA आपस में मेल खाते हैं।
- [ ] हर IP निर्माता का असाइनमेंट सूचीबद्ध है या कमी चिह्नित।
- [ ] विदेशी निवेश हो तो FEMA फ़ाइलिंग अलग से जाँची गई।
- [ ] व्यक्तिगत डेटा न्यूनतम; साझा स्तर तय।
- [ ] कोई दस्तावेज़ अनुमान से "तैयार" नहीं दिखाया गया।

## सीमाएँ

- यह कानूनी या कर सलाह नहीं है। कंपनी अधिनियम, FEMA, GST और श्रम अनुपालन के सुधार CA/CS/वकील करें; फ़ॉर्म नंबर और समय-सीमाएँ बदलती हैं — MCA/RBI पोर्टल से पुष्टि करें।
- यह सूची पूर्णता ट्रैक करती है, किसी दस्तावेज़ की कानूनी पर्याप्तता नहीं।
- दस्तावेज़, तिथियाँ या फ़ाइलिंग न गढ़ें; अज्ञात पर `[जाँचें]`।
