skills.body:
# Churn और Win/Loss Analysis

बिखरे हुए churn और deal-outcome data को drivers की ranked list में बदलता है जिन पर product team काम कर सके। Self-reported कारणों को सावधानी से लेता है ("बहुत महँगा" का मतलब अक्सर "value कम मिली" होता है), जो product ठीक कर सकता है उसे pricing, sales, onboarding या support की ज़िम्मेदारी से अलग करता है, और हर finding को source records तक traceable रखता है।

## कब उपयोग करें / कब नहीं

उपयोग करें जब:
- Churn, downgrade या uninstall बढ़ा है और leadership वजह पूछ रही है।
- Sales हार का कारण सिर्फ़ "features की कमी" बताता है।
- Cancellation-survey responses, exit interviews या CRM loss reasons का synthesis करना है।

उपयोग न करें जब:
- सामान्य feedback summary → `product-voice-of-customer-report-hi`
- एक खास request की demand → `product-feature-request-demand-sizing-hi`
- Churn metric की गणना या cohort curves → `product-activation-retention-cohorts-hi`; यह skill कारण समझाता है।

## पहले क्या पूछें

1. Scope: churn, downgrade, trial/free-to-paid न होना, uninstall/लंबी inactivity, lost deals, won deals (wins भी — वे बताते हैं क्या मायने रखता है)।
2. Data: cancellation reasons और comments, exit interview notes, CRM win/loss fields, call centre/WhatsApp history, churn से पहले का usage — IDs और तारीख़ों के साथ।
3. अवधि और records की संख्या (सभी records या sample)।
4. Segment fields: plan, size, tenure, शहर tier/राज्य, भाषा, acquisition channel (जैसे cashback campaign), बताया गया competitor।
5. अवधि में ज्ञात बदलाव: price बदलाव, launches, outages, OTP/payment failures, sales team बदलाव।
6. Findings पर कौन काम करेगा (product, pricing, CS, sales)।

## चरण

1. **Inventory और bias check।** Source, size, response rate लिखें। Biases: optional surveys, sales द्वारा भरे loss reasons, interview self-selection; जो users बिना कुछ कहे uninstall कर देते हैं वे surveys में नहीं दिखते।
2. **बताए गए कारण code करें** एक तय list से: price, missing capability, usability/complexity (भाषा की बाधा सहित), reliability (OTP न आना, payment failure), onboarding/time-to-value, support, competitor, business change (budget, बंद हुआ), champion चला गया, offer/cashback ख़त्म होना, other।
3. **Root causes खोजें।** बताए गए कारण को comments, usage history (कभी activate नहीं हुआ? X के बाद usage गिरा?) और support history के साथ मिलाएँ। बताया गया और अनुमानित root cause दोनों लिखें; inference का confidence चिह्नित करें।
4. **Controllable बनाम uncontrollable** churn अलग करें (business बंद बनाम poor fit बनाम product gap; केवल cashback के लिए आए users अलग)।
5. **Drivers का आकार** accounts और, अगर दिया गया हो, revenue से; segment और tenure के हिसाब से। छोटे samples को percentages नहीं, counts में बताएँ।
6. **Wins बनाम losses** की तुलना (deals scope में हों तो): कौन-सी capabilities/factors wins में हैं पर losses में नहीं; competitor patterns।
7. **Owners और actions से जोड़ें।** हर top driver के लिए product action (feature, fix, onboarding बदलाव, vernacular support) या दूसरा owner (pricing, sales qualification, CS)। At-risk accounts जल्दी पकड़ने के leading indicators भी।
8. **आगे की research सुझाएँ** जहाँ evidence पतला है (जैसे किसी segment में सिर्फ़ 5 exit calls)।

## आउटपुट फ़ॉर्मेट

```
# Churn / win-loss analysis: [scope, अवधि]   [तारीख़]
## Summary (3–5 bullets)
## Sources और caveats
| Source | Records | Coverage / response rate | Bias |

## Drivers
| Driver | Stated count | Root-cause count (conf.) | Accounts | Revenue (अगर दिया) | Segments | Controllable? |
### Driver 1: [नाम]
Evidence: [record IDs, छोटे verbatims]  Usage/support pattern: ...
Owner और प्रस्तावित action: ...  Early-warning signal: ...

## Wins बनाम losses
## Uncontrollable churn
## Actions और owners   ## Research gaps
```

## गुणवत्ता जाँच

- बताए गए और root-cause कारण दोनों दिखते हैं; inferences पर confidence लिखा है।
- Counts की unit तय है (accounts बनाम users बनाम revenue); छोटे samples percentages में नहीं।
- हर top driver का owner और action है — सब कुछ product पर नहीं डाला।
- Deal data हो तो wins शामिल हैं।
- Verbatims हूबहू, anonymised और sourced हैं।

## सीमाएँ

- Churn rates, revenue, कारण या quotes कभी न गढ़ें; सिर्फ़ वही बताएँ जो data में है।
- Usage data में correlation cause साबित नहीं करता; यह साफ़ लिखें।
- Customer और revenue data internal access नियमों और DPDP Act के अनुसार संभालें।
- Strategy, pricing और staffing के जवाब उनके owners तय करते हैं।

skills.description: Sizes the real demand behind a feature request: consolidates mentions across channels into unique accounts, uncovers the underlying job behind the ask, segments requesters by value and fit, checks usage data for the related workflow, estimates reach and revenue at stake with explicit ranges and assumptions, and recommends whether to build, test or decline. Use when a PM asks "how many customers want this", "size this request", "is this request worth building", "sales keeps asking for X", or "demand for feature Y".
skills.body:
# Feature Request Demand Sizing

Answers "how much does this request actually matter?" with evidence instead of volume or volume-of-voice. It separates raw mentions from unique customers, distinguishes the requested solution from the underlying need, weights requesters by segment, and produces a range — not a falsely precise number — that can feed prioritisation.

## When to use / when not to use

Use when:
- Sales, CS or a large customer pushes a specific feature.
- A request recurs in support or reviews and you need to know if it is widespread.
- You need a Reach or revenue input for `product-prioritization-scoring`.

Do not use when:
- You need to tag a whole feedback stream — use `product-feedback-triage-tagging`.
- You need to explore many opportunities for an outcome — use `product-opportunity-solution-tree`.
- The question is why customers left — use `product-churn-win-loss-analysis`.

## What to ask for first

1. The request in the requester's words, plus any internal description.
2. All mentions you can export: tickets, CRM notes, lost-deal reasons, reviews, community posts — with account IDs and dates.
3. Account data: plan, revenue band, segment, renewal date (if allowed to use).
4. Usage data for the related workflow (how many users reach that point; workarounds seen).
5. Total addressable base for the segment (active accounts/users).
6. Any commitments already made to customers.

## Steps

1. **Define the request precisely** and list near-duplicates that express the same need differently.
2. **Uncover the job.** From verbatims, write the underlying need ("needs to share results with people outside the tool") and note alternative solutions that could meet it. Requests for the same job count together; requests for different jobs do not.
3. **Consolidate mentions** into unique accounts/users; dedupe repeated asks from the same customer; note who asked (end user, admin, buyer, internal sales).
4. **Segment requesters**: plan/tier, ICP fit, revenue band, region, and whether they are active, at risk, prospective, or churned.
5. **Triangulate with behaviour.** Check usage of the related workflow, workaround signals (exports, manual steps, third-party tools) and drop-off points. Note where data is unavailable.
6. **Estimate reach and value as ranges.** Low/likely/high, e.g., observed requesters → extrapolated share of segment using stated assumptions (silent-majority ratio, channel coverage). Revenue at stake only from real account data; label everything else `[ESTIMATE]`.
7. **Assess fit**: strategy alignment, cost-to-serve, whether it serves ideal customers or pulls toward a niche.
8. **Recommend**: build, run a cheap test (fake door, prototype, concierge), offer a workaround, or decline — and what evidence would change the call.
9. **Close the loop** with a draft response for requesters.

## Output format

```
# Demand sizing: [request]   [date]
Underlying job: ...   Alternatives that meet it: ...

## Evidence
| Source | Mentions | Unique accounts | Period |
## Requesters by segment
| Segment | Accounts | Status (active/at-risk/prospect/churned) | Revenue band (if given) |
## Behaviour signals
## Estimate (ranges)
| Measure | Low | Likely | High | Assumptions |
## Fit & risks
## Recommendation & what would change it
## Draft reply to requesters
```

## Quality checks

- Unique accounts and raw mentions are reported separately.
- The underlying job is stated; requests are grouped by job, not wording.
- Every extrapolation shows its assumption; ranges, not single numbers.
- Revenue figures come from provided data only.
- Internal requesters (sales) are distinguished from customers.
- Recommendation includes a falsifiable next step.

## Limits

- Never invent request counts, account names, revenue or usage numbers; mark gaps `[DATA NEEDED]`.
- Feedback channels miss silent users; extrapolation is a labelled estimate, not a measurement.
- Do not promise delivery to customers; commitments are made by the product owner.
- Using account revenue data must follow internal data-access rules.

# 기능 요청 수요 산정

"이 요청이 실제로 얼마나 중요한가?"에 목소리 크기가 아닌 근거로 답합니다. 단순 언급 수와 고유 고객 수를 분리하고, 요청된 해결책과 그 뒤의 니즈를 구분하며, 요청 고객을 세그먼트별로 가중하고, 우선순위 결정에 넣을 수 있는 범위 값을 만듭니다. 근거 없이 정밀해 보이는 숫자는 만들지 않습니다.

## 사용 시점 / 사용하지 않는 경우

사용하는 경우:
- 영업, CS, 대형 고객사가 특정 기능을 강하게 요구할 때
- CS 문의나 앱 리뷰에 같은 요청이 반복되어 얼마나 퍼져 있는지 알아야 할 때
- `product-prioritization-scoring-ko`에 넣을 Reach·매출 값이 필요할 때

사용하지 않는 경우:
- 피드백 전체 태깅 → `product-feedback-triage-tagging-ko`
- 하나의 성과를 위한 여러 기회 탐색 → `product-opportunity-solution-tree-ko`
- 고객 이탈 원인 → `product-churn-win-loss-analysis-ko`

## 먼저 확인할 사항

1. 요청자의 원래 표현과 내부 설명
2. 추출 가능한 모든 언급: CS 티켓, 카카오톡 상담, CRM 메모, 실주 사유, 앱 리뷰, 커뮤니티 글 — 계정 ID와 날짜 포함
3. 계정 정보: 요금제, 매출 구간, 세그먼트, 갱신일(사용 가능한 경우)
4. 관련 업무 흐름의 사용 데이터(해당 지점 도달 사용자 수, 우회 방법 흔적)
5. 세그먼트의 전체 모수(활성 계정·사용자)
6. 이미 고객에게 한 약속

## 작성 절차

1. **요청을 정확히 정의**하고, 같은 니즈를 다르게 표현한 유사 요청을 나열합니다.
2. **진짜 과업을 찾습니다.** 원문에서 근본 니즈("도구 밖의 사람에게 결과를 공유해야 함")를 쓰고, 이를 충족할 대안 해결책을 적습니다. 같은 과업의 요청은 합산하고, 다른 과업은 합치지 않습니다.
3. **언급을 고유 고객으로 통합합니다.** 같은 고객의 반복 요청을 중복 제거하고, 요청 주체(실사용자, 관리자, 구매 결정권자, 사내 영업)를 표시합니다.
4. **요청 고객을 나눕니다.** 요금제, 목표 고객(ICP) 적합도, 매출 구간, 지역, 상태(활성, 이탈 위험, 잠재, 이탈)
5. **행동 데이터와 교차 확인합니다.** 관련 기능 사용량, 우회 흔적(엑셀 다운로드, 수작업, 외부 도구), 이탈 지점을 봅니다. 데이터가 없으면 없다고 적습니다.
6. **도달과 가치를 범위로 추정합니다.** 하한/유력/상한. 관측된 요청 고객에서 세그먼트 비율로 확장할 때는 가정(침묵하는 다수 비율, 채널 커버리지)을 명시합니다. 걸린 매출은 실제 계정 데이터로만 계산하고, 나머지는 `[추정]`으로 표시합니다.
7. **적합도를 봅니다.** 전략 정합성, 운영 비용, 핵심 고객을 위한 것인지 틈새로 끌려가는 것인지
8. **권고합니다.** 개발, 저비용 검증(페이크 도어, 프로토타입, 컨시어지), 우회 방법 안내, 거절 중 하나와 판단을 바꿀 근거
9. **요청자 답변 초안**을 작성합니다.

## 출력 형식

```
# 수요 산정: [요청]   [날짜]
근본 과업: ...   이를 충족할 대안: ...

## 근거
| 출처 | 언급 수 | 고유 계정 수 | 기간 |
## 세그먼트별 요청 고객
| 세그먼트 | 계정 수 | 상태(활성/위험/잠재/이탈) | 매출 구간(제공 시) |
## 행동 신호
## 추정(범위)
| 항목 | 하한 | 유력 | 상한 | 가정 |
## 적합도·리스크
## 권고와 판단을 바꿀 조건
## 요청자 답변 초안
```

## 품질 점검

- 고유 계정 수와 단순 언급 수를 따로 보고합니다.
- 근본 과업이 명시되어 있고, 문구가 아닌 과업 기준으로 묶었습니다.
- 모든 확장 추정에 가정이 있고, 단일 값이 아닌 범위입니다.
- 매출 수치는 제공된 데이터에서만 나왔습니다.
- 사내 요청자(영업)와 고객을 구분했습니다.
- 권고에 반증 가능한 다음 단계가 있습니다.

## 한계

- 요청 건수, 고객사명, 매출, 사용량을 지어내지 않습니다. 빈칸은 `[데이터 필요]`로 둡니다.
- 피드백 채널은 말하지 않는 사용자를 놓치므로, 확장 값은 측정이 아닌 표시된 추정입니다.
- 고객에게 개발을 약속하지 않습니다. 약속은 제품 책임자가 합니다.
- 계정 매출 데이터 사용은 사내 데이터 접근 규칙과 개인정보 보호 기준을 따릅니다.

skills.description: किसी feature request के पीछे की असली demand आँकता है: channels में फैले mentions को unique accounts में जोड़ता है, request के पीछे का असली job खोजता है, requesters को value और fit से segment करता है, संबंधित workflow का usage data देखता है, reach और revenue at stake को साफ़ ranges और assumptions के साथ estimate करता है, और build, test या decline की सिफ़ारिश करता है। जब PM पूछे "कितने customers यह चाहते हैं", "इस request को size करो", "क्या यह बनाने लायक है", "sales बार-बार X माँग रहा है", या "feature Y की demand", तब उपयोग करें।
skills.body:
# Feature Request Demand Sizing

"यह request असल में कितनी मायने रखती है?" का जवाब आवाज़ की ऊँचाई नहीं, evidence से देता है। Raw mentions को unique customers से अलग करता है, माँगे गए solution को underlying need से अलग करता है, requesters को segment के हिसाब से तौलता है, और prioritisation में डालने लायक एक range देता है — झूठी सटीकता वाला एक नंबर नहीं।

## कब उपयोग करें / कब नहीं

उपयोग करें जब:
- Sales, field team, CS या कोई बड़ा customer/partner किसी खास feature पर ज़ोर दे।
- Call centre, WhatsApp support या Play Store reviews में एक request बार-बार आए और जानना हो कि यह कितनी फैली है।
- `product-prioritization-scoring-hi` के लिए Reach या revenue input चाहिए।

उपयोग न करें जब:
- पूरी feedback stream tag करनी है → `product-feedback-triage-tagging-hi`
- एक outcome के लिए कई opportunities खोजनी हैं → `product-opportunity-solution-tree-hi`
- Customers क्यों छोड़ गए → `product-churn-win-loss-analysis-hi`

## पहले क्या पूछें

1. Requester के शब्दों में request, और internal विवरण।
2. Export हो सकने वाले सभी mentions: tickets, WhatsApp chats, call centre logs, CRM notes, lost-deal reasons, reviews, community posts — account IDs और तारीख़ों के साथ।
3. Account data: plan, revenue band, segment, शहर tier/राज्य, renewal तारीख़ (अगर इस्तेमाल की अनुमति हो)।
4. संबंधित workflow का usage data (कितने users उस बिंदु तक पहुँचते हैं; workarounds के संकेत)।
5. Segment का कुल आधार (active accounts/users)।
6. Customers से पहले किए गए वादे।

## चरण

1. **Request को ठीक से परिभाषित करें** और ऐसे near-duplicates लिखें जो वही need अलग शब्दों में कहते हैं (Hindi, English, Hinglish रूप भी)।

```
Underlying job: ...   इसे पूरा करने वाले विकल्प: ...

| Source | Mentions | Unique accounts | अवधि |
## Segment-wise requesters
| Segment | Accounts | Status (active/at-risk/prospect/churned) | Revenue band (अगर दिया) |
## Behaviour signals
## Estimate (ranges)
| Measure | Low | Likely | High | Assumptions |
## Fit और risks
## Recommendation और क्या इसे बदलेगा
```

skills.body:
# Feedback Triage & Tagging

Gives a product team an operational way to handle the steady inflow of feedback — support tickets, app reviews, sales notes, in-app widgets, community posts — so that each item is tagged consistently, deduplicated, routed to an owner and counted. This is ongoing intake for product decisions, not a one-off research synthesis (for that, use `feedback-affinity-synthesis`).

## When to use / when not to use

Use when:
- Feedback arrives from many channels and nobody knows what is in it.
- Tags are inconsistent between people, so counts are meaningless.
- You need a weekly or sprint-level triage routine and summary.

Do not use when:
- You are synthesising a research study's interviews — use `feedback-affinity-synthesis` or `product-interview-to-opportunities`.
- You need a periodic narrative for leadership — use `product-voice-of-customer-report` on the tagged data.
- You need to estimate demand for one specific request — use `product-feature-request-demand-sizing`.

## What to ask for first

1. Channels and rough volumes per week (support, reviews, sales/CS notes, NPS comments, social, community).
2. Sample batch of raw items (anonymised) with IDs and dates.
3. Product areas/teams and their owners, so routing has destinations.
4. Existing tags or taxonomy, if any, and the tool used (helpdesk, spreadsheet, feedback tool).
5. Segments that matter: plan/tier, customer size, region, platform, new vs. tenured.
6. Escalation rules already in place (security, legal, outages).

## Steps

1. **Design a small, stable taxonomy** (or audit the existing one):
   - Product area (one per item, matching owners).
   - Type: bug, feature request, UX friction, performance, pricing/billing, praise, churn signal, question/how-to.
   - Severity for bugs/friction: blocking, major, minor.
   - Segment and channel as metadata, not tags.
   Keep each list short with definitions and examples; add an "other — review" bucket.
2. **Define escalation fast lanes**: security/privacy reports, data loss, legal threats, outages, safety — route immediately, outside the weekly cycle.
3. **Tag the batch.** One area, one type per item; keep the original text and ID. Where unsure, mark `low confidence` instead of forcing a tag.
4. **Deduplicate into canonical issues.** Link each item to a canonical issue/request ("Export to CSV from reports"), counting unique customers/accounts separately from raw mentions.
5. **Route.** Assign each canonical issue to an owner with the action: fix (bug), consider (request), investigate (friction), reply (customer awaiting answer).
6. **Close the loop.** Track which customers asked so they can be told when something ships or is declined.
7. **Write the triage summary**: volume by type/area, new canonical issues, top movers vs. last period, escalations, untagged/"other" items to refine the taxonomy.
8. **Calibrate.** Periodically have two people tag the same sample and compare; refine definitions where they disagree.

## Output format

```
# Feedback triage: [period]   Sources: [...]   Items: [n given]
## Taxonomy (version x)
| Tag | Definition | Example |

## Tagged items
| ID | Channel | Date | Segment | Area | Type | Severity | Canonical issue | Confidence |

## Canonical issues
| Issue | Area | Type | Mentions | Unique accounts | Owner | Action | Status |

## Escalations sent
## Summary: volume by type & area, new issues, movers, notes for taxonomy
```

## Quality checks

- Each item has exactly one area and one type; ambiguous ones are flagged, not guessed.
- Mentions and unique customers are counted separately.
- Every canonical issue has an owner and an action.
- Escalation categories bypass the weekly cycle.
- Original text and source IDs are preserved for traceability.
- Personal data is removed or masked before items are shared beyond the support tool.

## Limits

- Counts only reflect the data provided; channel volume is not the same as customer prevalence (vocal users are over-represented).
- Never fabricate items, quotes or counts; if a batch is a sample, say so.
- Tagging supports decisions; prioritisation and responses are decided by owners.

# 피드백 분류·태깅

플레이스토어·앱스토어 리뷰, CS 티켓, 카카오톡 채널 상담, 영업·사업 메모, 인앱 피드백, 커뮤니티 글처럼 꾸준히 들어오는 피드백을 일관되게 태그하고, 중복을 묶고, 담당자에게 배정하고, 집계할 수 있는 운영 방식을 제공합니다. 제품 의사결정을 위한 상시 수집 체계이며, 일회성 리서치 종합은 `feedback-affinity-synthesis-ko`를 사용합니다.

## 사용 시점 / 사용하지 않는 경우

- 주간·스프린트 단위 분류 루틴과 요약이 필요할 때

- 경영진용 정기 리포트 → 태깅된 데이터로 `product-voice-of-customer-report-ko`
- 특정 요청 하나의 수요 산정 → `product-feature-request-demand-sizing-ko`

2. 비식별 처리된 원자료 샘플(ID, 날짜 포함)

skills.body:
# Feedback Triage और Tagging

Product team को लगातार आने वाले feedback को संभालने का operational तरीका देता है, ताकि हर item एक जैसे tag हो, duplicates जुड़ें, owner तक पहुँचे और गिना जा सके। यह product फ़ैसलों के लिए ongoing intake है, एक बार का research synthesis नहीं (उसके लिए `feedback-affinity-synthesis-hi`)।

## कब उपयोग करें / कब नहीं

उपयोग करें जब:
- कई channels से feedback आता है और किसी को नहीं पता उसमें क्या है।
- अलग-अलग लोग अलग tags लगाते हैं, इसलिए counts का कोई मतलब नहीं।
- Weekly या sprint-level triage routine और summary चाहिए।

उपयोग न करें जब:
- Research interviews का synthesis → `feedback-affinity-synthesis-hi` या `product-interview-to-opportunities-hi`
- Leadership के लिए periodic narrative → tagged data पर `product-voice-of-customer-report-hi`
- किसी एक request की demand आँकनी → `product-feature-request-demand-sizing-hi`

## पहले क्या पूछें

1. Channels और हफ़्ते का अनुमानित volume (call centre, WhatsApp support, Play Store/App Store, field/sales notes, NPS comments, social, community)।
2. Raw items का anonymised sample, IDs और तारीख़ों के साथ।
3. Product areas/teams और उनके owners, ताकि routing की मंज़िल हो।
4. मौजूदा tags/taxonomy और tool (helpdesk, spreadsheet, feedback tool)।
5. ज़रूरी segments: plan/tier, शहर tier (metro/tier-2/tier-3), राज्य, भाषा, device/OS, नया या पुराना user।
6. पहले से escalation नियम (security, fraud, legal, outages)।

## चरण

1. **छोटी, स्थिर taxonomy बनाएँ** (या मौजूदा की जाँच करें):
   - Product area (हर item में एक, owners से मेल खाता)।
   - Type: bug, feature request, UX friction, performance (slow/data usage), payments/refund, OTP/login, language/translation issue, praise, churn signal, सवाल/how-to।
   - Severity (bugs/friction): blocking, major, minor।
   - Segment, भाषा और channel metadata हैं, tags नहीं।
   हर list छोटी, definitions और उदाहरणों के साथ; "other — review" bucket रखें।
2. **Escalation fast lanes तय करें:** security/privacy report, fraud या unauthorised debit की शिकायत, पैसा कटा पर service नहीं मिली, data loss, legal threat, outage — weekly cycle का इंतज़ार किए बिना तुरंत route।
3. **Batch tag करें।** हर item में एक area, एक type; original text (मूल भाषा में) और ID रखें। Hinglish/vernacular text का अर्थ English में साथ लिखें, पर मूल न बदलें। अनिश्चित हो तो ज़बरदस्ती tag करने के बजाय `low confidence` लिखें।
4. **Canonical issues में deduplicate करें।** हर item को एक canonical issue ("UPI payment pending दिखता है पर पैसा कट गया") से जोड़ें; unique customers को raw mentions से अलग गिनें।
5. **Route करें।** हर canonical issue का owner और action: fix (bug), consider (request), investigate (friction), reply (customer जवाब का इंतज़ार कर रहा है)।
6. **Loop बंद करें।** किस customer ने माँगा, यह track करें ताकि ship या decline होने पर (उनकी भाषा में, WhatsApp/SMS से) बताया जा सके।
7. **Triage summary लिखें:** type/area-wise volume, नए canonical issues, पिछली अवधि से top movers, escalations, untagged/"other" items।
8. **Calibrate करें।** समय-समय पर दो लोग एक ही sample tag करें और तुलना करें; जहाँ मतभेद हो वहाँ definitions सुधारें।

## आउटपुट फ़ॉर्मेट

```
# Feedback triage: [अवधि]   Sources: [...]   Items: [दिए गए n]
## Taxonomy (version x)
| Tag | Definition | उदाहरण |

## Tagged items
| ID | Channel | तारीख़ | Segment | भाषा | Area | Type | Severity | Canonical issue | Confidence |

## Canonical issues
| Issue | Area | Type | Mentions | Unique customers | Owner | Action | Status |

## भेजे गए escalations
## Summary: type और area-wise volume, नए issues, movers, taxonomy notes
```

## गुणवत्ता जाँच

- हर item में ठीक एक area और एक type; अस्पष्ट items flag किए गए, अंदाज़े से नहीं भरे।
- Mentions और unique customers अलग गिने गए।
- हर canonical issue का owner और action है।
- Escalation categories weekly cycle को bypass करती हैं।
- Original text (मूल भाषा) और source IDs traceability के लिए सुरक्षित हैं।

# Feedback Triage और Tagging

Product team को लगातार आने वाले feedback को संभालने का operational तरीका देता है, ताकि हर item एक जैसे tag हो, duplicates जुड़ें, owner तक पहुँचे और गिना जा सके। यह product फ़ैसलों के लिए ongoing intake है, एक बार का research synthesis नहीं (उसके लिए `feedback-affinity-synthesis-hi`)।

## कब उपयोग करें / कब नहीं

उपयोग करें जब:
- कई channels से feedback आता है और किसी को नहीं पता उसमें क्या है।
- अलग-अलग लोग अलग tags लगाते हैं, इसलिए counts का कोई मतलब नहीं।
- Weekly या sprint-level triage routine और summary चाहिए।

उपयोग न करें जब:
- Research interviews का synthesis → `feedback-affinity-synthesis-hi` या `product-interview-to-opportunities-hi`
- Leadership के लिए periodic narrative → tagged data पर `product-voice-of-customer-report-hi`
- किसी एक request की demand आँकनी → `product-feature-request-demand-sizing-hi`

## पहले क्या पूछें

1. Channels और हफ़्ते का अनुमानित volume (call centre, WhatsApp support, Play Store/App Store, field/sales notes, NPS comments, social, community)।
2. Raw items का anonymised sample, IDs और तारीख़ों के साथ।
3. Product areas/teams और उनके owners, ताकि routing की मंज़िल हो।
4. मौजूदा tags/taxonomy और tool (helpdesk, spreadsheet, feedback tool)।
5. ज़रूरी segments: plan/tier, शहर tier (metro/tier-2/tier-3), राज्य, भाषा, device/OS, नया या पुराना user।
6. पहले से escalation नियम (security, fraud, legal, outages)।

## चरण

1. **छोटी, स्थिर taxonomy बनाएँ** (या मौजूदा की जाँच करें):
   - Product area (हर item में एक, owners से मेल खाता)।
   - Type: bug, feature request, UX friction, performance (slow/data usage), payments/refund, OTP/login, language/translation issue, praise, churn signal, सवाल/how-to।
   - Severity (bugs/friction): blocking, major, minor।
   - Segment, भाषा और channel metadata हैं, tags नहीं।
   हर list छोटी, definitions और उदाहरणों के साथ; "other — review" bucket रखें।
2. **Escalation fast lanes तय करें:** security/privacy report, fraud या unauthorised debit की शिकायत, पैसा कटा पर service नहीं मिली, data loss, legal threat, outage — weekly cycle का इंतज़ार किए बिना तुरंत route।
3. **Batch tag करें।** हर item में एक area, एक type; original text (मूल भाषा में) और ID रखें। Hinglish/vernacular text का अर्थ English में साथ लिखें, पर मूल न बदलें। अनिश्चित हो तो ज़बरदस्ती tag करने के बजाय `low confidence` लिखें।
4. **Canonical issues में deduplicate करें।** हर item को एक canonical issue ("UPI payment pending दिखता है पर पैसा कट गया") से जोड़ें; unique customers को raw mentions से अलग गिनें।
5. **Route करें।** हर canonical issue का owner और action: fix (bug), consider (request), investigate (friction), reply (customer जवाब का इंतज़ार कर रहा है)।
6. **Loop बंद करें।** किस customer ने माँगा, यह track करें ताकि ship या decline होने पर (उनकी भाषा में, WhatsApp/SMS से) बताया जा सके।
7. **Triage summary लिखें:** type/area-wise volume, नए canonical issues, पिछली अवधि से top movers, escalations, untagged/"other" items।
8. **Calibrate करें।** समय-समय पर दो लोग एक ही sample tag करें और तुलना करें; जहाँ मतभेद हो वहाँ definitions सुधारें।

## आउटपुट फ़ॉर्मेट

```
# Feedback triage: [अवधि]   Sources: [...]   Items: [दिए गए n]
## Taxonomy (version x)
| Tag | Definition | उदाहरण |

## Tagged items
| ID | Channel | तारीख़ | Segment | भाषा | Area | Type | Severity | Canonical issue | Confidence |

## Canonical issues
| Issue | Area | Type | Mentions | Unique customers | Owner | Action | Status |

## भेजे गए escalations
## Summary: type और area-wise volume, नए issues, movers, taxonomy notes
```

## गुणवत्ता जाँच

- हर item में ठीक एक area और एक type; अस्पष्ट items flag किए गए, अंदाज़े से नहीं भरे।
- Mentions और unique customers अलग गिने गए।
- हर canonical issue का owner और action है।
- Escalation categories weekly cycle को bypass करती हैं।
- Original text (मूल भाषा) और source IDs traceability के लिए सुरक्षित हैं।
- Support tool से बाहर share करने से पहले नाम, mobile number, UPI ID, account/order number हटाए या mask किए गए (DPDP Act के purpose limitation का ध्यान)।

## सीमाएँ

- Counts सिर्फ़ दिए गए data को दर्शाते हैं; channel volume सभी customers में प्रसार नहीं है (मुखर users ज़्यादा दिखते हैं; जो users लिखते नहीं, वे call centre पर ही मिलते हैं)।
- Items, quotes या counts कभी न गढ़ें; batch sample है तो बताएँ।
- Tagging फ़ैसलों में मदद करता है; prioritisation और जवाब owners तय करते हैं।

skills.name: product-interview-to-opportunities
skills.description: Turns customer interview notes or transcripts into a PM-ready opportunity backlog: extracts needs, pains and desires as opportunity statements, links each to verbatim evidence and participants, rates evidence strength, connects opportunities to the team's outcome, and lists which assumptions to test next. Use when a PM says "what did we learn from these interviews", "turn interview notes into opportunities", "interview snapshot", "discovery debrief", or "feed these interviews into the roadmap".
skills.body:
# Interview Notes to Opportunities

Converts a batch of discovery interviews into decisions-ready material: one-page snapshots per interview, a deduplicated list of opportunity statements tied to evidence, and a view of which opportunities matter most for the team's outcome. It is framed for product decisions — feeding an opportunity solution tree or roadmap — rather than for full research reporting.

## When to use / when not to use

Use when:
- The team just ran a handful (often 3–12) of discovery interviews and must decide what to do next.
- Interview notes sit in docs nobody reads.
- You want to update an opportunity solution tree with new evidence.

Do not use when:
- You need to plan or script the interviews — use `user-interview-guide`.
- You have a large mixed dataset and need full thematic research synthesis — use `feedback-affinity-synthesis`.
- You need personas or JTBD profiles — use `persona-jtbd-builder`.

## What to ask for first

1. Notes or transcripts, with participant IDs, date, segment and interviewer.
2. The team's target outcome or research question.
3. Existing opportunity list or tree to update (if any).
4. Segment definitions and any screening data.
5. Whether quotes may be shared beyond the team (consent scope).

## Steps

1. **Snapshot each interview** (one per participant): who, context, key story they told, notable quotes (exact), pains, needs, desires, current workarounds, surprises.
2. **Extract opportunity statements** from the customer's point of view ("I need to know my report is correct before my manager sees it"). Avoid solutions in the statement; if the participant asked for a feature, capture the feature and infer the need behind it, marked as inference.
3. **Distinguish evidence types**: past behaviour told as a specific story (strongest), stated preference, hypothetical ("I would use…", weakest).
4. **Deduplicate and structure** opportunities into parent/child, merging same-need statements across participants.
5. **Rate evidence strength** per opportunity: number of participants, segments, evidence type, any supporting data. One participant = signal, not pattern.
6. **Connect to the outcome**: how directly each opportunity could move the target metric.
7. **Flag contradictions** (segments wanting opposite things) and surprises that challenge current beliefs or the roadmap.
8. **Propose next steps**: opportunities to explore, assumptions to test, gaps in who was interviewed (e.g., no churned users), and suggested updates to the tree via `product-opportunity-solution-tree`.

## Output format

```
# Discovery debrief: [topic]   Interviews: [n given], [dates]   Outcome: [...]
## Interview snapshots
### P01 — [segment], [date]
Story: ...  Quotes: "..."  Pains: ...  Needs: ...  Workarounds: ...  Surprises: ...

## Opportunities
| # | Opportunity (customer voice) | Parent | Participants | Evidence type | Strength | Link to outcome |

## Contradictions & surprises
## What this changes for our plan / beliefs
## Next steps: explore / test / recruit gaps
```

Opportunity statement examples:
```
Weak (solution):   "Add a Slack integration."
Weak (vague):      "Users want better collaboration."
Strong (need):     "I don't know whether my approver has seen the request, so I chase them by chat." [P02, P05 — told as recent stories]
Inferred (marked): P07 asked for "bulk edit" → inferred need: "fixing the same mistake across many records takes my whole afternoon" [INFERENCE]
```

## Quality checks

- Opportunities are needs, not features; inferred needs are marked.
- Every opportunity lists participant IDs; quotes are exact and attributable.
- Strength reflects participant count and evidence type; single-source items aren't called patterns.
- Interview coverage gaps are explicit.
- At least one finding challenges or confirms a current assumption — stated plainly.

## Limits

- Never invent quotes, participants or counts; paraphrase outside quotation marks only.
- Small qualitative samples show what exists, not how common it is; size with data before major bets.
- Respect the consent scope for quotes and recordings; remove identifying details.
- What to pursue is the product team's decision.

skills.description: 고객 인터뷰 메모·녹취록을 PM이 바로 쓸 수 있는 기회 백로그로 바꿉니다. 니즈·불편·욕구를 기회 문장으로 뽑고, 원문 근거와 참여자를 연결하며, 근거 강도를 평가하고, 팀 성과와의 연결과 다음에 검증할 가정을 정리합니다. "인터뷰에서 뭘 배웠지", "인터뷰 메모를 기회로", "인터뷰 스냅샷", "디스커버리 회고", "인터뷰 결과를 로드맵에 반영" 같은 요청에 사용합니다.
skills.body:
# 인터뷰 메모를 기회로

디스커버리 인터뷰 묶음을 의사결정용 자료로 바꿉니다. 인터뷰별 한 장 스냅샷, 근거가 연결된 중복 없는 기회 목록, 팀 성과에 어떤 기회가 가장 중요한지를 정리합니다. 전체 리서치 보고서가 아니라 기회-해결책 트리나 로드맵에 넣기 위한 제품 의사결정용입니다.

## 사용 시점 / 사용하지 않는 경우

사용하는 경우:
- 팀이 디스커버리 인터뷰를 몇 건(보통 3~12건) 마쳤고 다음 행동을 정해야 할 때
- 인터뷰 메모가 아무도 안 읽는 문서에 묻혀 있을 때
- 기회-해결책 트리를 새 근거로 갱신하고 싶을 때

사용하지 않는 경우:
- 인터뷰 계획·질문지 작성 → `user-interview-guide-ko`
- 대규모 혼합 자료의 본격 리서치 종합 → `feedback-affinity-synthesis-ko`
- 페르소나·JTBD → `persona-jtbd-builder-ko`

## 먼저 확인할 사항

1. 메모·녹취록과 참여자 ID, 날짜, 세그먼트, 인터뷰어
2. 팀의 목표 성과 또는 조사 질문
3. 갱신할 기존 기회 목록·트리
4. 세그먼트 정의와 스크리닝 정보
5. 원문 인용을 팀 밖에 공유해도 되는지(동의 범위)

## 작성 절차

1. **인터뷰별 스냅샷을 만듭니다.** 누구인지, 맥락, 들려준 핵심 경험담, 주목할 원문 인용(정확히), 불편, 니즈, 욕구, 현재 우회 방법, 놀라운 점
2. **기회 문장을 뽑습니다.** 고객 관점으로 씁니다("팀장님이 보기 전에 보고서 숫자가 맞는지 확인하고 싶어요"). 해결책을 문장에 넣지 않습니다. 참여자가 기능을 요청했다면 그 기능을 기록하고 뒤의 니즈를 추론하되 추론임을 표시합니다.
3. **근거 유형을 구분합니다.** 구체적 과거 경험(가장 강함), 선호 진술, 가정형("있으면 쓸 것 같아요", 가장 약함)
4. **중복을 합치고 구조화합니다.** 참여자 간 같은 니즈를 합치고 상위/하위 기회로 묶습니다.
5. **기회별 근거 강도를 평가합니다.** 참여자 수, 세그먼트, 근거 유형, 뒷받침 데이터. 한 명은 신호이지 패턴이 아닙니다.
6. **성과와 연결합니다.** 각 기회가 목표 지표를 얼마나 직접 움직일 수 있는지
7. **상충과 의외의 발견을 표시합니다.** 세그먼트 간 반대되는 요구, 현재 믿음이나 로드맵에 도전하는 발견
8. **다음 단계를 제안합니다.** 탐색할 기회, 검증할 가정, 인터뷰 대상 공백(예: 이탈 고객 없음), `product-opportunity-solution-tree-ko`에 반영할 갱신 사항

## 출력 형식

```
# 디스커버리 회고: [주제]   인터뷰: [제공 건수], [날짜]   성과: [...]
## 인터뷰 스냅샷
### P01 — [세그먼트], [날짜]
경험담: ...  인용: "..."  불편: ...  니즈: ...  우회 방법: ...  놀라운 점: ...

## 기회
| # | 기회(고객 관점) | 상위 기회 | 참여자 | 근거 유형 | 강도 | 성과 연결 |

## 상충·의외의 발견
## 우리 계획·믿음에 주는 변화
## 다음 단계: 탐색 / 검증 / 모집 공백
```

기회 문장 예시:
```
약함(해결책):  "슬랙 연동 추가"
약함(모호함):  "사용자는 더 나은 협업을 원함"
강함(니즈):    "결재자가 요청을 봤는지 몰라서 메신저로 계속 확인해요." [P02, P05 — 최근 경험담]
추론(표시):    P07이 "일괄 수정"을 요청 → 추론된 니즈: "같은 실수를 여러 건 고치느라 오후가 다 가요" [추론]
```

# 인터뷰 메모를 기회로

디스커버리 인터뷰 묶음을 의사결정용 자료로 바꿉니다. 인터뷰별 한 장 스냅샷, 근거가 연결된 중복 없는 기회 목록, 팀 성과에 어떤 기회가 가장 중요한지를 정리합니다. 전체 리서치 보고서가 아니라 기회-해결책 트리나 로드맵에 넣기 위한 제품 의사결정용입니다.

## 사용 시점 / 사용하지 않는 경우

사용하는 경우:
- 팀이 디스커버리 인터뷰를 몇 건(보통 3~12건) 마쳤고 다음 행동을 정해야 할 때
- 인터뷰 메모가 아무도 안 읽는 문서에 묻혀 있을 때
- 기회-해결책 트리를 새 근거로 갱신하고 싶을 때

사용하지 않는 경우:
- 인터뷰 계획·질문지 작성 → `user-interview-guide-ko`
- 대규모 혼합 자료의 본격 리서치 종합 → `feedback-affinity-synthesis-ko`
- 페르소나·JTBD → `persona-jtbd-builder-ko`

## 먼저 확인할 사항

1. 메모·녹취록과 참여자 ID, 날짜, 세그먼트, 인터뷰어
2. 팀의 목표 성과 또는 조사 질문
3. 갱신할 기존 기회 목록·트리
4. 세그먼트 정의와 스크리닝 정보
5. 원문 인용을 팀 밖에 공유해도 되는지(동의 범위)

## 작성 절차

1. **인터뷰별 스냅샷을 만듭니다.** 누구인지, 맥락, 들려준 핵심 경험담, 주목할 원문 인용(정확히), 불편, 니즈, 욕구, 현재 우회 방법, 놀라운 점
2. **기회 문장을 뽑습니다.** 고객 관점으로 씁니다("팀장님이 보기 전에 보고서 숫자가 맞는지 확인하고 싶어요"). 해결책을 문장에 넣지 않습니다. 참여자가 기능을 요청했다면 그 기능을 기록하고 뒤의 니즈를 추론하되 추론임을 표시합니다.
3. **근거 유형을 구분합니다.** 구체적 과거 경험(가장 강함), 선호 진술, 가정형("있으면 쓸 것 같아요", 가장 약함)
4. **중복을 합치고 구조화합니다.** 참여자 간 같은 니즈를 합치고 상위/하위 기회로 묶습니다.
5. **기회별 근거 강도를 평가합니다.** 참여자 수, 세그먼트, 근거 유형, 뒷받침 데이터. 한 명은 신호이지 패턴이 아닙니다.
6. **성과와 연결합니다.** 각 기회가 목표 지표를 얼마나 직접 움직일 수 있는지
7. **상충과 의외의 발견을 표시합니다.** 세그먼트 간 반대되는 요구, 현재 믿음이나 로드맵에 도전하는 발견
8. **다음 단계를 제안합니다.** 탐색할 기회, 검증할 가정, 인터뷰 대상 공백(예: 이탈 고객 없음), `product-opportunity-solution-tree-ko`에 반영할 갱신 사항

## 출력 형식

```
# 디스커버리 회고: [주제]   인터뷰: [제공 건수], [날짜]   성과: [...]
## 인터뷰 스냅샷
### P01 — [세그먼트], [날짜]
경험담: ...  인용: "..."  불편: ...  니즈: ...  우회 방법: ...  놀라운 점: ...

## 기회
| # | 기회(고객 관점) | 상위 기회 | 참여자 | 근거 유형 | 강도 | 성과 연결 |

## 상충·의외의 발견
## 우리 계획·믿음에 주는 변화
## 다음 단계: 탐색 / 검증 / 모집 공백
```

기회 문장 예시:
```
약함(해결책):  "슬랙 연동 추가"
약함(모호함):  "사용자는 더 나은 협업을 원함"

추론(표시):    P07이 "일괄 수정"을 요청 → 추론된 니즈: "같은 실수를 여러 건 고치느라 오후가 다 가요" [추론]
```

- 모든 기회에 참여자 ID가 있고, 인용은 정확하며 출처를 알 수 있습니다.

- 현재 가정을 뒤집거나 확인하는 발견이 최소 하나 분명히 적혀 있습니다.

## 한계

- 인용, 참여자, 건수를 지어내지 않습니다. 따옴표 밖에서만 요약합니다.
- 작은 정성 표본은 무엇이 존재하는지 보여줄 뿐 얼마나 흔한지는 아닙니다. 큰 투자 전에는 데이터로 규모를 확인합니다.
- 인용·녹음의 동의 범위를 지키고, 개인을 알아볼 수 있는 정보는 제거합니다.
- 무엇을 추진할지는 제품팀이 결정합니다.

skills.body:
# Interview Notes से Opportunities

Discovery interviews के एक batch को फ़ैसलों के लायक सामग्री में बदलता है: हर interview का एक-पेज snapshot, evidence से जुड़ी deduplicated opportunity statements की list, और यह कि team के outcome के लिए कौन-सी opportunities सबसे ज़्यादा मायने रखती हैं। यह product फ़ैसलों के लिए है — opportunity solution tree या roadmap में डालने के लिए — पूरी research reporting के लिए नहीं।

## कब उपयोग करें / कब नहीं

उपयोग करें जब:
- Team ने अभी कुछ (अक्सर 3–12) discovery interviews किए हैं — field visits, phone calls, kirana/retailer visits — और आगे क्या करना है तय करना है।
- Interview notes ऐसे docs में पड़े हैं जिन्हें कोई नहीं पढ़ता।
- Opportunity solution tree को नए evidence से update करना है।

उपयोग न करें जब:
- Interviews plan या script करने हैं → `user-interview-guide-hi`
- बड़े mixed dataset का पूरा thematic research synthesis → `feedback-affinity-synthesis-hi`
- Personas या JTBD → `persona-jtbd-builder-hi`

## पहले क्या पूछें

1. Notes या transcripts, participant IDs, तारीख़, segment और interviewer के साथ।
2. Team का target outcome या research question।
3. Update करने के लिए मौजूदा opportunity list या tree।
4. Segment definitions (शहर tier, भाषा, पहली बार online payment करने वाले आदि) और screening data।
5. Quotes को team से बाहर share करने की अनुमति (consent का दायरा)।

## चरण

1. **हर interview का snapshot** (हर participant के लिए एक): कौन, संदर्भ, सुनाई गई मुख्य कहानी, ख़ास quotes (हूबहू, मूल भाषा में; ज़रूरत हो तो साथ में अर्थ), pains, needs, desires, मौजूदा workarounds (जैसे "बेटे से करवाता हूँ", "दुकान वाले से पूछ लेते हैं"), चौंकाने वाली बातें।
2. **Opportunity statements निकालें** customer की नज़र से ("मुझे पक्का होना चाहिए कि पैसा सही आदमी को गया, तभी चैन मिलता है")। Statement में solution न डालें; अगर participant ने feature माँगा, तो उसे दर्ज करें और पीछे की need का अनुमान लगाएँ — अनुमान के रूप में चिह्नित।
3. **Evidence types अलग करें:** खास कहानी के रूप में बताया गया past behaviour (सबसे मज़बूत), stated preference, hypothetical ("होता तो use करता", सबसे कमज़ोर)। ध्यान रखें कि कुछ participants interviewer को खुश करने के लिए "हाँ" कह देते हैं — व्यवहार की कहानी को ज़्यादा वज़न दें।
4. **Deduplicate और structure करें** — participants में एक जैसी need वाले statements मिलाएँ, parent/child में बाँटें।
5. **हर opportunity की evidence strength आँकें:** participants की संख्या, segments, evidence type, supporting data। एक participant = signal, pattern नहीं।
6. **Outcome से जोड़ें:** हर opportunity target metric को कितना सीधे हिला सकती है।
7. **विरोधाभास और चौंकाने वाली बातें** flag करें (segments की उलटी ज़रूरतें; मौजूदा मान्यताओं या roadmap को चुनौती देने वाले findings)।
8. **अगले कदम सुझाएँ:** explore करने लायक opportunities, test करने लायक assumptions, किससे बात नहीं हुई (जैसे churned users, महिलाएँ, किसी राज्य के users), और `product-opportunity-solution-tree-hi` में किए जाने वाले updates।

## आउटपुट फ़ॉर्मेट

```
# Discovery debrief: [विषय]   Interviews: [दिए गए n], [तारीख़ें]   Outcome: [...]
## Interview snapshots
### P01 — [segment], [तारीख़]
कहानी: ...  Quotes: "..."  Pains: ...  Needs: ...  Workarounds: ...  चौंकाने वाली बातें: ...

## Opportunities
| # | Opportunity (customer की आवाज़) | Parent | Participants | Evidence type | Strength | Outcome से संबंध |

## विरोधाभास और चौंकाने वाली बातें
## इससे हमारे plan / मान्यताओं में क्या बदलता है
## अगले कदम: explore / test / recruit gaps
```

Opportunity statement के उदाहरण:
```
कमज़ोर (solution):  "Voice search जोड़ो।"
कमज़ोर (धुंधला):    "Users को बेहतर experience चाहिए।"
मज़बूत (need):      "Product का नाम English में type नहीं कर पाता, इसलिए दुकान वाले को फ़ोन करके पूछता हूँ।" [P02, P05 — हाल की कहानियाँ]
अनुमानित (चिह्नित): P07 ने "Hindi app" माँगा → अनुमानित need: "Refund की शर्तें समझ नहीं आतीं तो डर लगता है कि पैसा फँस जाएगा" [INFERENCE]
```

## गुणवत्ता जाँच

- Opportunities needs हैं, features नहीं; अनुमानित needs चिह्नित हैं।
- हर opportunity में participant IDs हैं; quotes हूबहू और attributable हैं।
- Strength participant count और evidence type दर्शाती है; single-source को pattern नहीं कहा।
- Interview coverage के gaps स्पष्ट हैं।
- कम से कम एक finding साफ़ तौर पर किसी मौजूदा assumption को चुनौती देता या पुष्टि करता है।

## सीमाएँ

- Quotes, participants या counts कभी न गढ़ें; quote marks के बाहर ही paraphrase करें।
- छोटे qualitative samples बताते हैं कि क्या मौजूद है, यह नहीं कि कितना आम है; बड़े bets से पहले data से size करें।
- Quotes और recordings के consent दायरे का सम्मान करें (DPDP Act); पहचान वाली जानकारी हटाएँ।
- किस पर आगे बढ़ना है, यह product team तय करती है।

4. Segment definitions (शहर tier, भाषा, पहली बार online payment करने वाले आदि) और screening data।
5. Quotes को team से बाहर share करने की अनुमति (consent का दायरा)।

## चरण

1. **हर interview का snapshot** (हर participant के लिए एक): कौन, संदर्भ, सुनाई गई मुख्य कहानी, ख़ास quotes (हूबहू, मूल भाषा में; ज़रूरत हो तो साथ में अर्थ), pains, needs, desires, मौजूदा workarounds (जैसे "बेटे से करवाता हूँ", "दुकान वाले से पूछ लेते हैं"), चौंकाने वाली बातें।
2. **Opportunity statements निकालें** customer की नज़र से ("मुझे पक्का होना चाहिए कि पैसा सही आदमी को गया, तभी चैन मिलता है")। Statement में solution न डालें; अगर participant ने feature माँगा, तो उसे दर्ज करें और पीछे की need का अनुमान लगाएँ — अनुमान के रूप में चिह्नित।
3. **Evidence types अलग करें:** खास कहानी के रूप में बताया गया past behaviour (सबसे मज़बूत), stated preference, hypothetical ("होता तो use करता", सबसे कमज़ोर)। ध्यान रखें कि कुछ participants interviewer को खुश करने के लिए "हाँ" कह देते हैं — व्यवहार की कहानी को ज़्यादा वज़न दें।
4. **Deduplicate और structure करें** — participants में एक जैसी need वाले statements मिलाएँ, parent/child में बाँटें।
5. **हर opportunity की evidence strength आँकें:** participants की संख्या, segments, evidence type, supporting data। एक participant = signal, pattern नहीं।
6. **Outcome से जोड़ें:** हर opportunity target metric को कितना सीधे हिला सकती है।
7. **विरोधाभास और चौंकाने वाली बातें** flag करें (segments की उलटी ज़रूरतें; मौजूदा मान्यताओं या roadmap को चुनौती देने वाले findings)।
8. **अगले कदम सुझाएँ:** explore करने लायक opportunities, test करने लायक assumptions, किससे बात नहीं हुई (जैसे churned users, महिलाएँ, किसी राज्य के users), और `product-opportunity-solution-tree-hi` में किए जाने वाले updates।

## आउटपुट फ़ॉर्मेट

```
# Discovery debrief: [विषय]   Interviews: [दिए गए n], [तारीख़ें]   Outcome: [...]
## Interview snapshots
### P01 — [segment], [तारीख़]
कहानी: ...  Quotes: "..."  Pains: ...  Needs: ...  Workarounds: ...  चौंकाने वाली बातें: ...

## Opportunities
| # | Opportunity (customer की आवाज़) | Parent | Participants | Evidence type | Strength | Outcome से संबंध |

## विरोधाभास और चौंकाने वाली बातें
## इससे हमारे plan / मान्यताओं में क्या बदलता है
## अगले कदम: explore / test / recruit gaps
```

Opportunity statement के उदाहरण:
```
कमज़ोर (solution):  "Voice search जोड़ो।"
कमज़ोर (धुंधला):    "Users को बेहतर experience चाहिए।"
मज़बूत (need):      "Product का नाम English में type नहीं कर पाता, इसलिए दुकान वाले को फ़ोन करके पूछता हूँ।" [P02, P05 — हाल की कहानियाँ]
अनुमानित (चिह्नित): P07 ने "Hindi app" माँगा → अनुमानित need: "Refund की शर्तें समझ नहीं आतीं तो डर लगता है कि पैसा फँस जाएगा" [INFERENCE]
```

## गुणवत्ता जाँच

- Opportunities needs हैं, features नहीं; अनुमानित needs चिह्नित हैं।
- हर opportunity में participant IDs हैं; quotes हूबहू और attributable हैं।
- Strength participant count और evidence type दर्शाती है; single-source को pattern नहीं कहा।
- Interview coverage के gaps स्पष्ट हैं।
- कम से कम एक finding साफ़ तौर पर किसी मौजूदा assumption को चुनौती देता या पुष्टि करता है।

## सीमाएँ

- Quotes, participants या counts कभी न गढ़ें; quote marks के बाहर ही paraphrase करें।
- छोटे qualitative samples बताते हैं कि क्या मौजूद है, यह नहीं कि कितना आम है; बड़े bets से पहले data से size करें।
- Quotes और recordings के consent दायरे का सम्मान करें (DPDP Act); पहचान वाली जानकारी हटाएँ।
- किस पर आगे बढ़ना है, यह product team तय करती है।

skills.body:
# Voice of Customer Report

Produces a concise, decision-oriented report that tells leadership what customers are experiencing, what has changed, and what the product team proposes to do. It combines quantitative signal (volumes, scores) with qualitative evidence (verbatims) while being explicit about sample sources and biases.

## When to use / when not to use

Use when:
- A monthly or quarterly feedback readout is due.
- Leadership asks "what are customers telling us?".
- You need to connect feedback themes to roadmap decisions.

Do not use when:
- Raw feedback isn't tagged yet — run `product-feedback-triage-tagging` first.
- You're synthesising one research study — use `feedback-affinity-synthesis`.
- You need to explain lost or churned customers specifically — use `product-churn-win-loss-analysis`.

## What to ask for first

1. Period covered and comparison period.
2. Data: tagged feedback export, support volumes by category, NPS/CSAT scores and comments, review ratings, research findings — each with source.
3. Audience and decisions they own.
4. Current goals/OKRs so themes can be linked to them.
5. Actions already in progress on known themes.
6. Segments to break out (plan, region, platform, customer size).

## Steps

1. **Inventory sources** with counts, period and known bias (e.g., "support tickets skew to admins"; "app reviews skew to unhappy users").
2. **Rank themes** by a stated combination of reach (unique customers), severity, trend and strategic relevance. State the rule used.
3. **Evidence each theme**: count of mentions and unique customers, segments affected, 1–3 short verbatims with source IDs (quoted exactly, anonymised), and supporting metric if available.
4. **Show change.** New, growing, shrinking, resolved themes vs. the prior period; note if a change might be caused by volume shifts or channel changes rather than customer experience.
5. **Link to goals** — which themes threaten or support which OKR.
6. **State the response** per theme: in roadmap (link), under investigation, deliberately not addressing (and why), needs decision.
7. **Highlight praise** briefly — what to protect.
8. **List decisions or asks** of leadership.
9. **Write an executive summary** last: 3–5 bullets.

## Output format

```
# Voice of Customer — [period]   Prepared by [PM], [date]
## Executive summary (3–5 bullets)
## Sources & caveats
| Source | Items | Period | Known bias |

## Top themes
| # | Theme | Unique customers | Mentions | Segments | Trend | Linked goal | Response |
### Theme 1: [name]
What we hear: ...  Evidence: "[verbatim]" (T-1043), ...  Metric: ...  Response: ...

## Changes since last period: new / growing / resolved
## What customers value (protect)
## Decisions requested
## Appendix: method, taxonomy version
```

## Quality checks

- Every theme has counts with a defined unit and at least one sourced verbatim.
- Verbatims are exact, short, anonymised and traceable; none are composite or paraphrased inside quotes.
- Biases and source limits are stated up front.
- Each theme has a response status — the report is not just a list of complaints.
- Trend claims compare like with like.
- Executive summary fits on one screen.

## Limits

- Never invent verbatims, scores, counts or trends; if data is missing, say so.
- Feedback volume indicates what is being said, not how common a problem is across all users; pair with usage data where possible.
- Personal data must be removed before distribution.
- Responses and priorities are decided by the product team and leadership.

skills.body:
# VOC(고객의 소리) 리포트

고객이 무엇을 겪고 있는지, 무엇이 달라졌는지, 제품팀이 어떻게 대응할지를 경영진에게 간결하게 전달하는 의사결정 중심 리포트를 만듭니다. 정량 신호(건수, 점수)와 정성 근거(원문)를 함께 보여주되, 표본 출처와 편향을 분명히 밝힙니다.

## 사용 시점 / 사용하지 않는 경우

사용하는 경우:
- 월간·분기 VOC 보고가 필요할 때
- 경영진이 "고객들이 뭐라고 하나요?"라고 물을 때
- 피드백 테마를 로드맵 결정과 연결해야 할 때

사용하지 않는 경우:
- 원자료가 아직 태깅되지 않음 → 먼저 `product-feedback-triage-tagging-ko`
- 단일 리서치 종합 → `feedback-affinity-synthesis-ko`
- 이탈·해지 고객 원인 분석 → `product-churn-win-loss-analysis-ko`

## 먼저 확인할 사항

1. 대상 기간과 비교 기간
2. 데이터: 태깅된 피드백, 유형별 CS 건수, 카카오톡 상담 기록, 앱 리뷰 평점·내용, NPS·CSAT 점수와 코멘트, 리서치 결과 — 각 출처
3. 보고 대상과 그들이 가진 결정 권한
4. 테마와 연결할 현재 목표·OKR
5. 이미 진행 중인 대응
6. 나눠 볼 세그먼트(요금제, 지역, OS, 고객 규모)

## 작성 절차

1. **출처를 정리합니다.** 건수, 기간, 알려진 편향을 적습니다(예: "CS 문의는 관리자 계정 비중이 높음", "앱 리뷰는 불만 사용자 비중이 높음", "카카오톡 상담은 결제·배송 문의 위주").
2. **테마 순위를 매깁니다.** 도달(고유 고객 수), 심각도, 추세, 전략 관련성을 어떤 규칙으로 조합했는지 밝힙니다.
3. **테마마다 근거를 붙입니다.** 언급 수와 고유 고객 수, 영향 세그먼트, 출처 ID가 달린 짧은 원문 1~3개(정확히 인용, 비식별), 가능하면 관련 지표
4. **변화를 보여줍니다.** 신규·증가·감소·해결 테마. 고객 경험 변화가 아니라 문의량이나 채널 변화 때문일 수 있으면 그렇게 적습니다.
5. **목표와 연결합니다.** 어떤 테마가 어떤 OKR을 위협하거나 돕는지
6. **대응 상태를 적습니다.** 로드맵 반영(링크), 조사 중, 의도적으로 대응 안 함(이유), 결정 필요
7. **칭찬도 짧게** 정리합니다. 지켜야 할 것을 알려줍니다.
8. **경영진에게 요청할 결정**을 나열합니다.
9. **요약은 마지막에** 3~5줄로 씁니다.

## 출력 형식

```
# VOC 리포트 — [기간]   작성 [PM], [날짜]
## 요약(3~5줄)
## 출처와 유의사항
| 출처 | 건수 | 기간 | 알려진 편향 |

## 주요 테마
| # | 테마 | 고유 고객 수 | 언급 수 | 세그먼트 | 추세 | 연결 목표 | 대응 |
### 테마 1: [이름]
고객 이야기: ...  근거: "[원문]" (CS-1043), ...  지표: ...  대응: ...

## 전 기간 대비 변화: 신규 / 증가 / 해결
## 고객이 좋아하는 점(유지할 것)
## 요청 의사결정
## 부록: 방법, 분류 체계 버전
```

## 품질 점검

- 모든 테마에 단위가 정의된 건수와 출처가 있는 원문이 하나 이상 있습니다.
- 원문은 정확하고 짧으며 비식별 처리되어 추적 가능합니다. 따옴표 안에 합성하거나 바꿔 쓴 문장이 없습니다.
- 편향과 출처 한계를 앞부분에 밝혔습니다.
- 테마마다 대응 상태가 있어 불만 목록으로 끝나지 않습니다.
- 추세 비교가 같은 기준끼리 이뤄졌습니다.
- 요약이 한 화면 안에 들어갑니다.

## 한계

- 원문, 점수, 건수, 추세를 지어내지 않습니다. 데이터가 없으면 없다고 씁니다.
- 피드백 양은 무엇이 이야기되는지를 보여줄 뿐, 전체 사용자 중 문제가 얼마나 흔한지는 아닙니다. 가능하면 사용 데이터와 함께 봅니다.
- 배포 전 이름, 연락처, 주문번호 등 개인정보를 제거합니다.
- 대응과 우선순위는 제품팀과 경영진이 결정합니다.

사용하는 경우:
- 월간·분기 VOC 보고가 필요할 때
- 경영진이 "고객들이 뭐라고 하나요?"라고 물을 때
- 피드백 테마를 로드맵 결정과 연결해야 할 때

사용하지 않는 경우:
- 원자료가 아직 태깅되지 않음 → 먼저 `product-feedback-triage-tagging-ko`
- 단일 리서치 종합 → `feedback-affinity-synthesis-ko`
- 이탈·해지 고객 원인 분석 → `product-churn-win-loss-analysis-ko`

## 먼저 확인할 사항

1. 대상 기간과 비교 기간
2. 데이터: 태깅된 피드백, 유형별 CS 건수, 카카오톡 상담 기록, 앱 리뷰 평점·내용, NPS·CSAT 점수와 코멘트, 리서치 결과 — 각 출처
3. 보고 대상과 그들이 가진 결정 권한
4. 테마와 연결할 현재 목표·OKR
5. 이미 진행 중인 대응
6. 나눠 볼 세그먼트(요금제, 지역, OS, 고객 규모)

## 작성 절차

1. **출처를 정리합니다.** 건수, 기간, 알려진 편향을 적습니다(예: "CS 문의는 관리자 계정 비중이 높음", "앱 리뷰는 불만 사용자 비중이 높음", "카카오톡 상담은 결제·배송 문의 위주").
2. **테마 순위를 매깁니다.** 도달(고유 고객 수), 심각도, 추세, 전략 관련성을 어떤 규칙으로 조합했는지 밝힙니다.
3. **테마마다 근거를 붙입니다.** 언급 수와 고유 고객 수, 영향 세그먼트, 출처 ID가 달린 짧은 원문 1~3개(정확히 인용, 비식별), 가능하면 관련 지표
4. **변화를 보여줍니다.** 신규·증가·감소·해결 테마. 고객 경험 변화가 아니라 문의량이나 채널 변화 때문일 수 있으면 그렇게 적습니다.
5. **목표와 연결합니다.** 어떤 테마가 어떤 OKR을 위협하거나 돕는지
6. **대응 상태를 적습니다.** 로드맵 반영(링크), 조사 중, 의도적으로 대응 안 함(이유), 결정 필요
7. **칭찬도 짧게** 정리합니다. 지켜야 할 것을 알려줍니다.
8. **경영진에게 요청할 결정**을 나열합니다.
9. **요약은 마지막에** 3~5줄로 씁니다.

## 출력 형식

```
# VOC 리포트 — [기간]   작성 [PM], [날짜]
## 요약(3~5줄)
## 출처와 유의사항
| 출처 | 건수 | 기간 | 알려진 편향 |

## 주요 테마
| # | 테마 | 고유 고객 수 | 언급 수 | 세그먼트 | 추세 | 연결 목표 | 대응 |
### 테마 1: [이름]
고객 이야기: ...  근거: "[원문]" (CS-1043), ...  지표: ...  대응: ...

## 전 기간 대비 변화: 신규 / 증가 / 해결
## 고객이 좋아하는 점(유지할 것)
## 요청 의사결정
## 부록: 방법, 분류 체계 버전
```

## 품질 점검

- 모든 테마에 단위가 정의된 건수와 출처가 있는 원문이 하나 이상 있습니다.
- 원문은 정확하고 짧으며 비식별 처리되어 추적 가능합니다. 따옴표 안에 합성하거나 바꿔 쓴 문장이 없습니다.
- 편향과 출처 한계를 앞부분에 밝혔습니다.
- 테마마다 대응 상태가 있어 불만 목록으로 끝나지 않습니다.
- 추세 비교가 같은 기준끼리 이뤄졌습니다.
- 요약이 한 화면 안에 들어갑니다.

## 한계

- 원문, 점수, 건수, 추세를 지어내지 않습니다. 데이터가 없으면 없다고 씁니다.
- 피드백 양은 무엇이 이야기되는지를 보여줄 뿐, 전체 사용자 중 문제가 얼마나 흔한지는 아닙니다. 가능하면 사용 데이터와 함께 봅니다.
- 배포 전 이름, 연락처, 주문번호 등 개인정보를 제거합니다.
- 대응과 우선순위는 제품팀과 경영진이 결정합니다.

skills.body:
# Voice of Customer Report

Leadership को संक्षेप में बताता है कि customers क्या अनुभव कर रहे हैं, क्या बदला है, और product team क्या करने का प्रस्ताव रखती है। Quantitative signal (volumes, scores) और qualitative evidence (verbatims) को साथ रखता है, और sample sources व biases के बारे में साफ़ रहता है।

## कब उपयोग करें / कब नहीं

उपयोग करें जब:
- Monthly या quarterly feedback readout देना है।
- Leadership पूछे "customers हमें क्या बता रहे हैं?"।
- Feedback themes को roadmap फ़ैसलों से जोड़ना है।

उपयोग न करें जब:
- Raw feedback अभी tag नहीं हुआ → पहले `product-feedback-triage-tagging-hi`
- एक research study का synthesis → `feedback-affinity-synthesis-hi`
- खोए या churn हुए customers की खास वजहें → `product-churn-win-loss-analysis-hi`

## पहले क्या पूछें

1. अवधि और तुलना की अवधि।
2. Data: tagged feedback export, category-wise call centre/WhatsApp volumes, NPS/CSAT scores और comments, review ratings, research findings — हर एक का source।
3. Audience और उनके पास कौन-से फ़ैसले हैं।
4. मौजूदा goals/OKRs ताकि themes जोड़ी जा सकें।
5. जाने-पहचाने themes पर पहले से चल रहे actions।
6. किन segments में बाँटना है (plan, शहर tier, राज्य, भाषा, Android/iOS, customer size)।

## चरण

1. **Sources की सूची** counts, अवधि और ज्ञात bias के साथ बनाएँ (जैसे "Play Store reviews में नाराज़ users ज़्यादा"; "call centre पर tier-3 और पहली बार के users ज़्यादा, क्योंकि वे लिखने के बजाय फ़ोन करते हैं"; "WhatsApp chats में refund सवाल ज़्यादा")।
2. **Themes rank करें** reach (unique customers), severity, trend और strategic relevance के बताए गए संयोजन से। नियम लिखें।
3. **हर theme का evidence:** mentions और unique customers, प्रभावित segments, source IDs के साथ 1–3 छोटे verbatims (हूबहू, मूल भाषा में, ज़रूरत हो तो साथ में English/Hindi अर्थ, anonymised), और उपलब्ध हो तो supporting metric।
4. **बदलाव दिखाएँ।** नए, बढ़ते, घटते, हल हुए themes। अगर बदलाव volume या channel shift (जैसे festive sale, नया IVR) से हो सकता है, तो लिखें।
5. **Goals से जोड़ें** — कौन-सी theme किस OKR को खतरे में डालती या मदद करती है।
6. **हर theme का response:** roadmap में (link), जाँच जारी, जानबूझकर नहीं (क्यों), फ़ैसला चाहिए।
7. **तारीफ़ भी संक्षेप में** — क्या बचाकर रखना है।
8. **Leadership से माँगे फ़ैसले** लिखें।
9. **Executive summary अंत में** लिखें: 3–5 bullets।

## आउटपुट फ़ॉर्मेट

```
# Voice of Customer — [अवधि]   तैयार: [PM], [तारीख़]
## Executive summary (3–5 bullets)
## Sources और caveats
| Source | Items | अवधि | ज्ञात bias |

## Top themes
| # | Theme | Unique customers | Mentions | Segments | Trend | Linked goal | Response |
### Theme 1: [नाम]
हम क्या सुन रहे हैं: ...  Evidence: "[verbatim]" (WA-1043), ...  Metric: ...  Response: ...

## पिछली अवधि से बदलाव: नए / बढ़ते / हल हुए
## Customers क्या पसंद करते हैं (बचाकर रखें)
## माँगे गए फ़ैसले
## Appendix: method, taxonomy version
```

## गुणवत्ता जाँच

- हर theme के counts की unit परिभाषित है और कम से कम एक sourced verbatim है।
- Verbatims हूबहू, छोटे, anonymised और traceable हैं; quotes के अंदर जोड़े या बदले हुए वाक्य नहीं।
- Biases और source सीमाएँ शुरू में बताई गई हैं।
- हर theme का response status है — report सिर्फ़ शिकायतों की list नहीं।
- Trend दावे समान आधार पर तुलना करते हैं।
- Executive summary एक screen में आता है।

## सीमाएँ

- Verbatims, scores, counts या trends कभी न गढ़ें; data न हो तो साफ़ कहें।
- Feedback volume बताता है कि क्या कहा जा रहा है, यह नहीं कि सभी users में problem कितनी आम है; संभव हो तो usage data के साथ देखें।
- बाँटने से पहले personal data (नाम, mobile number, UPI ID) हटाएँ।
- Responses और priorities product team और leadership तय करते हैं।

skills.name: product-exec-review-deck
skills.description: Builds the storyline and slide-by-slide outline for a monthly or quarterly product review with executives (QBR/MBR): headline narrative, outcomes vs. goals, what we learned, roadmap status, risks, and the decisions or resources requested, with speaker notes and an appendix plan. Use when a PM says "prep my QBR", "exec review deck", "quarterly business review for product", "how should I structure this leadership readout", or "turn this quarter into slides".
skills.body:
# Product Executive Review Deck (QBR / MBR)

Produces an argument, not a status dump: a short deck that tells leadership how the product area performed against its goals, what the team learned, what it will do next and what it needs. The output is a storyline, a slide-by-slide outline with headline titles, speaker notes and a list of charts to build. Visual polish is out of scope.

## When to use / when not to use

Use when:
- A monthly, quarterly or half-year review with executives or a steering group is coming up.
- You have lots of material (OKR scores, metrics, launches) and need a narrative.
- You need leadership to make a decision or approve resources during the review.

Do not use when:
- It is a routine weekly update — use `product-weekly-status-update`.
- You are setting next quarter's OKRs — use `product-okr-drafting`; bring the draft as an input here.
- You are planning the roadmap itself — use `product-outcome-roadmap`.
- One contested choice needs a memo — use `product-tradeoff-decision-memo` and attach it.
- You need visual design polish of finished slides — use `slide-visual-polish`.
- It is an investor or board update — use the founder skills (`founder-monthly-investor-update`, `founder-board-meeting-pack`).

## What to ask for first

1. Meeting type, audience (names/roles), length, and how much is presentation vs. discussion.
2. Goals for the period (OKRs, targets) and their final or current scores.
3. Metric data with sources and dates; prior review deck for continuity.
4. Launches and experiments shipped, with results (link readouts, e.g. `product-experiment-readout`).
5. Misses and surprises — what did not go to plan.
6. Next-period plan and roadmap changes.
7. The decisions or resources you want from this meeting.
8. Company template, slide limit, pre-read vs. live presentation.

1. **Write the one-sentence headline** for the whole period (e.g. "Activation goal hit; retention flat — we're shifting Q[n] focus to week-4 habits"). Every slide must support it.

6. **Explain drivers with evidence.** Link movements to launches or experiments only where evidence exists (readout, cohort analysis); otherwise say "correlated, not proven".
7. **Turn misses into learnings** with a concrete change in plan.
8. **Specify each chart**: metric, time range, comparison, source; one message per chart.
9. **Draft speaker notes** (2–4 bullets per slide) and likely executive questions with prepared answers.
10. **Move detail to the appendix**: definitions, full metric tables, methodology.
11. **Time-box**: about 2 minutes per main slide; leave at least a third of the meeting for discussion.

```
Headline: [one sentence]
Asks: 1. [decision/resource] by [date]  2. ...

## Slide outline
| # | Action title | Content / chart spec (metric, range, source) | Speaker notes |

## Goals scorecard (slide 2)
| Goal | Target | Actual | Status | Why (1 line) |

## Anticipated questions

## Appendix list
- Metric definitions, full tables, experiment readouts, ...

## Pre-read note (if async)
```

- Asks appear at the start and end, each with an owner and a date.
- Misses are on main slides, not hidden in the appendix.
- Every number has source and date; definitions match the previous review or the change is flagged.
- Causal claims are backed by experiments or clearly labelled as correlation.
- The deck fits the time with room for discussion.

## Limits

- Never invent metric values, OKR scores or experiment results; leave `[DATA: metric, source]` placeholders.

skills.body:
# 제품 경영진 보고 자료(QBR / MBR)

현황 나열이 아니라 주장이 있는 보고 자료를 만듭니다. 제품 영역이 목표 대비 어떤 성과를 냈는지, 무엇을 배웠는지, 다음에 무엇을 할지, 무엇이 필요한지를 경영진에게 짧게 전달합니다. 결과물은 스토리라인, 결론형 제목이 붙은 장표별 구성안, 발표 노트, 만들 차트 목록입니다. 시각 디자인 다듬기는 범위 밖입니다.

## 사용 시점 / 사용하지 않는 경우

사용하는 경우:
- 월간·분기·반기 경영진 보고나 운영위원회가 다가올 때
- OKR 점수, 지표, 출시 내역 등 자료는 많은데 흐름이 없을 때
- 보고 자리에서 의사결정이나 자원 승인을 받아야 할 때

사용하지 않는 경우:
- 일상적인 주간 보고 → `product-weekly-status-update-ko`
- 다음 분기 OKR 수립 → `product-okr-drafting-ko` (초안을 이 자료의 입력으로 활용)
- 로드맵 자체 수립 → `product-outcome-roadmap-ko`
- 쟁점 하나에 대한 결정 메모 → `product-tradeoff-decision-memo-ko`를 첨부
- 완성된 장표의 시각적 완성도 → `slide-visual-polish-ko`
- 투자자·이사회 보고 → `founder-monthly-investor-update-ko`, `founder-board-meeting-pack-ko`

## 먼저 확인할 사항

1. 보고 유형, 참석자(이름·직책), 시간, 발표와 토론의 비중
2. 기간 목표(OKR, KPI)와 최종 또는 현재 달성도
3. 출처·기준일이 있는 지표 데이터, 직전 보고 자료
4. 출시·실험 내역과 결과(`product-experiment-readout-ko` 결과 링크)
5. 계획대로 되지 않은 것, 예상 밖의 일
6. 다음 기간 계획과 로드맵 변경
7. 이번 자리에서 받아야 할 결정·자원
8. 회사 템플릿, 장표 수 제한, 사전 배포 여부

## 작성 절차

1. **기간 전체를 한 문장 핵심 메시지로 씁니다.** (예: "활성화 목표 달성, 리텐션은 정체 — 다음 분기는 4주차 습관 형성에 집중합니다") 모든 장표가 이 문장을 뒷받침해야 합니다.
2. **구성을 정합니다**(장표 수에 맞게 조정):
   1) 핵심 메시지와 요청 사항 2) 목표 달성 현황 3) 성과 요인 4) 미달 항목과 배운 점 5) 고객 근거 6) 로드맵 현황·변경 7) 다음 기간 계획 8) 리스크 9) 요청할 결정·자원 / 부록
3. **요청 사항은 첫 장과 마지막 장에 둡니다.** 경영진이 처음부터 무엇을 결정해야 하는지 알아야 합니다.
4. **제목은 결론형 문장으로 씁니다.** "리텐션"이 아니라 "온보딩 개편 후 1주차 리텐션 3%p 상승"처럼 씁니다.
5. **목표 달성 현황은 정직하게 씁니다.** 목표, 목표치, 실적, 상태, 한 줄 원인. 미달도 달성만큼 잘 보이게 둡니다.
6. **성과 요인은 근거와 함께 씁니다.** 실험이나 코호트 분석 근거가 있을 때만 출시와 지표 변화를 연결하고, 아니면 "상관관계, 인과 미검증"이라고 표시합니다.
7. **미달 항목은 배운 점과 구체적인 계획 변경으로 바꿉니다.**
8. **차트마다 사양을 적습니다.** 지표, 기간, 비교 대상, 출처, 차트 한 장에 메시지 하나.
9. **발표 노트**(장표당 2~4줄)와 예상 질문·답변을 준비합니다.
10. **세부 내용은 부록으로 보냅니다.** 지표 정의, 전체 표, 분석 방법.
11. **시간 배분:** 본 장표당 약 2분, 회의의 3분의 1 이상은 토론에 남깁니다.

## 출력 형식

```
# [영역] [분기/월] 경영진 보고 — 스토리라인
핵심 메시지: [한 문장]
요청 사항: 1. [결정/자원] ([날짜]까지)  2. ...

## 장표 구성
| # | 결론형 제목 | 내용·차트 사양(지표, 기간, 출처) | 발표 노트 |

## 목표 달성 현황(2번 장표)
| 목표 | 목표치 | 실적 | 상태 | 원인(한 줄) |

## 예상 질문
- Q: ...  A: ... [근거 링크]

## 부록 목록
## 사전 배포용 요약(서면 보고 시)
```

## 품질 점검

- 장표 제목만 읽어도 전체 흐름이 이해됩니다.
- 요청 사항이 처음과 끝에 있고, 각각 담당자와 기한이 있습니다.
- 미달 항목이 부록이 아니라 본 장표에 있습니다.
- 모든 숫자에 출처와 기준일이 있고, 지표 정의가 직전 보고와 같거나 변경 사실을 표시했습니다.
- 인과 주장은 실험 근거가 있거나 상관관계로 명시했습니다.
- 토론 시간을 남기고도 시간 안에 끝납니다.

## 한계

- 지표 값, OKR 점수, 실험 결과를 지어내지 않습니다. `[데이터: 지표, 출처]`로 비워 둡니다.
- 근거 없이 출시 효과를 주장하지 않으며, 효과를 어떻게 추정했는지 밝힙니다.
- 향후 목표치는 경영진 승인 전까지 제안일 뿐입니다.
- 고객·직원 개인정보는 장표에 넣지 않고 집계하거나 비식별화합니다.

6. **성과 요인은 근거와 함께 씁니다.** 실험이나 코호트 분석 근거가 있을 때만 출시와 지표 변화를 연결하고, 아니면 "상관관계, 인과 미검증"이라고 표시합니다.
7. **미달 항목은 배운 점과 구체적인 계획 변경으로 바꿉니다.**
8. **차트마다 사양을 적습니다.** 지표, 기간, 비교 대상, 출처, 차트 한 장에 메시지 하나.
9. **발표 노트**(장표당 2~4줄)와 예상 질문·답변을 준비합니다.
10. **세부 내용은 부록으로 보냅니다.** 지표 정의, 전체 표, 분석 방법.
11. **시간 배분:** 본 장표당 약 2분, 회의의 3분의 1 이상은 토론에 남깁니다.

## 출력 형식

```
# [영역] [분기/월] 경영진 보고 — 스토리라인
핵심 메시지: [한 문장]
요청 사항: 1. [결정/자원] ([날짜]까지)  2. ...

## 장표 구성
| # | 결론형 제목 | 내용·차트 사양(지표, 기간, 출처) | 발표 노트 |

## 목표 달성 현황(2번 장표)
| 목표 | 목표치 | 실적 | 상태 | 원인(한 줄) |

## 예상 질문
- Q: ...  A: ... [근거 링크]

## 부록 목록
## 사전 배포용 요약(서면 보고 시)
```

## 품질 점검

- 장표 제목만 읽어도 전체 흐름이 이해됩니다.
- 요청 사항이 처음과 끝에 있고, 각각 담당자와 기한이 있습니다.
- 미달 항목이 부록이 아니라 본 장표에 있습니다.
- 모든 숫자에 출처와 기준일이 있고, 지표 정의가 직전 보고와 같거나 변경 사실을 표시했습니다.
- 인과 주장은 실험 근거가 있거나 상관관계로 명시했습니다.
- 토론 시간을 남기고도 시간 안에 끝납니다.

## 한계

- 지표 값, OKR 점수, 실험 결과를 지어내지 않습니다. `[데이터: 지표, 출처]`로 비워 둡니다.
- 근거 없이 출시 효과를 주장하지 않으며, 효과를 어떻게 추정했는지 밝힙니다.
- 향후 목표치는 경영진 승인 전까지 제안일 뿐입니다.
- 고객·직원 개인정보는 장표에 넣지 않고 집계하거나 비식별화합니다.

skills.body:
# Product Executive Review Deck (QBR / MBR)

Status dump नहीं, एक तर्क तैयार करता है: छोटा deck जो leadership को बताए कि product area ने goals के मुकाबले कैसा किया, team ने क्या सीखा, आगे क्या करेगी और उसे क्या चाहिए। Output: storyline, action-title वाली slide outline, speaker notes और बनाए जाने वाले charts की list। Visual polish इस skill के दायरे में नहीं।

## कब उपयोग करें / कब नहीं

उपयोग करें जब:
- Executives या steering group के साथ monthly, quarterly या half-yearly review आने वाला हो।
- बहुत सारी सामग्री (OKR scores, metrics, launches) हो पर narrative न हो।
- Review में leadership से decision या resource approval चाहिए।

उपयोग न करें जब:
- Routine weekly update → `product-weekly-status-update-hi`
- अगले quarter के OKRs → `product-okr-drafting-hi` (draft को यहाँ input बनाएँ)
- Roadmap बनाना → `product-outcome-roadmap-hi`
- एक विवादित choice पर memo → `product-tradeoff-decision-memo-hi` attach करें
- तैयार slides का visual polish → `slide-visual-polish-hi`
- Investor या board update → `founder-monthly-investor-update-hi`, `founder-board-meeting-pack-hi`

## पहले क्या पूछें

1. Meeting type, audience (नाम/role), अवधि, presentation बनाम discussion का अनुपात।
2. अवधि के goals (OKRs, targets) और उनके final/current scores।
3. Source और date सहित metric data; पिछला review deck।
4. Ship हुए launches और experiments, results के साथ (`product-experiment-readout-hi` के links)।
5. जो plan के मुताबिक नहीं हुआ, और surprises।
6. अगली अवधि का plan और roadmap बदलाव।
7. इस meeting से कौन-से decisions/resources चाहिए।
8. Company template, slide limit, pre-read या live presentation।

## चरण

1. **पूरी अवधि का एक-वाक्य headline लिखें** (जैसे "Activation goal पूरा; retention सपाट — अगले quarter week-4 habits पर फ़ोकस")। हर slide इसे support करे।
2. **Structure चुनें** (slide limit के हिसाब से):
   1) Headline और asks 2) Goals scorecard 3) Results के drivers 4) Misses और सीख 5) Customer evidence 6) Roadmap status और बदलाव 7) अगली अवधि का plan 8) Risks 9) माँगे गए decisions/resources · Appendix
3. **Asks पहली slide पर और अंत में फिर से रखें।**
4. **Action titles लिखें** — हर title पूरा takeaway वाक्य हो ("Onboarding redesign के बाद week-1 retention 3 pts ऊपर", न कि "Retention")।
5. **Scorecard ईमानदारी से बनाएँ।** Goal, target, actual, status, एक-line कारण। Misses उतने ही साफ़ दिखें जितनी wins।
6. **Drivers evidence के साथ समझाएँ।** Launch और metric बदलाव को सिर्फ़ तब जोड़ें जब experiment या cohort analysis हो; वरना "correlated, proven नहीं" लिखें।
7. **Misses को सीख में बदलें** और plan में ठोस बदलाव बताएँ।
8. **हर chart की spec दें**: metric, time range, comparison, source; एक chart में एक message।
9. **Indian context जोड़ें जहाँ लागू हो:** festive season (Diwali/Big sale events) का असर, regional splits (metro / tier-2 / tier-3, राज्य, भाषा), low-bandwidth या low-end Android segments — ताकि leadership averages से भ्रमित न हो।
10. **Speaker notes** (हर slide पर 2–4 bullets) और संभावित executive सवालों के जवाब तैयार करें।
11. **Detail appendix में डालें**: definitions, पूरी metric tables, methodology।
12. **Time-box**: हर main slide ~2 मिनट; meeting का कम से कम एक-तिहाई discussion के लिए।

## Output format

```
# [Area] [Q/Month] review — storyline
Headline: [एक वाक्य]
Asks: 1. [decision/resource], [date] तक  2. ...

## Slide outline
| # | Action title | Content / chart spec (metric, range, source) | Speaker notes |

## Goals scorecard (slide 2)
| Goal | Target | Actual | Status | क्यों (1 line) |

## संभावित सवाल
- Q: ...  A: ... [evidence link]

## Appendix list
## Pre-read note (async हो तो)
```

## Quality checks

- सिर्फ़ slide titles पढ़कर पूरी कहानी समझ आती है।
- Asks शुरू और अंत में हैं, हर एक का owner और date है।
- Misses main slides पर हैं, appendix में छिपे नहीं।
- हर number के साथ source और date है; definitions पिछले review जैसी हैं या बदलाव flag किया गया है।
- Causal claims experiments से समर्थित हैं या correlation के रूप में label हैं।
- Discussion के समय के साथ deck समय में फ़िट होता है।

## Limits

- Metric values, OKR scores या experiment results कभी न गढ़ें; `[DATA: metric, source]` placeholder रखें।
- बिना evidence किसी launch को impact का श्रेय न दें; बताएँ कि impact कैसे estimate हुआ।
- आगे के targets leadership approval तक proposal हैं।
- Slides में customers या employees का personal data न डालें — aggregate या anonymise करें (DPDP Act की भावना के अनुरूप)।

skills.name: product-internal-launch-notes
skills.description: Writes internal launch notes and release notes for a shipped product change aimed at colleagues (sales, support, success, marketing, ops, leadership): what shipped, who gets it and when, why it matters, how it works, known limitations, how to talk about it, FAQs, and where to get help. Use when a PM says "write the internal launch announcement", "release notes for the team", "enablement note for sales and support", "what changed this release", or "tell the company we shipped X".
skills.body:
# Internal Launch & Release Notes

Produces the internal announcement colleagues need when a product change goes live: enough to explain it to a customer, support it, sell it, or know it affects their work. It is tailored by audience, honest about limitations and rollout status, and links to the source of truth. External marketing announcements are out of scope.

## When to use / when not to use

Use when:
- A feature, change or fix is launching (beta, staged rollout or GA) and internal teams must be ready.
- You need a recurring internal release-notes digest (weekly/sprint).
- Support or sales keep asking "what changed?".

Do not use when:
- You are still deciding whether to ship — use `product-launch-go-no-go`.
- You need customer-facing launch content or campaigns — use `marketing-launch-announcement-kit`.
- The change is a delay or descope of a promised item — use `product-roadmap-change-comms`.
- It is the weekly program status — use `product-weekly-status-update`.

## What to ask for first

1. What shipped, in one sentence, plus the PRD/ticket links.
2. Rollout: stage (internal, % rollout, beta, GA), dates, eligible plans/regions/platforms, feature flag names.
3. The customer problem it solves and who benefits.
4. How it works (steps, screenshots or video to link).
5. Known limitations, bugs and what is explicitly not included.
6. Pricing/packaging impact, if any (confirmed by owner).
7. Support readiness: help article, macros, escalation path, on-call.
8. Success metric and when results will be shared.
9. Audiences to address and their channels.

## Steps

1. **Lead with the TL;DR**: what, who, when — in three lines.
2. **State rollout status precisely.** "Live for 10% of web users on Pro, ramping to 100% by [date] if guardrails hold" — never just "launched" if staged.
3. **Explain why it matters** in customer terms (problem → outcome), one short paragraph.
4. **Describe how it works** in numbered steps, linking visuals.
5. **List limitations and not-in-scope items** plainly, with any workarounds. This prevents over-promising.
6. **Add audience sections** only where content differs:
   - Support: how to identify affected users, common issues, macro, escalation.
   - Sales/success: who to tell, talk track in 2–3 sentences, what not to promise.
   - Marketing: external timing and approved messaging owner.
   - Ops/finance/legal: billing, data, policy impacts.
7. **Write an FAQ** (5–8 real questions, including "when will it be available to everyone?" and "what if a customer wants it off?").
8. **Say how success will be measured** and when the team will report results (do not report results yet unless measured).
9. **Provide help channels and owners.**
10. **For release-note digests**, group items as New / Improved / Fixed / Deprecated, one line each with the user impact.

## Output format

```
# [Feature] is [live for X / in beta / GA] — internal launch note
TL;DR: [what] for [who], [rollout + dates].

## Why it matters
## How it works
1. ...  [screenshot/video link]
## Rollout & eligibility
| Stage | Audience | Date | Flag |
## Limitations & not included
## For Support / For Sales & CS / For Marketing / For Ops (only those needed)
## FAQ
## How we'll measure success — results expected [date]
## Questions? [channel] · Owner: [PM] · Eng: [name] · Docs: [links]
```

## Quality checks

- A support agent could answer the top three customer questions from the note alone.
- Rollout status, eligibility and dates are exact and match the flag configuration.
- Limitations are stated as plainly as benefits.
- Nothing promises future features or dates without owner confirmation.
- Every audience section has an action or "nothing to do".
- Links point to the source of truth (PRD, help article), not copies.

## Limits

- Never invent dates, eligibility, pricing or metrics; mark gaps `[CONFIRM]`.
- Do not claim impact ("increased conversion by …") before an experiment or analysis exists.
- Pricing, legal and security statements need sign-off by their owners.
- Internal notes get forwarded; keep customer names and confidential data out unless approved.

# Internal Launch & Release Notes

Produces the internal announcement colleagues need when a product change goes live: enough to explain it to a customer, support it, sell it, or know it affects their work. It is tailored by audience, honest about limitations and rollout status, and links to the source of truth. External marketing announcements are out of scope.

## When to use / when not to use

Use when:
- A feature, change or fix is launching (beta, staged rollout or GA) and internal teams must be ready.
- You need a recurring internal release-notes digest (weekly/sprint).
- Support or sales keep asking "what changed?".

Do not use when:
- You are still deciding whether to ship — use `product-launch-go-no-go`.
- You need customer-facing launch content or campaigns — use `marketing-launch-announcement-kit`.
- The change is a delay or descope of a promised item — use `product-roadmap-change-comms`.
- It is the weekly program status — use `product-weekly-status-update`.

## What to ask for first

1. What shipped, in one sentence, plus the PRD/ticket links.
2. Rollout: stage (internal, % rollout, beta, GA), dates, eligible plans/regions/platforms, feature flag names.
3. The customer problem it solves and who benefits.
4. How it works (steps, screenshots or video to link).
5. Known limitations, bugs and what is explicitly not included.
6. Pricing/packaging impact, if any (confirmed by owner).
7. Support readiness: help article, macros, escalation path, on-call.
8. Success metric and when results will be shared.
9. Audiences to address and their channels.

## Steps

1. **Lead with the TL;DR**: what, who, when — in three lines.
2. **State rollout status precisely.** "Live for 10% of web users on Pro, ramping to 100% by [date] if guardrails hold" — never just "launched" if staged.
3. **Explain why it matters** in customer terms (problem → outcome), one short paragraph.
4. **Describe how it works** in numbered steps, linking visuals.
5. **List limitations and not-in-scope items** plainly, with any workarounds. This prevents over-promising.
6. **Add audience sections** only where content differs:
   - Support: how to identify affected users, common issues, macro, escalation.
   - Sales/success: who to tell, talk track in 2–3 sentences, what not to promise.
   - Marketing: external timing and approved messaging owner.
   - Ops/finance/legal: billing, data, policy impacts.
7. **Write an FAQ** (5–8 real questions, including "when will it be available to everyone?" and "what if a customer wants it off?").
8. **Say how success will be measured** and when the team will report results (do not report results yet unless measured).
9. **Provide help channels and owners.**
10. **For release-note digests**, group items as New / Improved / Fixed / Deprecated, one line each with the user impact.

## Output format

```
# [Feature] is [live for X / in beta / GA] — internal launch note
TL;DR: [what] for [who], [rollout + dates].

## Why it matters
## How it works
1. ...  [screenshot/video link]
## Rollout & eligibility
| Stage | Audience | Date | Flag |
## Limitations & not included
## For Support / For Sales & CS / For Marketing / For Ops (only those needed)
## FAQ
## How we'll measure success — results expected [date]
## Questions? [channel] · Owner: [PM] · Eng: [name] · Docs: [links]
```

## Quality checks

- A support agent could answer the top three customer questions from the note alone.
- Rollout status, eligibility and dates are exact and match the flag configuration.
- Limitations are stated as plainly as benefits.
- Nothing promises future features or dates without owner confirmation.
- Every audience section has an action or "nothing to do".
- Links point to the source of truth (PRD, help article), not copies.

## Limits

- Never invent dates, eligibility, pricing or metrics; mark gaps `[CONFIRM]`.
- Do not claim impact ("increased conversion by …") before an experiment or analysis exists.
- Pricing, legal and security statements need sign-off by their owners.
- Internal notes get forwarded; keep customer names and confidential data out unless approved.

skills.body:
# 사내 출시 공지·릴리스 노트

제품 변경이 배포될 때 동료들이 고객에게 설명하고, 지원하고, 판매하고, 자기 업무 영향을 알 수 있도록 사내 공지를 만듭니다. 독자별로 필요한 내용만 담고, 제약과 배포 상태를 정직하게 밝히며, 원본 문서로 연결합니다. 외부 마케팅 공지는 범위 밖입니다.

## 사용 시점 / 사용하지 않는 경우

사용하는 경우:
- 기능·변경·수정이 베타, 단계적 배포, 정식 출시되고 사내 팀이 준비해야 할 때
- 스프린트·주 단위 사내 릴리스 노트 정리가 필요할 때
- CS나 영업이 계속 "뭐가 바뀌었어요?"라고 물을 때

사용하지 않는 경우:
- 아직 출시 여부를 결정 중 → `product-launch-go-no-go-ko`
- 고객 대상 출시 콘텐츠·캠페인 → `marketing-launch-announcement-kit-ko`
- 약속한 항목의 지연·축소 공지 → `product-roadmap-change-comms-ko`
- 주간 진행 보고 → `product-weekly-status-update-ko`

## 먼저 확인할 사항

1. 출시 내용 한 문장, PRD·티켓 링크
2. 배포: 단계(사내, 비율 배포, 베타, 정식), 일정, 대상 요금제·지역·플랫폼(iOS/Android/웹), 피처 플래그 이름
3. 해결하는 고객 문제와 수혜자
4. 사용 방법(단계, 스크린샷·영상 링크)
5. 알려진 제약, 버그, 이번에 포함되지 않은 것
6. 요금·패키지 영향(담당자 확인 완료 여부)
7. CS 준비: 도움말, 상담 매크로, 카카오톡 채널 응대 문구, 에스컬레이션 경로
8. 성공 지표와 결과 공유 시점
9. 공지 대상과 채널

## 작성 절차

1. **세 줄 요약으로 시작합니다:** 무엇을, 누구에게, 언제.
2. **배포 상태를 정확히 씁니다.** 단계적 배포라면 "웹 Pro 사용자 10%에 적용, 가드레일 이상 없으면 [날짜]까지 100%"처럼 쓰고 "출시 완료"라고만 쓰지 않습니다.
3. **왜 중요한지** 고객 관점(문제 → 결과)으로 한 문단 씁니다.
4. **사용 방법**을 번호 목록으로 쓰고 이미지를 링크합니다.
5. **제약과 미포함 항목**을 우회 방법과 함께 분명히 씁니다. 과잉 약속을 막습니다.
6. **독자별 섹션**은 내용이 다를 때만 둡니다.
   - CS: 영향받는 고객 식별법, 예상 문의, 매크로, 에스컬레이션
   - 영업·고객성공: 누구에게 알릴지, 2~3문장 응대 멘트, 약속하면 안 되는 것
   - 마케팅: 외부 공개 시점과 메시지 승인 담당
   - 운영·재무·법무: 결제, 데이터, 약관·정책 영향
7. **FAQ** 5~8개를 씁니다("전체 사용자는 언제?", "고객이 끄고 싶다면?" 포함).
8. **성공 측정 방법**과 결과 공유 시점을 씁니다. 측정 전에는 결과를 쓰지 않습니다.
9. **문의 채널과 담당자**를 적습니다.
10. **릴리스 노트 모음**이라면 신규 / 개선 / 수정 / 지원 종료로 묶고 항목당 한 줄로 사용자 영향을 씁니다.

## 출력 형식

```
# [기능] [일부 적용/베타/정식 출시] — 사내 공지
요약: [무엇]을 [누구]에게, [배포 단계·일정]

## 왜 중요한가
## 사용 방법
1. ...  [이미지/영상 링크]
## 배포 단계와 대상
| 단계 | 대상 | 일정 | 플래그 |
## 제약 및 미포함 사항
## CS용 / 영업·고객성공용 / 마케팅용 / 운영용 (필요한 것만)
## FAQ
## 성공 측정 — 결과 공유 예정 [날짜]
## 문의: [채널] · PM: [이름] · 개발: [이름] · 문서: [링크]
```

## 품질 점검

- CS 담당자가 이 공지만으로 고객 문의 상위 3개에 답할 수 있습니다.
- 배포 상태, 대상, 일정이 정확하고 플래그 설정과 일치합니다.
- 제약이 장점만큼 분명하게 적혀 있습니다.
- 담당자 확인 없이 향후 기능이나 일정을 약속하지 않습니다.
- 독자별 섹션마다 할 일 또는 "조치 불필요"가 있습니다.
- 링크는 사본이 아니라 원본(PRD, 도움말)을 가리킵니다.

## 한계

- 일정, 대상, 요금, 지표를 지어내지 않습니다. 빈칸은 `[확인 필요]`로 둡니다.
- 실험·분석 전에는 "전환율 X% 상승" 같은 효과를 주장하지 않습니다.
- 요금, 법무, 보안 관련 문구는 각 담당자 승인을 받습니다.
- 사내 공지도 외부로 전달될 수 있으니 고객사명·기밀은 승인 없이 넣지 않습니다.
