skills.body:
# रुकी हुई डील को फिर से शुरू करना

डील एक छूटे ईमेल से नहीं मरती; वह इसलिए रुकती है क्योंकि प्राथमिकता, ज़िम्मेदार व्यक्ति या भरोसा बदल गया। भारत में आम कारण हैं: budget approval या PO में देरी, financial year-end (मार्च), मालिक/प्रमोटर की मंज़ूरी बाक़ी, procurement में तीन quotation की तुलना, या कम कीमत की उम्मीद में इंतज़ार। यह स्किल पहले कारण का अनुमान लगाती है, फिर 3–4 touches लिखती है जिनमें ग्राहक "नहीं" भी आसानी से कह सके।

## कब उपयोग करें / कब नहीं

उपयोग करें:
- मीटिंग, प्रस्ताव या quotation के बाद 2+ हफ़्ते से कोई जवाब नहीं।
- Champion चुप है या कंपनी छोड़ चुका है।
- तय करना है कि opportunity रखें, आगे बढ़ाएँ या बंद करें।

उपयोग न करें:
- Prospect कभी जुड़ा ही नहीं → `sales-prospecting-sequence-hi`
- डील सक्रिय है पर एक ही संपर्क → `sales-multithread-stakeholder-email-hi`
- मौजूदा ग्राहक का renewal जोखिम में → `sales-renewal-expansion-outreach-hi`
- ग्राहक ने आपत्ति उठाई है → `sales-objection-handling-hi`

## पहले क्या पूछें

1. Opportunity इतिहास: stage, आख़िरी दो-तरफ़ा बातचीत (तारीख़, चैनल, विषय), उसके बाद क्या भेजा।
2. डील के संपर्क और उनकी भूमिका; champion अब भी उसी कंपनी/पद पर है या नहीं।
3. आख़िरी मीटिंग में तय अगला कदम और उसकी तारीख़।
4. ज्ञात संदर्भ: budget चक्र, FY-end, reorg, प्रतिस्पर्धी, procurement/legal/IT review, vendor registration।
5. लक्ष्य: फिर शुरू करना, scope बदलना, या pipeline साफ़ करने के लिए स्पष्ट जवाब।

## चरण

1. **कारण का अनुमान** (सबसे संभावित + विकल्प):
   - प्राथमिकता घटी / कोई compelling event नहीं
   - Champion को अंदर समर्थन नहीं मिला या वह चला गया
   - कीमत या business case कमज़ोर; बेहतर discount की प्रतीक्षा
   - Procurement, PO, legal या IT security में अटका
   - प्रतिस्पर्धी चुना या "अभी कुछ नहीं"
   - हमारे follow-ups में जवाब देने का नया कारण नहीं था
2. **कारण के अनुसार play**:
   - प्राथमिकता घटी → प्रासंगिक insight/ट्रिगर साझा करें, पूछें कि timing बदली क्या।
   - Champion अटका → अंदर बेचने में मदद (एक-पेज सार, senior-to-senior कॉल)।
   - कीमत मुद्दा → केवल स्वीकृत विकल्पों में छोटा scope या चरणबद्ध शुरुआत; बिना approval नया discount नहीं।
   - प्रक्रिया अटकी → owner पूछें, दस्तावेज़ों में मदद (security के लिए `sales-security-questionnaire-draft-hi`)।
   - Champion गया → उत्तराधिकारी को संदर्भ के साथ संपर्क।
3. **~2 हफ़्ते में 3–4 touches**:
   - Touch 1: नई जानकारी + एक सवाल ("बस follow-up कर रहा था" नहीं)।
   - Touch 2: कॉल या WhatsApp (यदि पहले से उस चैनल पर बातचीत हुई है), पहले बताई प्राथमिकता का ज़िक्र।
   - Touch 3: दूसरे ज्ञात stakeholder को छोटा नोट — champion को नज़रअंदाज़ करने जैसा न लगे; हो सके तो पहले champion को बताएँ।
   - Touch 4: विनम्र समापन — विकल्प दें: "अभी भी प्राथमिकता / [महीना] में फिर बात / इस बार नहीं"।
4. **लहजा**: अपराध-बोध ("मैंने 6 बार कोशिश की") नहीं, नकली deadline या "आज ही ख़त्म" offer नहीं, त्योहार/FY-end के समय का ध्यान।
5. **CRM कार्रवाई**: stage रखें + नई close date, stage पीछे करें, या closed-lost (कारण सहित); अगला task तय करें।

## आउटपुट फ़ॉर्मेट

1. निदान: संभावित कारण, प्रमाण, विकल्प
2. चुना गया play और कारण
3. Touch योजना तालिका: दिन | चैनल | प्राप्तकर्ता | उद्देश्य | Copy
4. हर touch का पूरा copy (placeholders `[नाम]`, `[उनकी प्राथमिकता]`, `[कंपनी]`)
5. CRM सिफ़ारिश: stage, close date, next step, loss reason

## गुणवत्ता जाँच

- [ ] हर touch नई value या जवाब देने का आसान तरीका देता है
- [ ] कोई दबाव, नकली urgency या अस्वीकृत discount नहीं
- [ ] पुरानी बातचीत का हवाला सही है
- [ ] दूसरे stakeholder से संपर्क champion का सम्मान करता है
- [ ] WhatsApp/कॉल में DND, opt-in और DPDP का पालन
- [ ] स्पष्ट CRM निर्णय

## सीमाएँ

प्रतिस्पर्धी गतिविधि, कीमतें, discounts, deadlines, फ़ीचर या चुप्पी के कारण न गढ़ें; अनुमान को परिकल्पना कहें और `[जाँचें]` लगाएँ। कोई भी रियायत या नई commercial शर्त manager/deal desk की मंज़ूरी के बाद ही।

skills.name: sales-renewal-expansion-outreach
skills.description: Plans and writes outreach to existing customers for renewals, upsells and cross-sells: a renewal timeline working back from the contract end date, a value recap based on verified usage and outcomes, expansion emails to new teams or use cases, and handling for at-risk accounts and price-increase notices. Use when an account manager says 'renewal is in 90 days', 'write the renewal email', 'upsell email for more seats', 'introduce our new module to this customer', 'price increase notice' or 'this renewal is at risk'.
skills.body:
# Renewal & Expansion Outreach

Renewals are won in the months before the contract ends, not in the last week. This skill builds a renewal timeline and writes customer-facing messages grounded in what the customer actually achieved, then identifies expansion openings without pushing products the customer has no use for.

## When to use / when not to use

Use when:
- A renewal is 60–180 days out.
- You see an expansion signal (usage near limits, new team asking, new use case, acquisition).
- You need to communicate a price change or packaging change at renewal.
- A renewal is at risk (low usage, champion left, complaints).

Do not use when:
- New-logo prospecting → `sales-prospecting-sequence`.
- You need a formal renewal/expansion quote document → `sales-proposal-writer`.
- Pricing questions in a live negotiation → `sales-pricing-question-reply`.
- Analysis of why many customers churn → `product-churn-win-loss-analysis`.

## What to ask for first

1. Contract facts: end date, notice period, auto-renewal clause, current products/seats, current price and any contractual price-increase cap. Read from the contract or CRM, don't guess.
2. Usage and outcome data: adoption, active users, support tickets, agreed success metrics and whether they were met.
3. Relationship: champion, economic buyer, recent changes (reorg, new leadership, acquisition).
4. Expansion signals with source (CSM notes, usage report, inbound request).
5. Commercial guidance: approved renewal price, any approved uplift or multi-year options, who approves concessions.
6. Risk signals: escalations, NPS/CSAT comments, competitor evaluation.

## Steps

skills.body:
# 갱신·확장 아웃리치

갱신은 마지막 주가 아니라 만료 몇 달 전에 결정됩니다. 특히 한국 기업은 연간 예산을 전년도 4분기에 편성하고 품의·결재와 구매 절차에 시간이 걸리므로, 예산 편성 시기 전에 성과를 공유해야 합니다. 이 스킬은 갱신 일정을 세우고 고객이 실제로 얻은 성과를 근거로 메일을 작성하며, 필요 없는 제품을 밀어붙이지 않고 확장 기회를 찾습니다.

## 사용 시점 / 사용하지 않는 경우

사용하는 경우:
- 계약 만료 2~6개월 전
- 확장 신호(사용량 한도 근접, 다른 부서 문의, 신규 용도, 계열사 확대)
- 갱신 시 단가·구성 변경 안내
- 갱신 위험(사용률 저조, 담당자 변경, 불만 접수)

사용하지 않는 경우:
- 신규 고객 발굴 → `sales-prospecting-sequence-ko`
- 정식 갱신 견적서·제안서 → `sales-proposal-writer-ko`
- 협상 중 가격 질문 → `sales-pricing-question-reply-ko`
- 다수 고객의 이탈 원인 분석 → `product-churn-win-loss-analysis-ko`

## 먼저 확인할 사항

1. 계약 사실: 만료일, 해지 통보 기한, 자동 갱신 조항, 현재 제품·수량, 현재 단가(부가세 별도 여부), 단가 인상 상한 조항 — 계약서·CRM에서 확인하고 추측하지 않습니다.
2. 사용·성과 데이터: 활성 사용자, 사용량, 문의·장애 이력, 도입 시 합의한 성과 지표와 달성 여부
3. 관계: 실무 담당자, 결재권자, 최근 변화(조직 개편, 임원 교체, 인수합병)
4. 확장 신호와 출처(고객성공 메모, 사용량 보고서, 고객 문의)
5. 영업 정책: 승인된 갱신 단가, 인상률, 다년 계약 옵션, 조건 양보 승인권자
6. 위험 신호: 불만, 만족도 조사 의견, 경쟁사 검토

## 작성 절차

1. **일정 수립(만료일 기준 역산)**
   - 만료 120~90일 전: 내부 계정 점검, 이해관계자 확인, 위험 표시
   - 90일 전: 성과 공유 미팅(정기 리뷰) 요청 — 고객의 차년도 예산 편성 시기와 맞춥니다.
   - 60일 전: 갱신 제안서·견적서(부가세 별도 표기)와 확장 옵션
   - 45~30일 전: 고객 품의·구매 절차, 필요 시 보안 재검토, 계약서 날인 일정
   - 해지 통보 기한 전: 계약 체결 또는 갱신 확정
2. **성과 정리**: 도입 목표에 연결된 검증된 성과 3~5개(예: "[기간] 동안 [건수] 처리" — 사용량 보고서 출처). 측정하지 않았다면 그 사실을 밝히고 지표를 제안합니다. 데이터 없이 투자 효과를 추정하지 않습니다.
3. **갱신 메일**
   - 성과 리뷰 미팅 요청: 다룰 내용, 30분, 참석 권장 대상
   - 갱신 제안 안내 메일: 성과 요약, 승인된 갱신 조건 그대로, 선택안, 일정
   - 단가 변경 안내(해당 시): 충분히 일찍, 이유와 계약상 근거, 통화 제안. 계약상 통보 의무 확인
4. **확장 메일**: 신호별로 대상 부서·담당자, 언급된 과제, 해결하는 제품·등급(문서화된 기능만), 작은 다음 단계(데모, 한 부서 시범 적용). 실무 담당자에게 다른 부서 소개를 요청합니다. 그룹사·계열사 확장은 레퍼런스로서의 가치도 큽니다.
5. **위험 고객 대응**: 문제를 솔직히 인정하고, 담당자가 정해진 개선 계획을 제시하며, 필요 시 고객지원 책임자·임원을 참여시킵니다. 할인부터 꺼내지 않습니다.
6. **CRM**: 갱신·확장 영업 기회 생성·수정(마감일, 승인 단가 기준 금액, 위험 메모)

## 결과물 형식

1. 갱신 현황: 만료일, 통보 기한, 자동 갱신 여부, 현재 연 계약 금액 `[CRM 기준]`, 위험도(상·중·하)와 근거
2. 일정 표: 날짜 | 활동 | 담당 | 고객 측 대상
3. 성과 정리(항목별 데이터 출처)
4. 메일 초안: 리뷰 요청, 갱신 안내, 단가 변경 안내, 확장 메일, 위험 대응 메일
5. CRM 업데이트 목록

## 자체 점검

- [ ] 계약 일자·통보 기한·단가 조건이 계약서·CRM에서 나왔는가
- [ ] 모든 성과 주장에 데이터 출처가 있는가
- [ ] 확장 제안이 실제 신호와 문서화된 기능에 근거하는가
- [ ] 단가 변경이 계약과 내부 승인에 따르는가
- [ ] 금액에 부가세 별도 여부가 표기되었는가
- [ ] 다음 단계와 날짜가 명확한가

## 한계

사용량·성과·가격·인상률·할인·기능을 지어내지 않습니다. 자동 갱신, 통보 기한, 단가 상한, 해지권 등 계약 해석은 법무 또는 영업관리와 확인합니다. 빈 부분은 `[확인 필요]`로 표시합니다.

5. **위험 고객 대응**: 문제를 솔직히 인정하고, 담당자가 정해진 개선 계획을 제시하며, 필요 시 고객지원 책임자·임원을 참여시킵니다. 할인부터 꺼내지 않습니다.
6. **CRM**: 갱신·확장 영업 기회 생성·수정(마감일, 승인 단가 기준 금액, 위험 메모)

1. 갱신 현황: 만료일, 통보 기한, 자동 갱신 여부, 현재 연 계약 금액 `[CRM 기준]`, 위험도(상·중·하)와 근거
2. 일정 표: 날짜 | 활동 | 담당 | 고객 측 대상

- [ ] 계약 일자·통보 기한·단가 조건이 계약서·CRM에서 나왔는가
- [ ] 모든 성과 주장에 데이터 출처가 있는가
- [ ] 확장 제안이 실제 신호와 문서화된 기능에 근거하는가
- [ ] 단가 변경이 계약과 내부 승인에 따르는가
- [ ] 금액에 부가세 별도 여부가 표기되었는가
- [ ] 다음 단계와 날짜가 명확한가

## 한계

사용량·성과·가격·인상률·할인·기능을 지어내지 않습니다. 자동 갱신, 통보 기한, 단가 상한, 해지권 등 계약 해석은 법무 또는 영업관리와 확인합니다. 빈 부분은 `[확인 필요]`로 표시합니다.

skills.body:
# Renewal और Expansion आउटरीच

Renewal आख़िरी हफ़्ते में नहीं, महीनों पहले जीता जाता है। भारत में कई कंपनियों का budget अप्रैल–मार्च financial year पर चलता है और नया PO जारी होने में समय लगता है, इसलिए value recap budget planning से पहले पहुँचना चाहिए। यह स्किल renewal timeline बनाती है, ग्राहक के असली परिणामों पर आधारित संदेश लिखती है, और बिना ज़रूरत के उत्पाद थोपे expansion के मौक़े पहचानती है।

## कब उपयोग करें / कब नहीं

उपयोग करें:
- Renewal 60–180 दिन दूर है।
- Expansion संकेत: usage सीमा के पास, नई टीम/branch/plant से माँग, group company।
- Renewal पर price या packaging बदलाव बताना है।
- Renewal जोखिम में (कम usage, champion गया, शिकायतें)।

उपयोग न करें:
- नए ग्राहक का prospecting → `sales-prospecting-sequence-hi`
- औपचारिक renewal quotation/प्रस्ताव → `sales-proposal-writer-hi`
- बातचीत में कीमत के सवाल → `sales-pricing-question-reply-hi`
- कई ग्राहकों के churn का विश्लेषण → `product-churn-win-loss-analysis-hi`

## पहले क्या पूछें

1. Contract तथ्य: end date, notice period, auto-renewal clause, मौजूदा products/licences, मौजूदा कीमत (GST अलग), price-increase cap — contract/CRM से पढ़ें, अनुमान नहीं।
2. Usage और परिणाम: active users, उपयोग, support tickets, तय success metrics और क्या वे पूरे हुए।
3. रिश्ता: champion, economic buyer, हाल के बदलाव (reorg, नया नेतृत्व, acquisition)।
4. Expansion संकेत और उनका स्रोत।
5. Commercial दिशानिर्देश: स्वीकृत renewal कीमत, uplift, multi-year विकल्प, रियायत कौन स्वीकृत करता है।
6. जोखिम संकेत: escalations, CSAT टिप्पणियाँ, प्रतिस्पर्धी evaluation।

## चरण

1. **Timeline (end date से पीछे)**:
   - T-120 से -90: आंतरिक account review, stakeholders की पुष्टि, जोखिम चिह्नित।
   - T-90: business review / value recap मीटिंग अनुरोध — ग्राहक की budget planning (अक्सर जनवरी–मार्च) से पहले।
   - T-60: renewal quotation (GST व SAC के साथ) और expansion विकल्प।
   - T-45 से -30: procurement, नया PO, vendor master अपडेट, ज़रूरत हो तो IT review।
   - Notice deadline से पहले: signed order / PO या पक्का renewal मार्ग।
2. **Value recap**: मूल लक्ष्यों से जुड़े 3–5 सत्यापित परिणाम (जैसे usage report से "[अवधि] में [संख्या] invoices प्रोसेस")। माप नहीं हुआ तो यह स्वीकार करें और metrics सुझाएँ; बिना डेटा ROI न बताएँ।
3. **Renewal संदेश**:
   - Business review अनुरोध: एजेंडा, 30 मिनट, किसे बुलाएँ।
   - Renewal cover ईमेल: value सार, स्वीकृत शर्तें बिल्कुल वैसी ही, विकल्प, तारीख़ें।
   - Price-change सूचना: जल्दी, कारण और contract आधार के साथ, कॉल का प्रस्ताव। भारत में मोलभाव सामान्य है — पहले से तय करें कि कौन-से स्वीकृत विकल्प (multi-year, advance payment) दे सकते हैं।
   - WhatsApp पर छोटा reminder केवल यदि ग्राहक से उसी चैनल पर बात होती है।
4. **Expansion संदेश**: हर संकेत के लिए — कौन, कौन-सी समस्या, कौन-सा product/tier (केवल दस्तावेज़ित फ़ीचर), छोटा अगला कदम (demo, एक branch पर pilot)। Champion से दूसरी टीमों/group companies का intro माँगें।
5. **जोखिम वाला अकाउंट**: समस्याएँ ईमानदारी से मानें, owners के साथ सुधार योजना, CS/support नेतृत्व और ज़रूरत हो तो executive sponsor। Discount से शुरुआत नहीं।
6. **CRM**: renewal और expansion opportunities बनाएँ/अपडेट करें — close date, स्वीकृत pricing पर amount, जोखिम नोट।

## आउटपुट फ़ॉर्मेट

1. Renewal स्नैपशॉट: end date, notice deadline, auto-renew हाँ/नहीं, मौजूदा ARR `[CRM से]`, जोखिम स्तर कारण सहित
2. Timeline तालिका: तारीख़ | कार्य | Owner | ग्राहक stakeholder
3. Value recap (हर बिंदु का डेटा स्रोत)
4. ड्राफ़्ट: review अनुरोध, renewal ईमेल, price-change सूचना, expansion ईमेल, जोखिम ईमेल
5. CRM अपडेट सूची

## गुणवत्ता जाँच

- [ ] Contract तारीख़ें, notice period, कीमत शर्तें contract/CRM से
- [ ] हर परिणाम का डेटा स्रोत; अनुमानित ROI तथ्य की तरह नहीं
- [ ] Expansion असली संकेत और दस्तावेज़ित क्षमता पर आधारित
- [ ] कीमत बदलाव contract और approval के अनुसार; GST अलग दिखाया
- [ ] जोखिम वाले अकाउंट को पहले सुधार योजना
- [ ] अगले कदम और तारीख़ें स्पष्ट

## सीमाएँ

Usage आँकड़े, परिणाम, कीमतें, uplift, discount या फ़ीचर न गढ़ें। Auto-renewal, notice, price cap, termination जैसे contract प्रश्न legal/deal desk से पुष्टि करें। कमियाँ `[जाँचें]` से चिह्नित करें।

skills.name: sales-business-case-roi
skills.description: Builds a buyer-owned business case for a deal: baseline from the customer's own numbers, value drivers (cost saved, revenue gained, risk reduced), total cost of ownership from the approved quote, ROI, payback and NPV with formulas shown, conservative/expected scenarios and sensitivity, plus a one-page CFO summary. Use when a rep says 'build an ROI for Example Co.', 'the CFO wants a business case', 'justify the price', 'payback period for this deal' or 'help my champion get budget approved'.
skills.body:
# Business Case & ROI

A credible business case uses the buyer's numbers, shows every calculation, and is conservative enough that finance cannot easily knock it down. The aim is a document your champion presents as their own recommendation — not a vendor ROI calculator with inflated defaults.

## When to use / when not to use

Use when:
- An economic buyer or finance asks "what's the return?"
- The champion needs a budget request or capital approval.
- Price objections suggest value isn't established.

Do not use when:
- You haven't gathered baseline data yet — run discovery first (see `sales-call-prep-brief`).
- You need the whole proposal → `sales-proposal-writer` (include this as a section).
- Price/discount questions → `sales-pricing-question-reply`.
- Your own company's unit economics → `founder-unit-economics`.

## What to ask for first

1. Buyer-provided baseline: volumes, time spent, headcount/hourly loaded cost, error rates, current tool costs, revenue metrics — each with who provided it and when.
2. The 2–4 outcomes the buyer cares about most.
3. Evidence for improvement assumptions: buyer's pilot results, documented benchmarks from your approved case studies, or the buyer's own estimate. Never default to marketing claims without source.
4. Costs: approved quote (subscription, services, term), customer internal costs (implementation time, training, change management), costs avoided (retired tools).
5. Finance conventions: evaluation horizon (often 3 years), discount rate/hurdle rate, whether to include soft savings.

## Steps

1. **Baseline table.** Metric | Current value | Source | Date. Mark missing values `[NEEDS DATA]`; do not fill with guesses.
2. **Value drivers.** For each: mechanism ("automated matching removes manual reconciliation steps"), formula, and assumption.
   - Time savings = hours saved × loaded hourly cost × adoption rate. State whether time is redeployed (soft) or reduces spend (hard).
   - Cost avoidance = retired tool cost + avoided hires (only if the buyer confirms hiring plans).
   - Revenue impact = volume × conversion/price change × margin (use margin, not revenue).
   - Risk reduction = probability × impact (only with buyer-supported estimates).
3. **Costs (TCO).** Year-by-year: subscription, services, internal effort, minus avoided costs.
4. **Scenarios.** Conservative (lower improvement, slower adoption ramp) and expected. Avoid an "optimistic" case unless finance asks.
5. **Financial metrics (show the math).**
   - ROI = (total benefits − total costs) / total costs over the horizon.
   - Payback (months) = upfront + cumulative costs ÷ monthly net benefit, found where cumulative net benefit turns positive.
   - NPV = Σ (net benefit_t / (1 + r)^t) − initial cost, using the buyer's discount rate.
   - Worked example (placeholder data): 2,000 hours saved/yr × $50 loaded × 70% adoption = $70,000/yr benefit; cost $40,000/yr → net $30,000/yr; 3-year ROI = (210,000 − 120,000)/120,000 = 75%.
6. **Sensitivity.** Which assumption flips the decision? Show the break-even value (e.g., "ROI stays positive if adoption ≥ 40%").
7. **Non-financial benefits.** List separately (compliance, employee experience) without assigning dollar values unless the buyer does.
8. **CFO one-pager.** Decision requested, investment, expected and conservative ROI/payback, key assumptions, risks and mitigations.
9. **Validate with the buyer.** Review assumptions with the champion and ideally finance before presenting; record their edits.

## Output format

1. One-page summary.
2. Baseline table with sources.
3. Value driver table: Driver | Formula | Inputs | Conservative | Expected | Hard/soft.
4. Cost table by year.
5. Results: ROI, payback, NPV per scenario with calculations shown.
6. Sensitivity table and break-even points.
7. Assumptions & open data requests.

## Quality checks

- [ ] Every input has a source; buyer numbers preferred over vendor benchmarks.
- [ ] Formulas and arithmetic shown and re-checked.
- [ ] Margin used for revenue impact; hard vs soft savings separated.
- [ ] Conservative scenario still credible; break-even identified.
- [ ] Costs include the buyer's internal effort.
- [ ] Champion/finance reviewed assumptions.

## Limits

Never invent baselines, benchmark results, customer outcomes, prices or ROI figures; missing inputs are `[NEEDS DATA]` or `[VERIFY]`. A business case is an estimate, not a guarantee — avoid wording that promises outcomes, and do not put ROI commitments into contracts without legal approval.

skills.body:
# 투자 효과 분석 (비즈니스 케이스)

신뢰받는 투자 효과 분석은 고객의 수치를 쓰고, 모든 계산을 보여 주며, 재무팀이 쉽게 반박할 수 없을 만큼 보수적입니다. 한국 기업에서는 실무자가 이 자료를 품의서의 "도입 효과" 항목에 그대로 옮기는 경우가 많으므로, 실무자가 자기 이름으로 설명할 수 있는 수준이어야 합니다.

## 사용 시점 / 사용하지 않는 경우

사용하는 경우:
- 결재권자나 재무팀이 "효과가 얼마인가"를 묻는 경우
- 실무자가 예산 요청·품의를 준비하는 경우
- 가격 반론이 가치 설명 부족에서 비롯된 경우

사용하지 않는 경우:
- 기준 수치를 아직 모름 → 먼저 니즈 파악(`sales-call-prep-brief-ko`)
- 제안서 전체 → `sales-proposal-writer-ko`(이 분석을 한 장으로 포함)
- 가격·할인 문의 → `sales-pricing-question-reply-ko`
- 당사 수익 구조 분석 → `founder-unit-economics-ko`

## 먼저 확인할 사항

1. 고객 제공 기준 수치: 처리량, 소요 시간, 인원·인건비(1인당 연간 부대비용 포함), 오류율, 현재 솔루션 비용, 매출 지표 — 제공자와 일자 포함
2. 고객이 가장 중시하는 성과 2~4개
3. 개선 가정의 근거: 고객 시범 적용 결과, 승인된 사례의 실적, 고객 자체 추정. 출처 없는 마케팅 수치는 쓰지 않습니다.
4. 비용: 승인 견적(구독료, 구축비, 계약 기간, 부가세 별도), 고객 내부 비용(구축 참여 시간, 교육), 대체로 절감되는 기존 비용
5. 재무 기준: 분석 기간(보통 3년), 할인율, 간접 효과 포함 여부, 내부 품의 양식

## 작성 절차

1. **기준 수치 표**: 지표 | 현재 값 | 출처 | 일자. 없는 값은 `[데이터 필요]`로 두고 추측으로 채우지 않습니다.
2. **효과 요인**: 요인별 작동 원리, 계산식, 가정
   - 시간 절감 = 절감 시간 × 시간당 인건비 × 활용률. 인력 재배치(간접 효과)인지 실제 비용 감소(직접 효과)인지 구분합니다. 한국 기업은 인력 감축보다 재배치를 기대하는 경우가 많으므로 대개 간접 효과입니다.
   - 비용 회피 = 대체되는 기존 솔루션 비용 + 회피되는 채용(고객이 채용 계획을 확인한 경우만)
   - 매출 효과 = 물량 × 전환·단가 변화 × 이익률(매출이 아니라 이익 기준)
   - 위험 감소 = 발생 확률 × 영향(고객이 동의한 추정치만)
3. **총소유비용**: 연도별 구독료, 구축비, 내부 투입, 절감되는 기존 비용 차감
4. **시나리오**: 보수(낮은 개선율, 느린 정착)와 기본. 재무팀 요청이 없으면 낙관 시나리오는 생략합니다.
5. **재무 지표(계산 과정 표시)**
   - ROI = (총효과 − 총비용) ÷ 총비용
   - 회수 기간 = 누적 순효과가 0을 넘는 시점(개월)
   - NPV = Σ 순효과ₜ ÷ (1 + r)ᵗ − 초기 비용(고객 할인율 사용)
   - 예시(가상 데이터): 연 2,000시간 절감 × 시간당 5만 원 × 활용률 70% = 연 7,000만 원; 비용 연 4,000만 원 → 순효과 연 3,000만 원; 3년 ROI = (2억 1,000만 − 1억 2,000만) ÷ 1억 2,000만 = 75%
6. **민감도**: 결론을 뒤집는 가정과 손익분기 값("활용률 40% 이상이면 ROI 양수")
7. **정성 효과**: 규정 준수, 업무 만족도 등은 금액 없이 별도 나열
8. **임원용 1쪽 요약**: 요청 사항, 투자 금액(부가세 별도), 기본·보수 ROI와 회수 기간, 핵심 가정, 위험과 대응
9. **고객 검증**: 실무자(가능하면 재무 담당)와 가정을 검토하고 수정 내역을 기록합니다.

## 결과물 형식

1. 1쪽 요약(품의서 첨부용)
2. 기준 수치 표(출처 포함)
3. 효과 요인 표: 요인 | 계산식 | 입력값 | 보수 | 기본 | 직접·간접
4. 연도별 비용 표
5. 시나리오별 ROI·회수 기간·NPV와 계산 과정
6. 민감도 표, 손익분기 값
7. 가정 목록과 추가 데이터 요청

## 자체 점검

- [ ] 모든 입력값에 출처가 있고 고객 수치를 우선했는가
- [ ] 계산식과 산출 과정을 보이고 재검산했는가
- [ ] 매출 효과에 이익률을 썼고 직접·간접 효과를 구분했는가
- [ ] 보수 시나리오도 설득력이 있고 손익분기점을 제시했는가
- [ ] 고객 내부 투입 비용을 포함했는가
- [ ] 금액 단위(원, 만 원, 억 원)와 부가세 기준이 일관되는가

## 한계

기준 수치·벤치마크·고객 성과·가격·ROI를 지어내지 않으며 없는 값은 `[데이터 필요]` 또는 `[확인 필요]`로 표시합니다. 투자 효과 분석은 추정이며 보장이 아닙니다. 성과 보장 표현을 쓰지 않고, 계약서에 효과 보장을 넣으려면 법무 승인이 필요합니다.

   - 회수 기간 = 누적 순효과가 0을 넘는 시점(개월)
   - NPV = Σ 순효과ₜ ÷ (1 + r)ᵗ − 초기 비용(고객 할인율 사용)
   - 예시(가상 데이터): 연 2,000시간 절감 × 시간당 5만 원 × 활용률 70% = 연 7,000만 원; 비용 연 4,000만 원 → 순효과 연 3,000만 원; 3년 ROI = (2억 1,000만 − 1억 2,000만) ÷ 1억 2,000만 = 75%
6. **민감도**: 결론을 뒤집는 가정과 손익분기 값("활용률 40% 이상이면 ROI 양수")
7. **정성 효과**: 규정 준수, 업무 만족도 등은 금액 없이 별도 나열
8. **임원용 1쪽 요약**: 요청 사항, 투자 금액(부가세 별도), 기본·보수 ROI와 회수 기간, 핵심 가정, 위험과 대응
9. **고객 검증**: 실무자(가능하면 재무 담당)와 가정을 검토하고 수정 내역을 기록합니다.

## 결과물 형식

1. 1쪽 요약(품의서 첨부용)
2. 기준 수치 표(출처 포함)
3. 효과 요인 표: 요인 | 계산식 | 입력값 | 보수 | 기본 | 직접·간접
4. 연도별 비용 표
5. 시나리오별 ROI·회수 기간·NPV와 계산 과정
6. 민감도 표, 손익분기 값
7. 가정 목록과 추가 데이터 요청

## 자체 점검

- [ ] 모든 입력값에 출처가 있고 고객 수치를 우선했는가
- [ ] 계산식과 산출 과정을 보이고 재검산했는가
- [ ] 매출 효과에 이익률을 썼고 직접·간접 효과를 구분했는가
- [ ] 보수 시나리오도 설득력이 있고 손익분기점을 제시했는가
- [ ] 고객 내부 투입 비용을 포함했는가
- [ ] 금액 단위(원, 만 원, 억 원)와 부가세 기준이 일관되는가

## 한계

기준 수치·벤치마크·고객 성과·가격·ROI를 지어내지 않으며 없는 값은 `[데이터 필요]` 또는 `[확인 필요]`로 표시합니다. 투자 효과 분석은 추정이며 보장이 아닙니다. 성과 보장 표현을 쓰지 않고, 계약서에 효과 보장을 넣으려면 법무 승인이 필요합니다.

skills.body:
# Business Case और ROI

विश्वसनीय business case ग्राहक के आँकड़े इस्तेमाल करता है, हर गणना दिखाता है और इतना conservative होता है कि finance आसानी से न गिरा सके। भारत में कीमत पर मोलभाव आम है; ठोस business case बातचीत को "discount कितना" से हटाकर "value कितनी" पर लाता है। लक्ष्य ऐसा दस्तावेज़ है जिसे champion अपनी सिफ़ारिश की तरह पेश कर सके।

## कब उपयोग करें / कब नहीं

उपयोग करें:
- Economic buyer, मालिक या finance पूछे "return क्या है?"
- Champion को budget/capex approval चाहिए।
- कीमत पर आपत्ति बताती है कि value स्थापित नहीं हुई।

उपयोग न करें:
- Baseline डेटा अभी नहीं है → पहले discovery (`sales-call-prep-brief-hi`)
- पूरा proposal → `sales-proposal-writer-hi` (इसे एक section बनाएँ)
- कीमत/discount सवाल → `sales-pricing-question-reply-hi`
- अपनी कंपनी की unit economics → `founder-unit-economics-hi`

## पहले क्या पूछें

1. ग्राहक का baseline: volumes, लगा समय, headcount और loaded cost (CTC आधार), error rates, मौजूदा tool लागत, राजस्व metrics — किसने और कब दिया।
2. ग्राहक के लिए सबसे अहम 2–4 परिणाम।
3. सुधार की मान्यताओं का प्रमाण: ग्राहक का pilot, स्वीकृत case study के आँकड़े, या ग्राहक का अपना अनुमान।
4. लागत: स्वीकृत quote (subscription, services, अवधि, GST अलग), ग्राहक की आंतरिक लागत (implementation समय, training), बचने वाली लागत।
5. Finance मानक: अवधि (अक्सर 3 साल), discount rate, soft savings शामिल हों या नहीं। GST input credit लागत गणना बदल सकता है — finance से पूछें `[जाँचें]`।

## चरण

1. **Baseline तालिका**: Metric | मौजूदा मान | स्रोत | तारीख़। ग़ायब मान `[डेटा चाहिए]` — अनुमान से न भरें।
2. **Value drivers**: हर driver का तंत्र, सूत्र, मान्यता।
   - समय बचत = बचे घंटे × loaded hourly cost × adoption rate; बताएँ कि समय दूसरे काम में लगेगा (soft) या ख़र्च घटेगा (hard)।
   - लागत बचाव = हटने वाले tool की लागत + टली हुई भर्ती (केवल यदि ग्राहक भर्ती योजना की पुष्टि करे)।
   - राजस्व प्रभाव = volume × conversion/price बदलाव × margin (revenue नहीं, margin)।
   - जोखिम में कमी = संभावना × प्रभाव (ग्राहक-समर्थित अनुमान से)।
3. **TCO**: साल-दर-साल subscription, services, आंतरिक प्रयास, घटाएँ बचने वाली लागत।
4. **Scenarios**: conservative (कम सुधार, धीमा adoption) और expected।
5. **वित्तीय metrics (गणना दिखाएँ)**:
   - ROI = (कुल लाभ − कुल लागत) ÷ कुल लागत
   - Payback = वह महीना जब संचयी शुद्ध लाभ धनात्मक हो
   - NPV = Σ शुद्ध लाभ_t ÷ (1 + r)^t − प्रारंभिक लागत
   - उदाहरण (काल्पनिक डेटा): 2,000 घंटे/वर्ष × ₹800 loaded × 70% adoption = ₹11,20,000/वर्ष लाभ; लागत ₹6,00,000/वर्ष → शुद्ध ₹5,20,000/वर्ष; 3-वर्ष ROI = (33,60,000 − 18,00,000) ÷ 18,00,000 ≈ 87%
6. **Sensitivity**: कौन-सी मान्यता निर्णय पलट देती है; break-even मान ("adoption ≥ 40% पर भी ROI धनात्मक")।
7. **ग़ैर-वित्तीय लाभ**: compliance, कर्मचारी अनुभव — अलग सूची, बिना रुपये मूल्य के जब तक ग्राहक न दे।
8. **एक-पेज सार**: माँगा गया निर्णय, निवेश (GST अलग), expected व conservative ROI/payback, मुख्य मान्यताएँ, जोखिम। SME मालिक के लिए सरल भाषा और लाख/करोड़ में राशि।
9. **ग्राहक से सत्यापन**: champion और यदि संभव हो finance के साथ मान्यताओं की समीक्षा; उनके बदलाव दर्ज करें।

## आउटपुट फ़ॉर्मेट

1. एक-पेज सार
2. Baseline तालिका (स्रोत सहित)
3. Value driver तालिका: Driver | सूत्र | Inputs | Conservative | Expected | Hard/soft
4. साल-वार लागत तालिका
5. हर scenario के ROI, payback, NPV गणना सहित
6. Sensitivity और break-even
7. मान्यताएँ और डेटा अनुरोध

## गुणवत्ता जाँच

- [ ] हर input का स्रोत; ग्राहक के आँकड़े vendor benchmarks से पहले
- [ ] सूत्र और गणना दिखाई और दोबारा जाँची
- [ ] राजस्व प्रभाव में margin; hard/soft अलग
- [ ] Conservative scenario विश्वसनीय; break-even पहचाना
- [ ] ग्राहक की आंतरिक लागत शामिल
- [ ] राशि इकाई (₹, लाख, करोड़) और GST आधार एकरूप

## सीमाएँ

Baseline, benchmark, ग्राहक परिणाम, कीमतें या ROI न गढ़ें; ग़ायब inputs `[डेटा चाहिए]` या `[जाँचें]`। Business case अनुमान है, गारंटी नहीं — परिणामों का वादा करने वाली भाषा न लिखें; contract में ROI प्रतिबद्धता legal की मंज़ूरी के बिना नहीं।

skills.name: sales-deck-storyline
skills.description: Builds the storyline and slide-by-slide outline for a customer-facing sales deck — first-meeting pitch, tailored demo narrative, executive briefing or proposal presentation — with headline-style slide titles, the buyer's problem before the product, approved proof, speaker notes and a clear ask. Use when a rep says 'build a deck for my meeting with Example Co.', 'tailor our pitch deck to this account', 'outline the demo story', 'exec presentation for the CFO' or 'our deck is too product-heavy'.
skills.body:
# Sales Deck Storyline

Most sales decks fail because they open with the vendor and close with a logo wall. This skill builds a buyer-first narrative: their world, the change that makes the problem urgent, what good looks like, how you get them there, proof, and a specific next step. It produces an outline with headlines and speaker notes, ready to drop into your company template.

## When to use / when not to use

Use when:
- Preparing a first-meeting, discovery-to-demo, executive or proposal presentation.
- Tailoring the corporate deck to an account, industry or persona.
- Restructuring a deck that is too long or feature-led.

Do not use when:
- A fundraising pitch → `founder-pitch-deck-storyline`.
- A written proposal document → `sales-proposal-writer`.
- The quantified value model itself → `sales-business-case-roi` (the deck can summarize it).
- Pre-call research on the account → `sales-call-prep-brief`.

## What to ask for first

1. Meeting type, audience (names, roles, seniority), length, in person or virtual.
2. What you know about their situation (research brief, discovery notes) and what's still assumed.
3. Goal of the meeting: the one decision or next step you want.
4. Approved assets: corporate deck, product screenshots, case studies, customer logos cleared for use, analyst quotes with license.
5. Competitive context, if known, and what the buyer already believes.
6. Your company's template and slide count limit.

## Steps

1. **Set the single message.** One sentence the audience should repeat afterward: "[Company] can [outcome] by [approach] without [main risk]."
2. **Choose the arc by meeting type.**
   - First meeting: shift in their world → cost of standing still → what winners do → how we help → proof → discovery questions → next step.
   - Demo narrative: their 2–3 priority use cases → "day in the life" before/after → only features that serve those use cases → recap → next step.
   - Executive briefing: their strategic goal → risk/opportunity → options (including doing nothing) → recommendation → investment and plan → decision.

3. **Write headline titles.** Each slide title is a full-sentence takeaway ("Manual reconciliation is costing your team ~9 days each close" — with source), not a label ("Challenges").

6. **Build in interaction.** Add discovery checkpoints ("Is this how it works for you?") after the problem slides; for executives, leave half the time for discussion.
7. **Speaker notes.** For each slide: the point, the transition, a question to ask, and the evidence source.
8. **End with the ask.** Last content slide proposes the specific next step with date and owners.

## Output format

1. Single message and meeting goal.
2. Slide table:

| # | Headline title | Content / visual | Proof & source | Speaker note / question |
|---|---|---|---|---|

3. Appendix slide list.
4. Assumptions to validate in the meeting (marked `[VERIFY]`).
5. Tailoring checklist for the account (names, industry examples, their terminology).

## Quality checks

- [ ] Buyer's problem appears before the product.
- [ ] Every title is a takeaway sentence; the titles alone tell the story.
- [ ] Every claim has a source or is marked as an assumption.
- [ ] Logos, quotes, case studies and analyst material are cleared for use.
- [ ] Slide count fits the time; detail moved to appendix.
- [ ] The final slide asks for one specific next step.

## Limits

Never invent features, metrics, ROI, customer logos, testimonials or security certifications. Roadmap content requires product approval and a forward-looking disclaimer. Third-party data and analyst content must respect licensing.

skills.body:
# 영업 자료 스토리라인

대부분의 회사소개서는 회사 연혁으로 시작해 로고 나열로 끝납니다. 이 스킬은 고객 중심 흐름 — 고객의 환경 변화, 과제가 시급한 이유, 바람직한 모습, 해결 방법, 근거, 구체적 다음 단계 — 으로 장표 구성과 헤드메시지, 발표 스크립트를 만듭니다. 한국 기업 보고 문화에 맞춰 각 장표 상단에 결론을 먼저 쓰고, 임원용은 짧게, 실무용은 상세 부록을 둡니다.

## 사용 시점 / 사용하지 않는 경우

사용하는 경우:
- 첫 미팅 소개, 데모, 임원 보고, 제안 발표(PT) 준비
- 회사 표준 소개서를 특정 고객·업종·직무에 맞게 수정
- 너무 길거나 기능 나열식인 자료 재구성

사용하지 않는 경우:
- 투자 유치용 IR 자료 → `founder-pitch-deck-storyline-ko`
- 문서형 제안서 → `sales-proposal-writer-ko`
- 투자 효과 산정 자체 → `sales-business-case-roi-ko`(요약만 장표에 반영)
- 미팅 전 고객 조사 → `sales-call-prep-brief-ko`

## 먼저 확인할 사항

1. 미팅 종류, 참석자(이름·직책·직급), 시간, 대면·화상 여부
2. 고객 현황 파악 정도(조사 자료, 미팅 메모)와 아직 추정인 부분
3. 미팅 목표: 얻고자 하는 결정 또는 다음 단계 하나
4. 승인 자료: 표준 소개서, 화면 캡처, 사례, 사용 승인된 고객사 로고, 인증서
5. 경쟁 상황과 고객이 이미 가진 인식
6. 회사 템플릿과 장표 수 제한, 출력 배포 여부(인쇄본을 선호하는 임원도 있습니다)

## 작성 절차

1. **핵심 메시지 한 문장**: "[고객사]는 [방법]으로 [주요 위험] 없이 [성과]를 얻을 수 있습니다."
2. **미팅 유형별 흐름**
   - 첫 미팅: 업계·고객 환경 변화 → 현상 유지의 비용 → 앞선 기업의 방식 → 당사의 지원 방식 → 사례 → 확인 질문 → 다음 단계
   - 데모: 고객 우선 과제 2~3개 → 업무 전·후 비교 → 그 과제에 필요한 기능만 → 요약 → 다음 단계
   - 임원 보고: 전략 목표 → 위험·기회 → 대안(현상 유지 포함) → 권고안 → 투자·일정 → 의사결정 요청
   - 제안 발표(PT): 합의된 과제 → 제안 범위 → 추진 일정 → 기대 효과 → 견적 요약(부가세 별도) → 계약까지 일정
3. **헤드메시지**: 장표 제목을 "현황" 같은 명사 대신 결론 문장으로("수작업 대사로 월 마감마다 약 9일이 소요되고 있습니다" + 출처).
4. **분량**: 첫 미팅 8~12장, 임원 5~8장, 데모 6~10단계. 제품 상세·보안·회사 연혁은 부록으로.
5. **근거 배치**: 주요 주장마다 관련 사례 하나. 한국 고객은 동종 업계·유사 규모 레퍼런스를 중시하므로 사용 승인된 사례를 우선 배치하고, 익명 사례는 익명임을 표시합니다.
6. **질문 삽입**: 과제 장표 뒤에 확인 질문("귀사도 이런 방식으로 진행하십니까?"). 임원 보고는 시간의 절반을 논의에 남깁니다.
7. **발표 스크립트**: 장표별 요지, 연결 멘트, 질문, 근거 출처
8. **마지막 장표**: 날짜와 담당이 있는 구체적 다음 단계 제안

## 결과물 형식

1. 핵심 메시지와 미팅 목표
2. 장표 구성표

| 번호 | 헤드메시지 | 내용·시각 자료 | 근거·출처 | 발표 스크립트·질문 |
|---|---|---|---|---|

3. 부록 장표 목록
4. 미팅에서 확인할 가정(`[확인 필요]`)
5. 고객 맞춤 점검표(고객사명, 업종 사례, 고객 용어)

## 자체 점검

- [ ] 제품보다 고객 과제가 먼저 나오는가
- [ ] 헤드메시지만 읽어도 이야기가 이어지는가
- [ ] 모든 주장에 출처가 있거나 가정으로 표시되었는가
- [ ] 로고·사례·인용·인증서 사용 승인을 받았는가
- [ ] 시간에 맞는 분량이고 상세는 부록에 있는가
- [ ] 마지막에 구체적 요청이 하나 있는가

## 한계

기능·수치·투자 효과·고객사 로고·추천사·보안 인증을 지어내지 않습니다. 로드맵은 제품팀 승인과 "향후 계획이며 변경될 수 있음" 문구가 필요합니다. 외부 리포트·통계는 이용 조건을 지킵니다.

# Sales Deck Storyline

ज़्यादातर sales decks कंपनी के इतिहास से शुरू होकर logo wall पर ख़त्म होते हैं। यह स्किल ग्राहक-पहले कहानी बनाती है: उनकी दुनिया, समस्या अभी क्यों ज़रूरी है, अच्छा परिणाम कैसा दिखता है, हम वहाँ कैसे पहुँचाते हैं, प्रमाण, और एक ठोस अगला कदम। भारतीय संदर्भ में SME मालिकों के लिए छोटी, सरल और हिंदी/हिंग्लिश में भी समझ आने वाली deck, और enterprise CXOs के लिए data-आधारित संक्षिप्त deck बेहतर काम करती है।

## कब उपयोग करें / कब नहीं

उपयोग करें:
- पहली मीटिंग, demo, executive या proposal प्रस्तुति की तैयारी।
- Corporate deck को अकाउंट, उद्योग या persona के अनुसार बदलना।
- बहुत लंबी या फ़ीचर-भरी deck को दोबारा गढ़ना।

उपयोग न करें:
- निवेशक pitch → `founder-pitch-deck-storyline-hi`
- लिखित proposal → `sales-proposal-writer-hi`
- ROI मॉडल स्वयं → `sales-business-case-roi-hi` (deck में केवल सार)
- मीटिंग से पहले अकाउंट रिसर्च → `sales-call-prep-brief-hi`

## पहले क्या पूछें

1. मीटिंग प्रकार, दर्शक (नाम, पद, वरिष्ठता), अवधि, व्यक्तिगत या वर्चुअल।
2. उनकी स्थिति के बारे में क्या पता है (research brief, discovery नोट्स) और क्या अनुमान है।
3. मीटिंग का लक्ष्य: एक निर्णय या अगला कदम।
4. स्वीकृत सामग्री: corporate deck, screenshots, case studies, उपयोग-स्वीकृत logos।
5. प्रतिस्पर्धी संदर्भ और ग्राहक की मौजूदा धारणा।
6. कंपनी template, स्लाइड सीमा, भाषा (अंग्रेज़ी/हिंदी)।

## चरण

1. **एक मुख्य संदेश**: "[कंपनी] [तरीक़े] से [मुख्य जोखिम] के बिना [परिणाम] पा सकती है।"
2. **मीटिंग प्रकार के अनुसार कहानी**:
   - पहली मीटिंग: उद्योग/उनकी दुनिया में बदलाव → वैसे ही चलते रहने की लागत → आगे रहने वाली कंपनियाँ क्या करती हैं → हम कैसे मदद करते हैं → प्रमाण → discovery सवाल → अगला कदम
   - Demo: उनके 2–3 प्राथमिक use cases → पहले/बाद का "एक दिन" → केवल वे फ़ीचर जो इन use cases की सेवा करें → सार → अगला कदम
   - Executive/मालिक briefing: रणनीतिक लक्ष्य → जोखिम/अवसर → विकल्प (कुछ न करना भी) → सिफ़ारिश → निवेश और योजना → निर्णय
   - Proposal प्रस्तुति: तय समस्या → समाधान व scope → योजना → value → commercials सार (GST अलग) → PO तक का रास्ता
3. **Headline titles**: हर स्लाइड का शीर्षक पूरा takeaway वाक्य ("Manual reconciliation में हर month-end ~9 दिन लगते हैं" + स्रोत), न कि "Challenges" जैसा लेबल।
4. **संक्षिप्त रखें**: पहली मीटिंग 8–12 स्लाइड, executive 5–8, demo 6–10 beats; product गहराई, security, कंपनी इतिहास appendix में।
5. **प्रमाण सोच-समझकर**: हर बड़े दावे के लिए एक प्रासंगिक case study; भारतीय ग्राहक उसी उद्योग/शहर के reference को महत्व देते हैं — केवल स्वीकृत नाम, अन्यथा "एक अग्रणी [उद्योग] कंपनी" लिखें।
6. **बातचीत के बिंदु**: समस्या स्लाइड्स के बाद सवाल ("क्या आपके यहाँ भी ऐसा ही होता है?"); senior लोगों के लिए आधा समय चर्चा को।
7. **Speaker notes**: हर स्लाइड — मुख्य बात, transition, सवाल, प्रमाण स्रोत।
8. **Ask से अंत**: अंतिम स्लाइड पर तारीख़ और owners के साथ अगला कदम।

## आउटपुट फ़ॉर्मेट

1. मुख्य संदेश और मीटिंग लक्ष्य
2. स्लाइड तालिका:

| # | Headline title | सामग्री/visual | प्रमाण व स्रोत | Speaker note/सवाल |
|---|---|---|---|---|

3. Appendix स्लाइड सूची
4. मीटिंग में पुष्टि करने वाली मान्यताएँ (`[जाँचें]`)
5. Tailoring चेकलिस्ट (नाम, उद्योग उदाहरण, उनकी शब्दावली)

## गुणवत्ता जाँच

- [ ] ग्राहक की समस्या product से पहले
- [ ] सिर्फ़ titles पढ़कर कहानी समझ आती है
- [ ] हर दावे का स्रोत या "मान्यता" लेबल
- [ ] Logos, quotes, case studies उपयोग के लिए स्वीकृत
- [ ] स्लाइड संख्या समय के अनुरूप
- [ ] अंत में एक ठोस अनुरोध

## सीमाएँ

फ़ीचर, metrics, ROI, ग्राहक logos, testimonials या security प्रमाणन न गढ़ें। Roadmap के लिए product की मंज़ूरी और "भविष्य की योजना, बदल सकती है" disclaimer ज़रूरी। तृतीय-पक्ष डेटा की licensing का पालन करें।

skills.body:
# Mutual Action Plan

A mutual action plan turns "we hope to close this quarter" into a shared, dated list of steps the buyer agrees to. It starts from the buyer's own reason for a date (a go-live, a budget deadline, a contract expiring) and works backward, surfacing the security, legal and procurement steps that usually cause slippage.

## When to use / when not to use

Use when:
- The buyer has agreed a problem is worth solving and is evaluating a solution.
- Forecasting a deal and needing evidence the close date is real.
- A deal keeps slipping and the steps or owners are unclear.

Do not use when:
- Qualification is still unclear → `sales-deal-qualification-meddicc` first.
- You need the proposal document → `sales-proposal-writer`.
- Internal forecast write-up → `sales-forecast-commit-summary`.

## What to ask for first

1. The buyer's compelling event and target date (go-live, renewal of incumbent, budget expiry, regulatory deadline) and why it matters.
2. Decision process: who evaluates, who signs, approval thresholds, board/committee dates.
3. Paper process: security review, legal review (whose paper), procurement/vendor onboarding, PO requirement, typical durations.
4. Remaining evaluation steps: demo, technical validation, references, pilot.
5. Your internal steps: deal desk approvals, legal turnaround, implementation kickoff capacity.
6. Buyer contacts who can own steps.

## Steps

1. **Anchor on the buyer's goal.** Write the "why this date" in their words at the top. If there is no compelling event, say so — the plan's dates are then soft and the forecast should reflect it.
2. **List all steps from now to value.** Include post-signature steps (kickoff, go-live) so the plan is about their success, not just your signature.
   - Evaluation: technical validation, demo to wider team, references.
   - Business: business case review, budget confirmation, executive sponsor meeting.
   - Risk: security questionnaire, SOC 2 report review under NDA, data processing agreement, legal redlines.
   - Commercial: proposal, negotiation, final approval, signature, PO/vendor setup.
   - Launch: kickoff, configuration, training, go-live.
3. **Work backward from the target date.** Use realistic durations from the buyer (e.g., "security review takes 3–4 weeks here"). Flag where the critical path is already late.
4. **Assign owners on both sides.** Each step: buyer owner, seller owner, due date, status. Steps without a buyer owner are a risk.
5. **Identify dependencies and risks.** E.g., "legal can't start until security approves", "procurement requires vendor registration 10 business days before PO". Add mitigations.
6. **Draft the share email.** Position it as "here's how I understood your process — what did I get wrong?" and invite edits. A plan the buyer edits is a plan the buyer owns.
7. **Set the review cadence.** Weekly 15-minute check-in or update in a shared doc; update CRM next steps and close date when the plan moves.

## Output format

```
# Mutual Action Plan: Example Co. + [Your company]
Goal: [buyer outcome] by [date] because [compelling event]
Decision makers: ... | Signer: ... | Approval steps: ...

| # | Step | Buyer owner | Our owner | Due | Depends on | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

Risks & mitigations
Open questions
Last updated: [date] — shared with [names]
```
Plus the cover email to the champion.

## Quality checks

- [ ] The target date is tied to a buyer reason, or marked as soft.
- [ ] Security, legal, procurement and signature steps are included with realistic durations.
- [ ] Every step has a buyer owner and date.
- [ ] Critical path and dependencies are visible.
- [ ] The buyer has been asked to correct the plan.
- [ ] CRM close date matches the plan.

## Limits

Do not invent buyer process steps, durations, approvers or dates — ask, and mark assumptions `[VERIFY]`. A mutual action plan is not a contract; avoid language implying commitment to purchase. Legal terms raised during the plan go to legal review.

- Qualification is still unclear → `sales-deal-qualification-meddicc` first.
- You need the proposal document → `sales-proposal-writer`.
- Internal forecast write-up → `sales-forecast-commit-summary`.

## What to ask for first

1. The buyer's compelling event and target date (go-live, renewal of incumbent, budget expiry, regulatory deadline) and why it matters.
2. Decision process: who evaluates, who signs, approval thresholds, board/committee dates.
3. Paper process: security review, legal review (whose paper), procurement/vendor onboarding, PO requirement, typical durations.
4. Remaining evaluation steps: demo, technical validation, references, pilot.
5. Your internal steps: deal desk approvals, legal turnaround, implementation kickoff capacity.
6. Buyer contacts who can own steps.

## Steps

1. **Anchor on the buyer's goal.** Write the "why this date" in their words at the top. If there is no compelling event, say so — the plan's dates are then soft and the forecast should reflect it.
2. **List all steps from now to value.** Include post-signature steps (kickoff, go-live) so the plan is about their success, not just your signature.
   - Evaluation: technical validation, demo to wider team, references.
   - Business: business case review, budget confirmation, executive sponsor meeting.
   - Risk: security questionnaire, SOC 2 report review under NDA, data processing agreement, legal redlines.
   - Commercial: proposal, negotiation, final approval, signature, PO/vendor setup.
   - Launch: kickoff, configuration, training, go-live.
3. **Work backward from the target date.** Use realistic durations from the buyer (e.g., "security review takes 3–4 weeks here"). Flag where the critical path is already late.
4. **Assign owners on both sides.** Each step: buyer owner, seller owner, due date, status. Steps without a buyer owner are a risk.
5. **Identify dependencies and risks.** E.g., "legal can't start until security approves", "procurement requires vendor registration 10 business days before PO". Add mitigations.
6. **Draft the share email.** Position it as "here's how I understood your process — what did I get wrong?" and invite edits. A plan the buyer edits is a plan the buyer owns.
7. **Set the review cadence.** Weekly 15-minute check-in or update in a shared doc; update CRM next steps and close date when the plan moves.

## Output format

```
# Mutual Action Plan: Example Co. + [Your company]
Goal: [buyer outcome] by [date] because [compelling event]
Decision makers: ... | Signer: ... | Approval steps: ...

| # | Step | Buyer owner | Our owner | Due | Depends on | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

Risks & mitigations
Open questions
Last updated: [date] — shared with [names]
```
Plus the cover email to the champion.

## Quality checks

- [ ] The target date is tied to a buyer reason, or marked as soft.
- [ ] Security, legal, procurement and signature steps are included with realistic durations.
- [ ] Every step has a buyer owner and date.
- [ ] Critical path and dependencies are visible.
- [ ] The buyer has been asked to correct the plan.
- [ ] CRM close date matches the plan.

## Limits

Do not invent buyer process steps, durations, approvers or dates — ask, and mark assumptions `[VERIFY]`. A mutual action plan is not a contract; avoid language implying commitment to purchase. Legal terms raised during the plan go to legal review.

skills.body:
# 공동 추진 계획 (Mutual Action Plan)

공동 추진 계획은 "이번 분기 안에 될 것 같습니다"를 고객이 동의한 날짜별 단계로 바꿉니다. 고객 측 날짜의 이유(시스템 오픈, 예산 집행 기한, 기존 계약 만료, 규제 시행일)에서 출발해 거꾸로 일정을 짜고, 한국 기업에서 지연이 자주 생기는 품의·결재, 정보보안 심의, 법무 검토, 협력사 등록, 발주 절차를 미리 드러냅니다.

## 사용 시점 / 사용하지 않는 경우

사용하는 경우:
- 고객이 과제 해결 필요성에 동의하고 솔루션을 검토하는 단계
- 예측(포캐스트)에 넣을 딜의 마감일 근거가 필요한 경우
- 딜이 계속 밀리고 단계·담당이 불분명한 경우

사용하지 않는 경우:
- 자격 검증이 아직 불분명 → 먼저 `sales-deal-qualification-meddicc-ko`
- 제안서 문서 → `sales-proposal-writer-ko`
- 내부 예측 보고 → `sales-forecast-commit-summary-ko`

## 먼저 확인할 사항

1. 고객의 목표 일자와 이유(오픈, 예산 소진 기한, 기존 계약 만료, 규제 시행) — 연말 예산 집행 마감이 흔한 이유입니다.
2. 의사결정 구조: 검토자, 결재권자, 금액별 전결 기준, 임원 회의·투자 심의 일정
3. 절차: 정보보안 검토, 법무 검토(어느 쪽 계약서), 협력사 등록, 품의·결재, 계약 날인(전자계약 여부), 발주, 일반적 소요 기간
4. 남은 검토 단계: 데모, 기술 검증, 레퍼런스 확인(방문·통화), 시범 적용
5. 당사 내부 절차: 영업관리 승인, 법무 검토 기간, 구축 착수 가능 일정
6. 단계를 맡을 고객 측 담당자

## 작성 절차

1. **고객 목표 명시**: 맨 위에 "왜 이 날짜인가"를 고객 표현으로. 명확한 이유가 없으면 그렇게 적고, 날짜는 유동적이며 예측에도 반영해야 함을 표시합니다.
2. **현재부터 성과 실현까지 모든 단계 나열**(계약 후 단계 포함 — 우리 계약이 아니라 고객 성공이 목표임을 보여 줍니다)
   - 검토: 기술 검증, 확대 데모, 레퍼런스 확인
   - 사업성: 투자 효과 검토, 예산 확인, 임원 미팅
   - 위험 검토: 보안 점검표, 개인정보 처리 위탁 계약, 법무 수정 의견
   - 구매·계약: 제안서·견적서, 협상, 품의·결재, 협력사 등록, 계약 날인, 발주
   - 착수: 킥오프, 설정, 교육, 오픈
3. **목표일에서 역산**: 고객이 알려 준 실제 소요 기간 사용("정보보안 심의는 3~4주 걸립니다"). 이미 늦은 핵심 경로를 표시합니다.
4. **양측 담당 지정**: 단계마다 고객 담당, 당사 담당, 기한, 상태. 고객 담당이 없는 단계는 위험입니다.
5. **선행 조건·위험**: 예) "보안 승인 후 법무 검토 시작", "협력사 등록 완료 후 발주 가능", "전결 금액 초과 시 임원 결재 추가". 대응 방안을 붙입니다.
6. **공유 메일 초안**: "이해한 귀사 절차를 정리했습니다. 틀린 부분을 고쳐 주시면 반영하겠습니다." 고객이 수정한 계획이 고객의 계획이 됩니다.
7. **점검 주기**: 주 1회 15분 점검 또는 공유 문서 업데이트, 계획이 바뀌면 CRM 다음 단계·예상 마감일도 수정

## 결과물 형식

```
# 공동 추진 계획: Example Co. × [당사]
목표: [날짜]까지 [고객 성과] — 이유: [목표 일자의 근거]
결재권자: ... | 계약 서명권자: ... | 결재 단계: ...

| 번호 | 단계 | 고객 담당 | 당사 담당 | 기한 | 선행 조건 | 상태 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

위험 및 대응
확인 필요 사항
최종 수정일: [날짜] — 공유 대상: [이름]
```
실무 담당자에게 보낼 공유 메일 포함

## 자체 점검

- [ ] 목표일이 고객 측 이유와 연결되었거나 유동적으로 표시되었는가
- [ ] 보안·법무·협력사 등록·품의·발주 단계가 현실적 기간으로 포함되었는가
- [ ] 모든 단계에 고객 담당과 기한이 있는가
- [ ] 핵심 경로와 선행 조건이 보이는가
- [ ] 고객에게 수정을 요청했는가
- [ ] CRM 예상 마감일이 계획과 일치하는가

## 한계

고객 절차·소요 기간·결재권자·날짜를 지어내지 않습니다. 물어보고, 가정은 `[확인 필요]`로 표시합니다. 공동 추진 계획은 계약이 아니므로 구매 확약처럼 읽히는 표현을 쓰지 않고, 과정에서 나온 계약 조건은 법무 검토로 넘깁니다.

# Mutual Action Plan

Mutual action plan "इस quarter में बंद हो जाएगी" को ग्राहक द्वारा स्वीकृत, तारीख़ वाले कदमों में बदलता है। यह ग्राहक के अपने कारण (go-live, budget ख़त्म होने की तारीख़, मौजूदा vendor का contract समाप्त, नियामक deadline) से शुरू होकर पीछे की ओर चलता है। भारत में सबसे ज़्यादा देरी vendor registration/vendor code, PO जारी होने, मालिक या purchase committee की मंज़ूरी और financial year-end (मार्च) के आसपास होती है — यह योजना इन्हें पहले से सामने लाती है।

## कब उपयोग करें / कब नहीं

उपयोग करें:
- ग्राहक समस्या को हल करने लायक मान चुका है और समाधान evaluate कर रहा है।
- Forecast में डील डालने के लिए close date का प्रमाण चाहिए।
- डील खिसक रही है और कदम या owners अस्पष्ट हैं।

उपयोग न करें:
- Qualification अभी साफ़ नहीं → पहले `sales-deal-qualification-meddicc-hi`
- Proposal दस्तावेज़ → `sales-proposal-writer-hi`
- आंतरिक forecast सार → `sales-forecast-commit-summary-hi`

## पहले क्या पूछें

1. ग्राहक का compelling event और लक्ष्य तारीख़, और यह क्यों अहम है।
2. निर्णय प्रक्रिया: कौन evaluate करता है, कौन sign करता है, approval सीमा, board/committee बैठक की तारीख़ें।
3. काग़ज़ी प्रक्रिया: IT/security review, legal review (किसका contract), vendor registration (PAN, GSTIN, बैंक विवरण, MSME प्रमाणपत्र), PO प्रक्रिया, सामान्य अवधि।
4. बाक़ी evaluation: demo, technical validation, reference कॉल/site visit, pilot।
5. हमारी आंतरिक प्रक्रिया: deal desk approval, legal turnaround, implementation क्षमता।
6. ग्राहक की ओर से कदमों के owners।

## चरण

1. **ग्राहक के लक्ष्य से शुरू करें**: सबसे ऊपर "यह तारीख़ क्यों" उनके शब्दों में। Compelling event न हो तो साफ़ लिखें — तारीख़ें soft हैं और forecast में यही दिखना चाहिए।
2. **अभी से value तक सभी कदम** (signature के बाद के कदम भी, ताकि योजना ग्राहक की सफलता पर हो):
   - Evaluation: technical validation, बड़ी टीम को demo, references।
   - Business: business case समीक्षा, budget पुष्टि, मालिक/sponsor मीटिंग।
   - Risk: security questionnaire, NDA, डेटा प्रोसेसिंग शर्तें (DPDP), legal redlines।
   - Commercial: proposal, negotiation, अंतिम approval, vendor code, PO, contract signature।
   - Launch: kickoff, configuration, training, go-live।
3. **लक्ष्य तारीख़ से पीछे**: ग्राहक की बताई वास्तविक अवधि ("हमारे यहाँ vendor registration में 2 हफ़्ते लगते हैं")। त्योहार/छुट्टियाँ और FY-end का ध्यान रखें। जो critical path पहले से देर में है उसे चिह्नित करें।
4. **दोनों पक्षों के owners**: हर कदम — ग्राहक owner, हमारा owner, तारीख़, स्थिति। बिना ग्राहक owner वाला कदम जोखिम है।
5. **Dependencies और जोखिम**: जैसे "IT approval के बाद ही legal शुरू", "vendor code के बिना PO नहीं"; हर जोखिम के साथ समाधान।
6. **साझा करने का ईमेल**: "मैंने आपकी प्रक्रिया ऐसे समझी है — कृपया जो ग़लत हो सुधार दें।" ग्राहक द्वारा सुधारी गई योजना ग्राहक की अपनी बन जाती है। सहमति हो तो WhatsApp पर भी छोटा reminder।
7. **समीक्षा ताल**: साप्ताहिक 15 मिनट या साझा दस्तावेज़; योजना बदले तो CRM में next step और close date अपडेट।

## आउटपुट फ़ॉर्मेट

```
# Mutual Action Plan: Example Co. + [हमारी कंपनी]
लक्ष्य: [तारीख़] तक [ग्राहक परिणाम], क्योंकि [compelling event]
निर्णयकर्ता: ... | Signatory: ... | Approval चरण: ...

| # | कदम | ग्राहक owner | हमारा owner | तारीख़ | निर्भरता | स्थिति |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

जोखिम और समाधान
खुले सवाल
अंतिम अपडेट: [तारीख़] — साझा: [नाम]
```
साथ में champion के लिए cover ईमेल।

## गुणवत्ता जाँच

- [ ] लक्ष्य तारीख़ ग्राहक के कारण से जुड़ी है, या soft चिह्नित
- [ ] Security, legal, vendor registration, PO और signature वास्तविक अवधि के साथ शामिल
- [ ] हर कदम का ग्राहक owner और तारीख़
- [ ] Critical path और dependencies दिखती हैं
- [ ] ग्राहक से योजना सुधारने को कहा गया
- [ ] CRM close date योजना से मेल खाती है

## सीमाएँ

ग्राहक के प्रक्रिया कदम, अवधि, approvers या तारीख़ें न गढ़ें — पूछें और मान्यताएँ `[जाँचें]` से चिह्नित करें। MAP अनुबंध नहीं है; ख़रीद की प्रतिबद्धता जैसी भाषा न लिखें। बीच में उठी अनुबंध शर्तें legal समीक्षा को भेजें।

skills.body:
# Sales Proposal Writer

A proposal should read as the buyer's own plan for solving their problem, with your offer as the obvious vehicle. This skill turns discovery notes and an approved quote into a concise proposal the champion can circulate to the economic buyer, procurement and legal.

## When to use / when not to use

Use when:
- Discovery is done and the buyer asked for a proposal or quote.
- Converting notes, a call summary or a MEDDICC record into a written offer.
- Renewal or expansion proposals for existing customers.

Do not use when:
- A paid pilot or proof of concept is the ask → `founder-pilot-proposal` (pilot scoping) or adapt with care.
- The buyer issued an RFP/RFI with a required format → `sales-rfp-response`.
- You need slides → `sales-deck-storyline`; quantified value case → `sales-business-case-roi`.
- You need a joint close plan → `sales-mutual-action-plan`.

## What to ask for first

1. Buyer details: company, contacts and roles, who will read it (champion, economic buyer, procurement).
2. Discovery facts: problems, impact (with the buyer's numbers), goals, required capabilities, timeline, decision criteria and process.
3. Scope: products/tiers, quantities, services, implementation approach, what is out of scope.
4. Approved quote: prices, discounts, term, billing frequency, payment terms, quote expiry — from CPQ/deal desk, not estimated.
5. Legal framework: your standard MSA/order form, or the customer's paper; any redlines already in play.
6. Proof: approved references, case studies, security documentation available.
7. Format preference: PDF document, slide-style, or the buyer's template.

## Steps

1. **Write the executive summary last but place it first.** 150–250 words: the buyer's situation, goals, recommended solution, expected outcomes (as the buyer defined them), investment summary, and the decision requested with a date.
2. **Current situation and objectives.** Restate the buyer's problems and goals in their words; include their numbers with source ("per your team, month-end close takes 9 days").
3. **Proposed solution.** Map each requirement to a capability: Requirement | How we address it | Status (available now / configuration / roadmap — roadmap only if product-approved and clearly labeled).
4. **Scope and deliverables.** In scope, out of scope, customer responsibilities, assumptions.
5. **Implementation plan.** Phases, milestones, durations, owners on both sides, go-live criteria.
6. **Success measures.** 3–5 measurable outcomes agreed with the buyer, with baseline and how they'll be tracked. For quantified value, link to `sales-business-case-roi`.
7. **Investment.** Reproduce the approved quote exactly: line items, quantity, unit price, discount, term, total, billing and payment terms, taxes (state "plus applicable taxes" if your policy), quote validity date. Never compute new discounts.
8. **Why us.** 3 differentiators relevant to their criteria, each backed by an approved proof point. No disparagement of competitors.
9. **Terms and next steps.** Reference the governing agreement; list documents to sign; path to signature (legal review, security review, PO). Hand off to `sales-mutual-action-plan` for dates.
10. **Tighten.** Remove generic boilerplate, replace "we" sentences with "you" outcomes, keep body to 5–10 pages.

## Output format

```
# Proposal: [Solution] for Example Co.
Prepared for: [Name, Title] | Prepared by: [Name] | Date | Valid until: [date from quote]
1. Executive summary
2. Your situation and objectives
3. Proposed solution (requirements map table)
4. Scope, deliverables, assumptions
5. Implementation plan (timeline table)
6. Success measures
7. Investment (approved quote table)
8. Why [Your company]
9. Terms and next steps
Appendix: references, security overview, product details
```

## Quality checks

- [ ] Executive summary stands alone and states the decision requested.
- [ ] Every problem and number traces to discovery notes.
- [ ] Every capability claim is documented; roadmap items labeled and approved.
- [ ] Pricing matches the approved quote line by line; validity date included.
- [ ] Out-of-scope and customer responsibilities are explicit.
- [ ] References and logos are approved for use.

## Limits

Never invent features, prices, discounts, customer names, ROI figures, SLAs or security certifications; mark gaps `[VERIFY]`. Contract terms, liability, SLAs and non-standard commitments require legal and deal-desk review before sending. A proposal is not a contract unless your legal team designs it as one.

```
Prepared for: [Name, Title] | Prepared by: [Name] | Date | Valid until: [date from quote]
1. Executive summary
2. Your situation and objectives
3. Proposed solution (requirements map table)
4. Scope, deliverables, assumptions
5. Implementation plan (timeline table)
6. Success measures
7. Investment (approved quote table)
8. Why [Your company]
9. Terms and next steps
Appendix: references, security overview, product details
```

## Quality checks

- [ ] Executive summary stands alone and states the decision requested.
- [ ] Every problem and number traces to discovery notes.
- [ ] Every capability claim is documented; roadmap items labeled and approved.
- [ ] Pricing matches the approved quote line by line; validity date included.
- [ ] Out-of-scope and customer responsibilities are explicit.
- [ ] References and logos are approved for use.

## Limits

Contract terms, liability, SLAs and non-standard commitments require legal and deal-desk review before sending. A proposal is not a contract unless your legal team designs it as one.

# 제안서 작성 (한국 B2B)

한국 B2B에서 제안서는 고객 실무자가 품의서에 첨부해 팀장·임원·구매·재무로 올리는 문서입니다. 따라서 "왜 이 과제가 필요한가, 왜 이 업체인가, 얼마이고 언제 끝나는가"에 결재 라인 누구나 답을 찾을 수 있어야 합니다. 이 스킬은 미팅 메모와 승인된 견적을 바탕으로 간결한 제안서와 견적서 초안을 만듭니다.

## 사용 시점 / 사용하지 않는 경우

사용하는 경우:
- 니즈 파악이 끝나고 고객이 제안서·견적서를 요청한 경우
- 미팅 메모·자격 검증(MEDDICC) 기록을 문서화된 제안으로 바꾸는 경우
- 기존 고객 갱신·확장 제안

사용하지 않는 경우:
- 유료 시범 사업(PoC)·파일럿 범위 설계 → `founder-pilot-proposal-ko`
- 고객이 정해진 양식의 RFP(제안요청서)를 보낸 경우·공공 입찰 → `sales-rfp-response-ko`
- 발표 자료 → `sales-deck-storyline-ko`, 투자 효과 산정 → `sales-business-case-roi-ko`
- 계약까지의 공동 일정 → `sales-mutual-action-plan-ko`

## 먼저 확인할 사항

1. 고객 정보: 회사명, 담당자·역할, 결재 라인(실무 → 팀장 → 임원·구매), 문서를 읽을 사람
2. 니즈 파악 내용: 과제, 영향(고객이 말한 수치), 목표, 필수 요구 사항, 일정, 선정 기준과 절차
3. 범위: 제품·등급, 수량, 서비스, 구축 방식, 범위 제외 사항
4. 승인된 견적: 단가, 할인, 계약 기간, 청구·지급 조건, 견적 유효기간 — 영업관리·견적 시스템 기준
5. 계약 형식: 당사 표준 계약서 또는 고객사 계약서, 협력사 등록·보안 서약 등 부속 서류
6. 근거 자료: 공개 승인된 레퍼런스(동종 업계 대기업 사례가 특히 중요), 보안 인증·자료
7. 형식: 문서형(PDF·한글·워드), 발표형, 고객사 지정 양식

## 작성 절차

1. **제안 요약(1쪽)**: 마지막에 쓰고 맨 앞에 둡니다. 고객 현황·목표, 제안 내용, 기대 효과(고객이 정의한 기준), 총 금액(부가세 별도), 요청 사항과 일정. 품의서에 그대로 옮길 수 있게 씁니다.
2. **현황과 목표**: 고객 표현과 수치를 출처와 함께("귀사 설명에 따르면 월 마감에 9일 소요").
3. **제안 솔루션**: 요구 사항 대응표 — 요구 사항 | 대응 방안 | 상태(즉시 제공 / 설정 / 개발 예정 — 개발 예정은 제품팀 승인 시에만, 명확히 표시).
4. **범위와 산출물**: 포함·제외 범위, 고객사 역할, 전제 조건
5. **추진 일정**: 단계, 주요 일정, 기간, 양측 담당, 검수(완료) 기준
6. **기대 성과**: 측정 가능한 3~5개 지표, 기준값, 측정 방법. 수치화는 `sales-business-case-roi-ko`와 연계합니다.
7. **견적**: 승인 견적을 그대로 옮깁니다. 품목 | 규격 | 수량 | 단가 | 금액 | 비고, 소계, "부가가치세 별도" 명시(또는 VAT 10% 포함 합계 병기 — 사내 기준 확인), 계약 기간, 지급 조건, 견적 유효기간, 공급자 정보(상호, 사업자등록번호 `[확인 필요]`, 대표자, 주소, 담당자). 새로운 할인은 계산하지 않습니다.
8. **수행 역량**: 고객 선정 기준과 연결된 차별점 3가지와 승인된 근거(레퍼런스, 인증). 경쟁사 비방 금지.
9. **계약 조건과 다음 단계**: 적용 계약서, 필요 서류(협력사 등록, 사업자등록증 사본, 통장 사본, 보안 서약서 등), 품의·계약·발주 일정 → `sales-mutual-action-plan-ko`
10. **다듬기**: 회사 소개는 부록으로, 본문 5~10쪽, "당사는"보다 "귀사는 ~할 수 있습니다" 중심으로.

## 결과물 형식

```
[표지] [솔루션명] 도입 제안서 — 제출처: Example Co. / 제출일 / 유효기간
1. 제안 요약
2. 현황 및 추진 목표
3. 제안 내용(요구 사항 대응표)
4. 범위·산출물·전제 조건
5. 추진 일정
6. 기대 성과
7. 견적(부가세 별도)
8. 수행 역량 및 레퍼런스
9. 계약 조건 및 향후 일정
[부록] 회사 소개, 보안 개요, 제품 상세
```

## 자체 점검

- [ ] 제안 요약만 읽어도 품의 판단이 가능한가
- [ ] 모든 과제·수치가 미팅 기록에 근거하는가
- [ ] 기능 주장이 문서화되어 있고 개발 예정 항목은 승인·표시되었는가
- [ ] 견적이 승인안과 항목별로 일치하고 부가세·유효기간이 표기되었는가
- [ ] 범위 제외 사항과 고객 역할이 명확한가
- [ ] 레퍼런스·로고 사용 승인을 받았는가

## 한계

기능·가격·할인·고객사명·투자 효과·SLA·보안 인증을 지어내지 않고 빈 부분은 `[확인 필요]`로 표시합니다. 계약 조건, 손해배상·책임 제한, SLA, 비표준 약속은 발송 전 법무·영업관리 검토가 필요합니다.

# Sales Proposal लेखन (भारत)

Proposal ग्राहक को अपनी समस्या हल करने की योजना जैसा लगना चाहिए, जिसमें आपका offer स्वाभाविक साधन हो। भारत में proposal के बाद आमतौर पर procurement तुलनात्मक quotations माँगता है, कीमत पर मोलभाव होता है, और अंत में PO जारी होता है — इसलिए commercial हिस्सा (GST, payment terms, validity) साफ़ और सटीक होना ज़रूरी है।

## कब उपयोग करें / कब नहीं

उपयोग करें:
- Discovery पूरी है और ग्राहक ने proposal या quotation माँगा है।
- नोट्स या MEDDICC रिकॉर्ड को लिखित offer में बदलना।
- मौजूदा ग्राहक के renewal/expansion proposal।

उपयोग न करें:
- Paid pilot/POC का scope → `founder-pilot-proposal-hi`
- ग्राहक का RFP/टेंडर या GeM bid → `sales-rfp-response-hi`
- स्लाइड्स → `sales-deck-storyline-hi`; ROI गणना → `sales-business-case-roi-hi`
- Closing की संयुक्त योजना → `sales-mutual-action-plan-hi`

## पहले क्या पूछें

1. ग्राहक: कंपनी, संपर्क और भूमिकाएँ, कौन पढ़ेगा (champion, मालिक/MD, procurement, finance)।
2. Discovery तथ्य: समस्याएँ, प्रभाव (ग्राहक के आँकड़े), लक्ष्य, ज़रूरी क्षमताएँ, समय-सीमा, निर्णय मानदंड।
3. Scope: products/plans, मात्रा, services, implementation, क्या scope से बाहर है।
4. स्वीकृत quote: कीमतें, discount, अवधि, billing, payment terms (advance/milestone/credit days), validity — deal desk से, अनुमान नहीं।
5. Tax विवरण: आपका GSTIN, SAC/HSN कोड, लागू GST दर `[जाँचें]`, place of supply (IGST बनाम CGST+SGST), ग्राहक का GSTIN।
6. अनुबंध: आपका standard agreement या ग्राहक का; vendor registration दस्तावेज़ (PAN, GST certificate, MSME/Udyam प्रमाणपत्र यदि लागू, cancelled cheque)।
7. स्वीकृत references, case studies, security दस्तावेज़; फ़ॉर्मेट प्राथमिकता।

## चरण

1. **Executive summary** (अंत में लिखें, शुरू में रखें, 150–250 शब्द): स्थिति, लक्ष्य, सुझाया समाधान, अपेक्षित परिणाम (ग्राहक की परिभाषा में), कुल निवेश (GST अलग), माँगा गया निर्णय और तारीख़।
2. **मौजूदा स्थिति और लक्ष्य**: ग्राहक के शब्द और आँकड़े स्रोत के साथ।
3. **समाधान**: requirement map — आवश्यकता | हम कैसे पूरा करते हैं | स्थिति (अभी उपलब्ध / configuration / roadmap — roadmap केवल product की मंज़ूरी से, स्पष्ट लेबल के साथ)।
4. **Scope और deliverables**: in-scope, out-of-scope, ग्राहक की ज़िम्मेदारियाँ, मान्यताएँ।
5. **Implementation योजना**: चरण, milestones, अवधि, दोनों पक्षों के owners, go-live/acceptance मानदंड।
6. **Success measures**: 3–5 मापने योग्य परिणाम, baseline और tracking तरीका; विस्तृत गणना `sales-business-case-roi-hi` से।
7. **Commercials (quotation)**: स्वीकृत quote बिल्कुल वैसा — विवरण | SAC/HSN | मात्रा | दर | राशि; उप-योग; GST (दर `[जाँचें]`) अलग पंक्ति में; कुल; payment terms; validity; billing entity और GSTIN। नोट: ग्राहक लागू TDS (जैसे धारा 194J/194C `[जाँचें]`) काट सकता है — यह ग्राहक की ज़िम्मेदारी है, कीमत में बदलाव नहीं। नया discount स्वयं न गिनें।
8. **मोलभाव की तैयारी (आंतरिक, ग्राहक को नहीं)**: स्वीकृत "give-get" विकल्प — multi-year, advance payment, बड़ा scope — और walk-away बिंदु deal desk से।
9. **हम क्यों**: ग्राहक के मानदंडों से जुड़े 3 अंतर, स्वीकृत प्रमाण सहित; प्रतिस्पर्धी की बुराई नहीं।
10. **शर्तें और अगले कदम**: लागू अनुबंध, vendor registration, legal/IT review, PO जारी होना → `sales-mutual-action-plan-hi`।

## आउटपुट फ़ॉर्मेट

```
# प्रस्ताव: Example Co. के लिए [समाधान]
तैयार किया: [नाम] | तारीख़ | मान्य: [quote से तारीख़]
1. Executive summary
2. आपकी स्थिति और लक्ष्य
3. प्रस्तावित समाधान (requirement map)
4. Scope, deliverables, मान्यताएँ
5. Implementation timeline
6. Success measures
7. Commercials (GST अलग, payment terms, validity)
8. हम क्यों
9. शर्तें और अगले कदम
परिशिष्ट: references, security सार, vendor दस्तावेज़ सूची
आंतरिक नोट: स्वीकृत give-get विकल्प (भेजा नहीं जाएगा)
```

## गुणवत्ता जाँच

- [ ] Executive summary अकेले पढ़ने योग्य और निर्णय माँगता है
- [ ] हर समस्या और आँकड़ा discovery नोट्स से
- [ ] हर क्षमता दस्तावेज़ित; roadmap लेबल और स्वीकृत
- [ ] कीमत स्वीकृत quote से मेल खाती है; GST, SAC, validity स्पष्ट
- [ ] Out-of-scope और ग्राहक ज़िम्मेदारियाँ स्पष्ट
- [ ] References/logos उपयोग के लिए स्वीकृत

## सीमाएँ

फ़ीचर, कीमतें, discount, ग्राहक नाम, ROI, SLA या security प्रमाणन न गढ़ें; कमियाँ `[जाँचें]` से चिह्नित करें। GST दर, SAC और TDS प्रावधान अपने CA/finance से पुष्टि करें। अनुबंध शर्तें, liability, SLA और ग़ैर-मानक वादे भेजने से पहले legal व deal desk की समीक्षा ज़रूरी है।

skills.body:
# RFP / RFI Response

RFPs reward precision and compliance more than prose. This skill decides whether to bid, breaks the document into every requirement, drafts answers only from approved sources, and organizes the team to submit on time in the buyer's required format.

## When to use / when not to use

Use when:
- A formal RFP, RFI, RFQ or tender arrives from a commercial or public-sector buyer.
- You need a bid/no-bid recommendation.
- You need a requirements compliance matrix and first-draft answers.

Do not use when:
- The buyer asked for a free-form proposal → `sales-proposal-writer`.
- Only a security questionnaire was sent → `sales-security-questionnaire-draft`.
- Single product questions by email → `sales-product-question-answer`.

## What to ask for first

1. The full RFP package: instructions, requirements, evaluation criteria and weights, pricing template, contract terms, Q&A deadline, submission deadline and method.
2. Relationship context: did you shape the requirements? Do you know the evaluators? Incumbent?
3. Approved content sources: previous RFP answers library, product documentation, security package (e.g., SOC 2 report, policies), legal-approved standard answers.
4. Team: who owns pricing, legal, security, technical answers, final review and submission.
5. Approved pricing and any deal-desk guidance.
6. For US public sector: registration requirements (e.g., SAM.gov for federal), small-business set-asides, required certifications `[VERIFY]`.

## Steps

1. **Bid/no-bid (score 1–5 each).** Fit with requirements, relationship/influence, competitive position, ability to meet mandatory items, deal size vs effort, timing. Recommend no-bid if mandatory requirements can't be met truthfully or you had no prior contact and the RFP looks written for a competitor. Document the rationale.
2. **Shred the RFP.** Extract every "shall/must/should" into a compliance matrix: ID | Section | Requirement | Mandatory? | Response (Comply / Partial / Roadmap / No) | Owner | Source | Status.
3. **Clarifying questions.** Draft questions for the Q&A window on ambiguities; never assume.
4. **Win themes (2–3).** Tie to the evaluation criteria and the buyer's stated goals; weave each into executive summary and relevant answers.
5. **Draft answers.**
   - Answer the question asked first ("Yes. [Product] supports SSO via SAML 2.0."), then how, then proof.
   - Pull from approved content; cite the source in an internal column. If no source exists, mark `[SME INPUT NEEDED]`.
   - Partial or roadmap answers must be honest; roadmap only with product approval and a forward-looking caveat.
   - Follow word/character limits and the required numbering.
6. **Pricing.** Fill the buyer's template from the approved quote; note assumptions and exclusions; taxes as policy dictates.
7. **Legal and exceptions.** List exceptions to the buyer's terms for legal review; never accept unlimited liability or other terms silently.
8. **Executive summary.** One page: understanding of their goals, approach, win themes, why you.
9. **Review schedule.** Work back from deadline: drafts (D-7), SME review (D-5), pricing/legal sign-off (D-3), final compliance check (D-2), submit (D-1 — never on the last hour).

## Output format

1. Bid/no-bid scorecard and recommendation.
2. Compliance matrix (table above).
3. Clarifying questions list.
4. Win themes.
5. Draft answers by section, with internal source column and flags.
6. Pricing section draft and assumptions.
7. Legal exceptions list.
8. Timeline with owners.

## Quality checks

- [ ] Every requirement in the RFP appears in the matrix.
- [ ] Every "Comply" answer is backed by a documented source.
- [ ] Mandatory requirements are met or the bid is flagged no-bid.
- [ ] Format, numbering, page and word limits match instructions.
- [ ] Pricing matches approved quote; exceptions reviewed by legal.
- [ ] Submission method and deadline (with time zone) confirmed.

## Limits

Never invent capabilities, certifications, customer references, prices or compliance status — false RFP statements can create contractual and legal liability. Mark unknowns `[VERIFY]` or `[SME INPUT NEEDED]`. Contract terms and exceptions require legal review; public-sector bids may carry specific certification and disclosure obligations.

4. Team: who owns pricing, legal, security, technical answers, final review and submission.
5. Approved pricing and any deal-desk guidance.
6. For US public sector: registration requirements (e.g., SAM.gov for federal), small-business set-asides, required certifications `[VERIFY]`.

## Steps

1. **Bid/no-bid (score 1–5 each).** Fit with requirements, relationship/influence, competitive position, ability to meet mandatory items, deal size vs effort, timing. Recommend no-bid if mandatory requirements can't be met truthfully or you had no prior contact and the RFP looks written for a competitor. Document the rationale.
2. **Shred the RFP.** Extract every "shall/must/should" into a compliance matrix: ID | Section | Requirement | Mandatory? | Response (Comply / Partial / Roadmap / No) | Owner | Source | Status.
3. **Clarifying questions.** Draft questions for the Q&A window on ambiguities; never assume.
4. **Win themes (2–3).** Tie to the evaluation criteria and the buyer's stated goals; weave each into executive summary and relevant answers.
5. **Draft answers.**
   - Answer the question asked first ("Yes. [Product] supports SSO via SAML 2.0."), then how, then proof.
   - Pull from approved content; cite the source in an internal column. If no source exists, mark `[SME INPUT NEEDED]`.
   - Partial or roadmap answers must be honest; roadmap only with product approval and a forward-looking caveat.
   - Follow word/character limits and the required numbering.
6. **Pricing.** Fill the buyer's template from the approved quote; note assumptions and exclusions; taxes as policy dictates.
7. **Legal and exceptions.** List exceptions to the buyer's terms for legal review; never accept unlimited liability or other terms silently.
8. **Executive summary.** One page: understanding of their goals, approach, win themes, why you.
9. **Review schedule.** Work back from deadline: drafts (D-7), SME review (D-5), pricing/legal sign-off (D-3), final compliance check (D-2), submit (D-1 — never on the last hour).

## Output format

1. Bid/no-bid scorecard and recommendation.
2. Compliance matrix (table above).
3. Clarifying questions list.
4. Win themes.
5. Draft answers by section, with internal source column and flags.
6. Pricing section draft and assumptions.
7. Legal exceptions list.
8. Timeline with owners.

## Quality checks

- [ ] Every requirement in the RFP appears in the matrix.
- [ ] Every "Comply" answer is backed by a documented source.
- [ ] Mandatory requirements are met or the bid is flagged no-bid.
- [ ] Format, numbering, page and word limits match instructions.
- [ ] Pricing matches approved quote; exceptions reviewed by legal.
- [ ] Submission method and deadline (with time zone) confirmed.

## Limits

Never invent capabilities, certifications, customer references, prices or compliance status — false RFP statements can create contractual and legal liability. Mark unknowns `[VERIFY]` or `[SME INPUT NEEDED]`. Contract terms and exceptions require legal review; public-sector bids may carry specific certification and disclosure obligations.

skills.body:
# 제안요청서(RFP) 대응

RFP 평가는 문장력보다 정확성과 요구 사항 충족 여부로 결정됩니다. 이 스킬은 참여 여부를 판단하고, 제안요청서의 모든 요구 사항을 분해하며, 승인된 자료로만 답변을 작성하고, 지정 양식으로 기한 내 제출하도록 팀 일정을 짭니다. 대기업 구매 입찰과 공공 입찰(나라장터) 모두에 적용합니다.

## 사용 시점 / 사용하지 않는 경우

사용하는 경우:
- 기업 또는 공공기관의 RFP, RFI, 견적 요청, 입찰 공고를 받은 경우
- 입찰 참여 여부 판단이 필요한 경우
- 요구 사항 대응표와 1차 답변이 필요한 경우

사용하지 않는 경우:
- 자유 형식 제안서 요청 → `sales-proposal-writer-ko`
- 보안 점검표만 받은 경우 → `sales-security-questionnaire-draft-ko`
- 메일로 온 개별 제품 문의 → `sales-product-question-answer-ko`

## 먼저 확인할 사항

1. 제안요청서 전체: 제출 안내, 요구 사항, 평가 기준·배점(기술·가격 비율), 가격 양식, 계약 조건, 질의 마감, 제출 마감·방식
2. 관계 상황: 사전 영업으로 요구 사항 형성에 참여했는지, 기존 공급사가 있는지
3. 승인 자료: 기존 제안서 답변 모음, 제품 문서, 보안 자료(인증서, 정책), 법무 승인 표준 답변
4. 담당: 가격, 법무, 보안, 기술 답변, 최종 검토, 제출
5. 승인된 가격과 영업관리 지침
6. 공공 입찰인 경우: 나라장터 입찰 참가 자격 등록, 업종·직접생산 확인 등 자격 요건, 제안서 평가 방식(협상에 의한 계약 등), 보증서·서약서 등 필요 서류 `[확인 필요]`
7. 대기업 입찰인 경우: 협력사 등록 상태, 구매 포털 제출 방식, 보안 서약서·비밀유지 서류

## 작성 절차

1. **참여 여부 판단(항목별 1~5점)**: 요구 사항 적합도, 관계·사전 영향력, 경쟁 우위, 필수 요건 충족 가능성, 규모 대비 투입, 일정. 필수 요건을 사실대로 충족할 수 없거나 특정 업체 맞춤형으로 보이면 불참을 권고하고 근거를 남깁니다.
2. **요구 사항 분해**: "~하여야 한다", "~할 것" 등 모든 요구를 대응표로. 번호 | 항목 | 요구 사항 | 필수 여부 | 대응(충족/부분/개발 예정/미충족) | 담당 | 근거 자료 | 상태
3. **질의서 작성**: 모호한 부분은 질의 기간 안에 공식 질의합니다. 추측하지 않습니다.
4. **차별화 메시지 2~3개**: 평가 기준과 고객 목표에 연결해 요약과 해당 답변에 반영
5. **답변 작성**
   - 결론 먼저("지원합니다. [제품]은 SAML 2.0 기반 SSO를 제공합니다."), 다음 방법, 다음 근거
   - 승인 자료만 사용하고 내부용 출처 열에 기록. 근거가 없으면 `[담당 부서 확인 필요]`
   - 부분 충족·개발 예정은 정직하게 표시(개발 예정은 제품팀 승인 필요)
   - 지정 목차·번호·분량을 지킵니다.
6. **가격 제안**: 지정 양식에 승인 견적을 입력, 부가세 포함·별도 기준은 공고문 지시를 따르고, 전제·제외 사항 명시
7. **계약 조건 검토**: 이견이 있는 조항(손해배상, 지체상금, 지식재산권, 하자보수 등)을 법무 검토 목록으로 정리. 조용히 수용하지 않습니다.
8. **제안 요약**: 1쪽 — 고객 목표 이해, 수행 방안, 차별화 메시지, 수행 역량
9. **검토 일정(역산)**: 초안 D-7, 담당 부서 검토 D-5, 가격·법무 승인 D-3, 최종 요건 점검 D-2, 제출 D-1(전자 제출 시스템 오류에 대비해 마감 직전 제출 금지)

## 결과물 형식

1. 참여 여부 평가표와 권고
2. 요구 사항 대응표
3. 질의서 목록
4. 차별화 메시지
5. 항목별 답변 초안(내부 출처 열, 확인 표시 포함)
6. 가격 제안 초안과 전제
7. 계약 조건 이견 목록
8. 담당자별 일정표

## 자체 점검

- [ ] 제안요청서의 모든 요구 사항이 대응표에 있는가
- [ ] "충족" 답변마다 문서화된 근거가 있는가
- [ ] 필수 요건을 충족하거나 불참으로 표시했는가
- [ ] 목차·번호·분량·제출 서류가 지시와 일치하는가
- [ ] 가격이 승인 견적과 일치하고 이견 조항을 법무가 검토했는가
- [ ] 제출 방식과 마감 일시를 확인했는가

## 한계

기능·인증·레퍼런스·가격·충족 여부를 지어내지 않습니다. 허위 기재는 계약상 책임, 공공 입찰에서는 부정당업자 제재 등 불이익으로 이어질 수 있습니다. 모르는 내용은 `[확인 필요]`로 표시하고, 계약 조건·공공 입찰 자격은 법무와 최신 공고문으로 확인합니다.

skills.body:
# RFP / टेंडर का जवाब

RFP और टेंडर में सुंदर भाषा से ज़्यादा सटीकता और compliance मायने रखती है। यह स्किल तय करती है कि bid करें या नहीं, दस्तावेज़ की हर requirement अलग करती है, केवल स्वीकृत स्रोतों से जवाब लिखती है, और टीम को समय पर, माँगे गए फ़ॉर्मेट में जमा करने के लिए व्यवस्थित करती है। यह निजी कंपनियों के RFP और सरकारी ख़रीद (GeM, CPPP/e-procurement टेंडर) दोनों पर लागू है।

## कब उपयोग करें / कब नहीं

उपयोग करें:
- औपचारिक RFP, RFI, RFQ, टेंडर या GeM bid आया है।
- Bid/no-bid सिफ़ारिश चाहिए।
- Compliance matrix और पहले ड्राफ़्ट जवाब चाहिए।

उपयोग न करें:
- ग्राहक ने मुक्त-फ़ॉर्मेट proposal माँगा → `sales-proposal-writer-hi`
- केवल security questionnaire → `sales-security-questionnaire-draft-hi`
- ईमेल पर एक-दो product सवाल → `sales-product-question-answer-hi`

## पहले क्या पूछें

1. पूरा दस्तावेज़: निर्देश, requirements, मूल्यांकन मानदंड (technical बनाम commercial, L1 या QCBS), price bid फ़ॉर्मेट, अनुबंध शर्तें, pre-bid query deadline, जमा करने की तारीख़ और तरीका।
2. संबंध संदर्भ: क्या requirements बनाने में आपकी भूमिका थी? Incumbent कौन है?
3. स्वीकृत सामग्री: पुराने RFP जवाब, product दस्तावेज़, security पैकेज, legal-स्वीकृत मानक जवाब।
4. टीम: pricing, legal, security, technical जवाब, अंतिम समीक्षा और upload के owners।
5. स्वीकृत pricing और deal desk निर्देश।
6. सरकारी ख़रीद हो तो: GeM पर seller registration और catalogue, पात्रता (turnover, अनुभव, OEM authorisation), EMD/bid security, MSE/स्टार्टअप छूट, Make in India local content शर्तें, आवश्यक घोषणाएँ और DSC `[जाँचें]`।

## चरण

1. **Bid/no-bid (हर मानदंड 1–5)**: requirement फ़िट, संबंध/प्रभाव, प्रतिस्पर्धी स्थिति, अनिवार्य शर्तें सच में पूरी हो सकती हैं या नहीं, मूल्य बनाम प्रयास, समय। L1 (सबसे कम कीमत) वाले टेंडर में margin जोखिम आँकें। अनिवार्य पात्रता पूरी न हो या दस्तावेज़ किसी प्रतिस्पर्धी के लिए लिखा लगे तो no-bid, कारण सहित।
2. **Requirements अलग करें**: हर "shall/must" को matrix में — ID | खंड | Requirement | अनिवार्य? | जवाब (Comply / Partial / Roadmap / No) | Owner | स्रोत | स्थिति।
3. **Pre-bid queries**: अस्पष्ट बिंदुओं पर औपचारिक सवाल समय-सीमा में; अनुमान नहीं।
4. **Win themes (2–3)**: मूल्यांकन मानदंड और ग्राहक के लक्ष्यों से जोड़ें।
5. **जवाब ड्राफ़्ट**:
   - पहले सीधा उत्तर ("हाँ। [Product] SAML 2.0 से SSO सपोर्ट करता है।"), फिर कैसे, फिर प्रमाण।
   - केवल स्वीकृत सामग्री; आंतरिक कॉलम में स्रोत। स्रोत न हो तो `[SME इनपुट चाहिए]`।
   - Partial/roadmap ईमानदारी से; roadmap केवल product की मंज़ूरी के साथ।
   - शब्द सीमा, क्रमांकन और फ़ॉर्मेट का पालन।
6. **Price bid**: ग्राहक के फ़ॉर्मेट में स्वीकृत quote; GST अलग या शामिल — दस्तावेज़ के निर्देश अनुसार, SAC/HSN सहित; मान्यताएँ और exclusions।
7. **अनुबंध शर्तें**: liability, penalty/LD, payment milestones, performance bank guarantee जैसी शर्तों पर आपत्तियाँ legal समीक्षा के लिए सूचीबद्ध करें; चुपचाप स्वीकार न करें।
8. **Executive summary**: एक पेज — लक्ष्यों की समझ, दृष्टिकोण, win themes, हम क्यों।
9. **Review schedule (पीछे से)**: ड्राफ़्ट D-7, SME review D-5, pricing/legal sign-off D-3, अंतिम compliance जाँच और दस्तावेज़ (PAN, GST, अनुभव प्रमाणपत्र) D-2, upload D-1 — पोर्टल धीमा हो सकता है, आख़िरी घंटे पर नहीं।

## आउटपुट फ़ॉर्मेट

1. Bid/no-bid scorecard और सिफ़ारिश
2. Compliance matrix
3. Pre-bid query सूची
4. Win themes
5. खंड-वार ड्राफ़्ट जवाब (आंतरिक स्रोत कॉलम और flags)
6. Price bid ड्राफ़्ट और मान्यताएँ
7. अनुबंध आपत्तियों की सूची
8. Owners के साथ timeline और दस्तावेज़ चेकलिस्ट

## गुणवत्ता जाँच

- [ ] दस्तावेज़ की हर requirement matrix में
- [ ] हर "Comply" के पीछे दस्तावेज़ित स्रोत
- [ ] अनिवार्य शर्तें पूरी या no-bid चिह्नित
- [ ] फ़ॉर्मेट, क्रमांकन, पेज/शब्द सीमा, आवश्यक दस्तावेज़ निर्देशों के अनुरूप
- [ ] Price bid स्वीकृत quote से मेल; आपत्तियाँ legal ने देखीं
- [ ] जमा करने का तरीका और deadline (समय सहित) पुष्टि

## सीमाएँ

क्षमताएँ, प्रमाणन, ग्राहक references, कीमतें या compliance स्थिति न गढ़ें — टेंडर में ग़लत घोषणा से अनुबंध दायित्व, EMD ज़ब्ती या blacklisting हो सकती है। अज्ञात बातें `[जाँचें]` से चिह्नित करें। अनुबंध शर्तें और सरकारी ख़रीद की पात्रता legal तथा नवीनतम टेंडर दस्तावेज़/GeM नियमों से पुष्टि करें।

skills.name: sales-competitor-comparison-reply
skills.description: Drafts a fair, verifiable reply when a buyer asks how you compare with a named competitor: clarifies what matters to them, compares on their decision criteria using approved battlecard content and publicly verifiable facts, admits where the competitor is strong, and suggests proof the buyer can check themselves (trial, reference, documentation). Use when a rep says 'they asked how we compare to Competitor X', 'X is cheaper, what do I say?', 'write a comparison table for the buyer', 'the customer is also evaluating X' or 'help me position against the incumbent'.
skills.body:
# Competitor Comparison Reply

Buyers ask for comparisons because they want to de-risk a choice, not because they want you to trash a rival. Credible replies compare on the buyer's criteria, use facts the buyer can verify, concede real competitor strengths, and steer toward proof. Exaggerated claims about competitors damage trust and can create legal risk.

## When to use / when not to use

Use when:
- A buyer asks directly how you compare with a named vendor or the incumbent.
- You need a written comparison or a talk track for a competitive deal.
- The buyer repeats a competitor's claim about you.

Do not use when:
- The objection is price alone → `sales-pricing-question-reply` and/or `sales-objection-handling`.
- It's a pure product question → `sales-product-question-answer`.
- You need a full RFP response → `sales-rfp-response`.

## What to ask for first

1. The buyer's exact question and what they've heard from the competitor.
2. The buyer's decision criteria and priorities (from discovery or MEDDICC record).
3. Approved competitive content: battlecard, win/loss notes, analyst content you're licensed to share — with dates.
4. Publicly verifiable competitor facts (their public docs, pricing pages, release notes) with URLs and access dates.
5. Your verified differentiators and proof (case studies, references in a similar situation).
6. Whether the competitor is the incumbent (switching cost and risk matter).

## Steps

1. **Clarify before comparing.** Ask what matters most to them and where the competitor impressed them. Comparisons on the buyer's criteria beat generic feature grids.
2. **Choose 3–5 criteria** from the buyer's list. For each, write what you offer (documented), what the competitor offers (publicly verifiable only, with source) or "not able to verify", and why it matters for this buyer.
3. **Concede honestly.** Name at least one area where the competitor is a reasonable choice ("If your priority is X, they're strong there"). This raises credibility for the rest.
4. **Reframe to outcomes.** Connect your differentiators to the buyer's stated goals and risks, not features in isolation.
5. **Offer verifiable proof.** Trial on their use case, reference customer who evaluated both, documentation links. Invite the buyer to ask the competitor specific questions ("Ask how they handle [scenario]") — fair "landmine" questions only, based on real, documented differences.
6. **Handle competitor claims about you.** Correct factual errors calmly with sources; don't speculate about motives.
7. **Keep it short in writing.** Email ≤200 words plus an optional table; offer a call for nuance. Avoid putting unverifiable competitive claims in writing.
8. **Log intel.** Record what the buyer shared about the competitor in CRM (no confidential documents of the competitor).

## Output format

1. Clarifying questions for the buyer.
2. Comparison table (for internal use or, if all facts are verified, for the buyer):

| Buyer criterion | Us (source) | Competitor (public source / "not verified") | Why it matters to you |
|---|---|---|---|

3. Email reply draft.
